[Footnote: At the beginning of the Tafsir of Surah al-Baqarah, on its virtues.]

Imam Ahmad also said: Yazid narrated to us, Hammam ibn Yahya informed us, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever memorises ten verses from the beginning of Surah al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal."

Al-Hakim recorded it in his *Mustadrak* from Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Mu'ammal, Fudayl [Footnote: In MS "t": "al-Fadl"] ibn Muhammad al-Sha'rani narrated to us, Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, Abu Hashim narrated to us, from Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn Ubad, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Kahf on Friday, there will be shone for him of light what is between him and the two Fridays." **Tafsir (exegesis) of Surah al-Kahf**

It is Meccan.

**Mention of what has been reported about its virtue, the first and last ten verses, and that it is a protection from the Dajjal (the Antichrist):**

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, who said: I heard al-Bara' say: A man recited Surah al-Kahf while there was an animal in the house, and it began to shy away. He looked and saw something like a cloud or a shadow (*dabbah* or *sahabah*) that had covered him. He mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Recite, so-and-so, for it was tranquility (*sakinah*) that descended at the recitation of the Qur'an," or "descended for the Qur'an."

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in the two Sahihs (the two most authentic collections of hadith), from the hadith of Shu'bah, with this chain. [Footnote: Musnad (4/281), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3614), Sahih Muslim no. (795).] This man who was reciting it was Usayd ibn al-Hudayr, as mentioned earlier in the Tafsir of Surah al-Baqarah. [Footnote: At the beginning of the Tafsir of Surah al-Baqarah, on its virtues.]

Imam Ahmad also said: Yazid narrated to us, Hammam ibn Yahya informed us, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever memorises ten verses from the beginning of Surah al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal."

Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and al-Tirmidhi recorded it from the hadith of Qatadah with this chain. [Footnote: In MS "f": "al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i".] The wording of al-Tirmidhi is: "Whoever memorises the three verses from the beginning of al-Kahf." And he said: Hasan sahih (good and authentic). [Footnote: Musnad (5/196), Sahih Muslim no. (809), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4323), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (8025), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2886).]

Another route: Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah: I heard Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd narrating from Ma'dan, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever recites the last ten verses of Surah al-Kahf will be protected from the trial of the Dajjal."

Muslim also recorded it, and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Qatadah with this chain. [Footnote: Musnad (6/446), Sahih Muslim no. (809), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (10786).] In the wording of al-Nasa'i: "Whoever recites ten verses of al-Kahf," and he mentioned it.

Another hadith: al-Nasa'i recorded it in *al-Yawm wa al-Laylah* from Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la, from Khalid, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Thawban, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Whoever recites the last ten verses of Surah al-Kahf, it will be a protection for him from the Dajjal." [Footnote: Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (10784).]

It is possible that Salim heard it from Thawban and from Abu al-Darda'.

Imam Ahmad also said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Zabban ibn Fayid narrated to us [Footnote: In MS "t": "Ziyad ibn Waqid"; in MS "f": "Thawban ibn Fayid".], from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas al-Juhani, from his father, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Whoever recites the beginning and the end of Surah al-Kahf, it will be a light for him from his foot to his head, and whoever recites it entirely, it will be a light for him between the earth and the heaven." [Footnote: In MS "f": "the heaven and the earth".] Ahmad alone recorded it, and they did not record it. [Footnote: In MS "t": "does not record it".] [Footnote: Musnad (4/439).]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh [in his Tafsir] [Footnote: Addition from MS "f".] narrated with a chain of his own that is gharib (rare), from Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Kahf on Friday, a light will shine for him from beneath his foot up to the clouds of the sky, illuminating for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will be forgiven what is between the two Fridays." [Footnote: Al-Mundhiri mentioned it in al-Targhib (1/513) and said: "Ibn Mardawayh recorded it with a chain that has no harm in it."]

In its attribution to the Prophet (ﷺ) there is room for doubt, and at best it is mawquf (stopping at a Companion).

Similarly, Imam Sa'id ibn Mansur recorded in his Sunan, from Hushaym ibn Bashir [Footnote: In MS "t": "Bishr".], from Abu Hashim [Footnote: In MSS "t" and "a": "Hisham".], from Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn Abbad [Footnote: In MS "f": "Ubadah".], from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Whoever recites Surah al-Kahf on Friday, there will be shone for him of light what is between him and the Ancient House (the Ka'bah).

This is how it occurred as a mawquf report. Likewise al-Thawri recorded it from Abu Hashim [Footnote: In MS "t": "Hisham"], with the same chain, as a mawquf report, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. [Footnote: Abu Ubayd recorded it in *Fada'il al-Qur'an* (p. 131), saying: Hushaym narrated to us with it as mawquf, and the difference over Hushaym will come later. As for the narration of al-Thawri, al-Nasa'i recorded it in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (10790) through Abd al-Rahman from Sufyan al-Thawri with it as mawquf. The virtuous scholar Muhammad Tarhuni, in his book *Mawsu'at Fada'il al-Qur'an* (1/337), examined the reports both raised and stopped and did well and was beneficial, may Allah reward him, and then favoured that it is mawquf but has the ruling of marfu' (raised).]

Al-Hakim recorded it in his *Mustadrak* from Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Mu'ammal, Fudayl [Footnote: In MS "t": "al-Fadl"] ibn Muhammad al-Sha'rani narrated to us, Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, Abu Hashim narrated to us, from Abu Mijlaz, from Qays ibn Ubad, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Kahf on Friday, there will be shone for him of light what is between him and the two Fridays." Then he said: This is a hadith whose chain is sahih, though they did not record it.

Likewise al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi recorded it in his Sunan from al-Hakim. [Footnote: *al-Mustadrak* (2/368) and *al-Sunan al-Kubra* of al-Bayhaqi (3/249).] Then al-Bayhaqi said: Yahya ibn Kathir also narrated it from Shu'bah, from Abu Hashim with its chain, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Kahf as it was revealed, it will be a light for him on the Day of Resurrection." [Footnote: Al-Tabarani recorded it in *al-Mu'jam al-Awsat* no. (428), *Majma' al-Bahrayn*, and there was disagreement over it from Shu'bah: Ghundar narrated it from Shu'bah as mawquf.] [And Allah knows best.] [Footnote: Addition from MS "a".]

In *al-Mukhtarah* of al-Hafiz Diya' al-Maqdisi, from the hadith of Abd Allah ibn Mus'ab ibn Manzur ibn Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from Ali, raised to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah al-Kahf on Friday, he will be protected until eight days from every trial, and if the Dajjal emerges, he will be protected from him." [Footnote: *al-Mukhtarah* no. (430), where he said: "Abd Allah ibn Mus'ab is not mentioned by al-Bukhari, nor by Ibn Abi Hatim in their two books."]

**In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful**

[My Lord, grant me success] [Footnote: Addition from MS "t".]

It has already been mentioned at the beginning of the Tafsir that He, the Exalted, praises His holy Self at the beginnings and endings of affairs, for He is the Praised in every state, and to Him belongs praise in this world and the Hereafter. Therefore He praised Himself for sending down His Mighty Book upon His noble Messenger Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. For it is the greatest blessing that Allah has bestowed upon the people of the earth, since through it He brought them out from darkness into light. He made it a straight Book with no crookedness in it and no deviation, but it guides to the Straight Path, clear, plain and manifest, a warner to the disbelievers and a bearer of glad tidings to the believers. Therefore He said: ﴿and has not made in it any crookedness﴾, i.e., He did not put in it any crookedness, deviation or inclination, but made it upright and straight. Therefore He said: ﴿a straight (qayyim) [Book]﴾, i.e., upright.

﴿to warn of severe punishment from Him﴾, i.e., to those who oppose it, deny it and do not believe in it, to warn them of severe punishment, a swift retribution in this world and a deferred one in the Hereafter, ﴿from Him﴾, i.e., from Allah, whose punishment no one can inflict and whose bonds no one can tie.

﴿and give good news to the believers﴾, i.e., by this Qur'an, those who confirm their faith by righteous deeds, ﴿that they will have a good reward﴾, i.e., a beautiful recompense from Allah.

﴿in which they will remain forever﴾, in their reward from Allah, which is Paradise, ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, lasting, with no end and no cessation.

﴿And to warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son."﴾ Ibn Ishaq said: They are the polytheists of the Arabs in their saying: "We worship the angels, and they are the daughters of Allah."

﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾, i.e., of this saying which they have invented and fabricated, ﴿nor do their fathers﴾, i.e., their forefathers.

﴿How great a word it is﴾: it is in the accusative as a specifier (*tamyiz*), its implied sense being: "How great is this word of theirs as a word!"

It was also said: it is an exclamation of wonder, its implied sense being: "How great is their word as a word!" as you say: "How honourable is Zayd as a man!" This was said by some of the Basran grammarians. Some of the Meccan readers read it: ﴿kabura kalimatan﴾, as one says: "Your word is great, and your affair is grand."

The meaning according to the reading of the majority is more apparent, for this is a denunciation of their statement and a magnification of their lie. Therefore He said: ﴿How great a word it is that comes out of their mouths﴾, i.e., it has no basis except their saying, and they have no proof for it except their falsehood and fabrication. Therefore He said: ﴿They say nothing but a lie﴾.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned the reason for the revelation of this noble Surah, saying: A man from the people of Egypt who came to us some forty years ago narrated to me, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Quraysh sent al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt to the rabbis of the Jews in Medina. They said: "You are the people of the Torah, and we have come to you so that you may inform us about this companion of ours." Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 18, verse 9–12:

This is a report about the story of the People of the Cave (ashab al-kahf) and al-Raqim, given in summary and brevity, after which He expanded upon it. He said: ﴿Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were among Our signs a wonder?﴾ meaning: O Muhammad, "that their matter is not astonishing in Our power and authority, for the creation of the heavens and the earth, the alternation of night and day, the subjugation of the sun, the moon and the stars, and other great signs that indicate the power of Allah the Exalted, and that He is capable of whatever He wills, and nothing is beyond His ability, is more wondrous than the accounts of the People of the Cave and al-Raqim." As Ibn Jurayj said, from Mujahid: ﴿Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were among Our signs a wonder?﴾ He says: "There has already been among Our signs what is more wondrous than that!"

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were among Our signs a wonder?﴾ He says: "The knowledge, the Sunnah and the Book that I have given you is better than the affair of the companions of the cave and the inscription."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: "What I have made manifest of My proofs to the servants is more wondrous than the affair of the companions of the cave and the inscription."

[As for "al-kahf" (the cave), it is: the cavern in the mountain, which these youths mentioned took refuge in.] As for "al-Raqim," al-Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: it is a valley near Ayla. Likewise said 'Atiyyah al-Awfi and Qatadah.

From this point he begins to expand on the story and explain it. He mentions that they were youths (*fityah*, meaning young men), and that they were more receptive to the truth and better guided to the path than the elders, who had persisted and grown obstinate (*'ataw wa 'asaw*, in one manuscript "ghashsaw") in the religion of falsehood. For this reason most of those who responded to Allah and His Messenger ﷺ were young. As for the elders of Quraysh, most of them remained upon their religion, and only a few of them embraced Islam. Likewise, Allah the Exalted described the People of the Cave as young men.

Mujahid said: "It has reached me that some of them had earrings (*qiratah*, meaning rings) in their ears. So Allah inspired them with their right guidance and granted them their piety. So they believed in their Lord," that is, they acknowledged His oneness and testified that there is no god but Him.

﴿And We increased them in guidance﴾. Several imams, such as al-Bukhari and others, have used this verse and similar ones as evidence for those who hold that faith increases and varies in degree, and that it can grow and diminish. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We increased them in guidance﴾, as He said: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and grants them their piety﴾ [Muhammad: 17], and He said: ﴿As for those who believed, it has increased them in faith﴾ [at-Tawbah: 124], and He said: ﴿That they may increase in faith along with their faith﴾ [al-Fath: 4], along with other verses that indicate this.

It has been mentioned that they were upon the religion of 'Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, but Allah knows best. The apparent view is that they were before the Christian religion altogether, for if they had been upon the Christian religion, the rabbis (*ahbar*, meaning scholars) of the Jews would not have taken care to preserve their report and their matter, since the Jews were opposed to the Christians. It has already been related from Ibn 'Abbas that the Quraysh sent to the rabbis of the Jews in Madinah, seeking from them things with which to test the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So they sent word to them to ask him about the story of these people, about the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn, and about the Spirit. This indicates that this matter is preserved in the books of the People of the Book, and that it precedes the Christian religion, and Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We strengthened their hearts when they stood up and said: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾. The Exalted says: We gave them patience in opposing their people and their city, and in leaving the comfortable life, happiness and blessings they had been in. Several exegetes from the early generations and later ones have mentioned that they were among the sons of the kings and leaders of the Romans. They went out one day to one of their people's festivals, which was a gathering they held once a year outside the city, where they worshipped idols and *tawaghit* (false deities, objects worshipped besides Allah) and slaughtered animals for them. They had a tyrannical, obstinate king called "Daqyanus," who commanded the people to do this, urged them toward it and called them to it. When the people went out to that gathering, and these youths went out with their fathers and their people, and they looked at what their people were doing with the eye of their insight, they realized that what their people were doing, prostrating to their idols and slaughtering for them, was not fitting except for Allah, who created the heavens and the earth. So each one of them began to separate himself from his people, withdraw from them and seek a place apart from them. The first of them to sit alone (*wahdah*) beneath the shade of a tree was one of them. Then another came and sat beside him, another came and sat beside both of them, another came and sat beside them, and another came, and another, and another, and none of them knew the other. What gathered them there was He who had gathered their hearts upon faith, as came in the hadith which al-Bukhari related in suspended form (*mu'allaq*), from the hadith of Yahya ibn Sa'id, from 'Amrah, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Souls are armies gathered together; those among them who recognize one another become friends, and those who are strangers to one another differ." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3336]. Muslim also related it in his Sahih from the hadith of Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ. [Sahih Muslim, no. 2638]

The people say: "The reason for the *damm* (the vowel *u*) is *al-jinsiyyah*" (the sense of kind or species).

The point is that each one of them concealed what he was in from his companions, out of fear of them, and did not know that they were like him, until one of them said: "By Allah, O people, what brought you out from your people and separated you from them is nothing but a matter. Let each one of you reveal his affair." Another said: "As for me, by Allah, I saw what my people were upon, and I knew that it was falsehood. What truly deserves to be worshipped alone, with nothing associated with Him, is Allah, who created everything: the heavens, the earth and what is between them." Another said: "And by Allah, the same happened to me." And another said the same, until they all agreed upon one word, and they became one hand and true brothers. So they built for themselves a place of worship in which they worshipped Allah. Their people came to know about them, so they informed on their affair to their king. He summoned them before him and asked them about their affair and what they were upon. They answered him with the truth and called him to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. For this reason the Exalted informed about them with His saying: ﴿And We strengthened their hearts when they stood up and said: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never call upon any god besides Him. Indeed, we would have spoken an excessive transgression﴾. The word *lan* (never) is for negating perpetuity, meaning: this will never happen from us, because if we did that it would be falsehood. For this reason He said of them: ﴿We would have spoken an excessive transgression﴾, that is, falsehood, lying and slander.

﴿These our people have taken gods besides Him. Why do they not bring for them a clear authority?﴾ That is, why did they not establish for what they went to a clear and sound proof? ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾ They say: Rather, they are unjust and liars in their saying that. It is said that when their king was called to belief in Allah, he refused them, threatened and warned them, and ordered that the garments of adornment of their people be stripped from them, and he gave them a respite to consider their affair, perhaps they would return to the religion they had been upon. This was from the *lutf* (subtle kindness) of Allah toward them, for during that respite they managed to flee from him and escape with their religion from the trial.

This is what is prescribed when trials befall people: that the servant flees from them out of fear for his religion, as came in the hadith: "It will soon be that the best property of one of you will be a flock he follows to the mountain peaks and the places of rain, fleeing with his religion from trials." [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 19, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.] In this state, withdrawal from people is legislated, and it is not legislated otherwise, because by it one would miss the congregations and Friday prayers.

At that moment the Prophet ﷺ said, when he saw the anxiety of al-Siddiq, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, if one of them looked at the place of our feet, he would see us." He said: "O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two whom Allah is the third of?" And Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿If you do not support him, Allah has already supported him when those who disbelieved expelled him, the second of two. When they were in the cave, when he said to his companion, "Do not grieve; indeed Allah is with us." So Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with soldiers you did not see, and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is the highest. And Allah is Mighty and Wise﴾ [at-Tawbah: 40]. So the story of this cave is more noble, greater, more magnificent and more wondrous than the story of the People of the Cave. It has been said: their people did overcome them, and they stood at the door of the cave they had entered, and said: "We did not want from them any punishment greater than what they inflicted upon themselves." So the king ordered that its door be sealed up over them, so that they would perish where they were, and that was done. About this there is room for consideration, and Allah knows best, for Allah the Exalted has informed that the sun enters upon them in the cave in the morning and the evening, as He said:

This is a proof that the entrance of this cave faces north, because He, exalted is He, informed that when the sun rises it inclines away from it to the right (﴿dhat al-yamin﴾), meaning the shade contracts toward the right, as Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatadah said. ﴿Tazawaru﴾ means it inclines. That is because whenever it rises higher on the horizon, its rays contract with its rising until nothing of it remains in that place at midday. Therefore He said: ﴿And when it sets, it passes them on the left﴾, meaning it enters their cave from the left side of its door, which is from the direction of the east. This confirms what we have said, and it is clear to anyone who reflects on it and has knowledge of the configuration of the heavens and the movement of the sun, moon and stars. Its explanation is that if the mouth of the cave were on the east side, nothing of the sun would enter it at sunset; and if it were on the qiblah side, nothing of it would enter at sunrise or sunset, and the shade would not incline to the right or left. And if it were on the west side, the sun would not enter it at sunrise, but only after midday, and it would remain in it until sunset. So what we have mentioned is established, and to Allah belongs all praise.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: ﴿taqriduhum﴾ means "they leave them."

Allah, exalted is He, has informed us of this and wanted us to understand and reflect upon it, but He did not inform us of the location of this cave in which of the lands of the earth, since there is no benefit for us in it and no legislated purpose. Some exegetes have burdened themselves and mentioned sayings about it. It has preceded from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: [it is] near Ayla. Ibn Ishaq said: it is near Nineveh. It was said: in the lands of the Romans. It was said: in the lands of al-Balqa'. And Allah knows best in which of Allah's lands it is. Had there been a religious benefit for us in it, Allah and His Messenger would have guided us to it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have not left anything that brings you closer to Paradise and distances you from the Fire except that I have informed you of it." So He informed us of its description and did not inform us of its place. Then He said: ﴿And you would see the sun, when it rises, inclining away from their cave to the right, and when it sets, passing them on the left while they were in a wide space within it﴾. Malik narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam: it inclines. ﴿Dhat al-yamin, and when it sets, passing them on the left, while they were in a wide space within it﴾, meaning in a spacious area within it, inside, such that it does not touch them; for if it struck them it would burn their bodies and their garments. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

﴿That is of the signs of Allah﴾, in that He guided them to this cave in which He made them living, while the sun and wind enter upon them in it so that their bodies would remain intact. Therefore He said: ﴿That is of the signs of Allah﴾.

Then He said: ﴿Whomever Allah guides, he is the rightly guided; but whomever He leads astray, you will not find for him a guiding ally﴾, meaning: He is the One who guided these youths to guidance from among their people, for whomever Allah guides is guided, and whomever He misguides has no guide.

Some scholars have mentioned that when God put them to sleep, He did not close their eyes, so that decay would not quickly reach them. If their eyes remain open to the air, they last longer. For this reason, God says: ﴿And you would think them awake, while they were asleep﴾.

It is also reported about the wolf that it sleeps by closing one eye and opening the other, then opens the first and closes the second while still asleep, as the poet said: [Hamid ibn Thawr, *Diwan*, p. 104; note from the Sha'b edition:] "He sleeps with one of his eyelids, and with the other he guards against calamities, so he is awake and asleep at once."

* *

God says: ﴿And We turned them to the right and to the left﴾. Some of the *salaf* (early generation) said: "They were turned twice a year." Ibn 'Abbas said: "If they had not been turned, the earth would have consumed them."

* *

God says: ﴿And their dog stretched out its forelegs at the threshold﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada, Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: *al-wasid* means the courtyard (*al-fina'*).

Ibn 'Abbas also said: "At the door." It was also said: "On the dust (*al-sa'id*)," which is earth. The correct view is that it refers to the courtyard, which is the door. From the same root is God's words: ﴿Indeed, it is closed over them﴾ [al-Humazah: 8], meaning sealed and shut. It is also said: *wasid* and *asid*.

The dog lay down at the door, as dogs customarily do. Ibn Jurayj said: "It guarded the door for them." This was part of its nature and disposition, as it lay at their door as if guarding them. Its sitting was outside the door, because angels do not enter a house that contains a dog, as is related in the Sahih, or an image, or a person in a state of major ritual impurity (*junub*), or a disbeliever, as the sound hadith states. [Ibn Kathir cites the hadith from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, marfu': "Angels do not enter a house containing an image, a dog, or one in a state of major impurity."] The blessing of their company extended to their dog, so it was struck by the same sleep they were in. This is the benefit of keeping good company, for this dog gained mention, news, and renown.

It has been said that it was a hunting dog belonging to one of them, and this is the most likely view. It was also said that it belonged to the king's cook, and that he had agreed with them on the religion, so his dog accompanied him. God knows best.

Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir related in his biography of Hammam ibn al-Walid al-Dimashqi: Sadaqa ibn 'Umar al-Ghassani narrated to us: 'Abbad al-Minqari narrated to us: I heard al-Hasan al-Basri, may God have mercy on him, say: "The name of Abraham's ram was Jarir, the name of Solomon's hoopoe was 'Anqaz, the name of the dog of the People of the Cave was Qitmir, and the name of the calf of the Children of Israel that they worshipped was Bahmut. Adam, peace be upon him, descended in India, Eve in Jeddah, Iblis at Dast Baysan, and the serpent at Isfahan."

[Ibn Kathir notes: see *Mukhtasar Tarikh Dimashq* by Ibn Manzur (27/143).]

It has previously been mentioned, from Shu'ayb al-Jubba'i, that he named it Himran.

They differed about its color, with views that yield no benefit, no advantage, and no evidence, and there is no need for them. Rather, they are among the things that are forbidden, for their basis is guessing about the unseen.

* *

God says: ﴿If you had looked at them, you would have turned away from them in flight, and you would have been filled with dread of them﴾. That is, God cast awe upon them, such that no one who looked at them failed to be awed, because of the majesty and terror with which they were clothed, so that no one would approach them or touch them, until the Decree reached its term and their sleep, which God willed for them, came to its end, owing to the conclusive proof and wisdom, and the vast mercy that He has in that.

Allah the Exalted says: Just as We put them to sleep, We raised them up with their bodies, hair and skin sound, having lost nothing of their condition or appearance. This was after three hundred and nine years. For this reason they asked one another: ﴿How long have you remained?﴾ That is, how long have you slept? ﴿They said: We have remained a day or part of a day.﴾ They had entered the cave at the start of a day and awoke at the end of a day. For this reason they corrected themselves and said: ﴿Or part of a day. Your Lord knows best how long you have remained.﴾ That is, Allah knows your condition best. It seems they had some doubt about the length of their long sleep, so Allah knows best. Then they turned to what mattered most to them at that time, which was their need for food and drink, and said: ﴿So send one of you with this silver of yours.﴾ That is, this silver of yours. They had brought dirhams with them from their homes for their needs, and they had given some of it in charity and some of it remained. For this reason they said: ﴿So send one of you with this silver of yours to the city.﴾ That is, your city from which you left. The definite article (al-alif wa al-lam) here indicates a known place.

﴿Then let him look to which of them has the purest food.﴾ That is, the best food. This is like His saying: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been purified﴾ [An-Nur: 21], and His saying: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself﴾ [Al-A'la: 14]. From this comes zakah (obligatory almsgiving), which purifies and cleanses wealth. It was also said: the most food, and from this comes the zakah of crops when they increase. The poet said: [The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (15/148) and is unattributed.]

Our tribes are seven, and you are three,
and the seven are purer and better than three.

The first view is the correct one, because their aim was only what is pure and lawful, whether it was little or much.

* *

His saying ﴿And let him be discreet﴾ means in his going out and his leaving, and in his buying and returning. They said: let him be as hidden as he can. ﴿And let him not alert anyone about you. Indeed, if they discover you, they will stone you﴾ means if they learn of your whereabouts, ﴿they will stone you or return you to their religion.﴾ They meant the companions of Decius (Daqyanus), whom they feared would discover their place. They would keep torturing them with every kind of torment until they returned them to the religion they followed, or they died. If they were to agree to return to the religion, then ﴿you will never succeed then, ever,﴾ neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. For this reason it was said: ﴿And you will never succeed then, ever.﴾

Allah the Exalted says: Just as We put them to sleep, We raised them up with their bodies, hair and skin sound, having lost nothing of their condition or appearance. This was after three hundred and nine years. For this reason they asked one another: ﴿How long have you remained?﴾ That is, how long have you slept? ﴿They said: We have remained a day or part of a day.﴾ They had entered the cave at the start of a day and awoke at the end of a day. For this reason they corrected themselves and said: ﴿Or part of a day. Your Lord knows best how long you have remained.﴾ That is, Allah knows your condition best. It seems they had some doubt about the length of their long sleep, so Allah knows best. Then they turned to what mattered most to them at that time, which was their need for food and drink, and said: ﴿So send one of you with this silver of yours.﴾ That is, this silver of yours. They had brought dirhams with them from their homes for their needs, and they had given some of it in charity and some of it remained. For this reason they said: ﴿So send one of you with this silver of yours to the city.﴾ That is, your city from which you left. The definite article (al-alif wa al-lam) here indicates a known place.

﴿Then let him look to which of them has the purest food.﴾ That is, the best food. This is like His saying: ﴿Had it not been for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been purified﴾ [An-Nur: 21], and His saying: ﴿He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself﴾ [Al-A'la: 14]. From this comes zakah (obligatory almsgiving), which purifies and cleanses wealth. It was also said: the most food, and from this comes the zakah of crops when they increase. The poet said: [The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (15/148) and is unattributed.]

Our tribes are seven, and you are three,
and the seven are purer and better than three.

The first view is the correct one, because their aim was only what is pure and lawful, whether it was little or much.

* *

His saying ﴿And let him be discreet﴾ means in his going out and his leaving, and in his buying and returning. They said: let him be as hidden as he can. ﴿And let him not alert anyone about you. Indeed, if they discover you, they will stone you﴾ means if they learn of your whereabouts, ﴿they will stone you or return you to their religion.﴾ They meant the companions of Decius (Daqyanus), whom they feared would discover their place. They would keep torturing them with every kind of torment until they returned them to the religion they followed, or they died. If they were to agree to return to the religion, then ﴿you will never succeed then, ever,﴾ neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. For this reason it was said: ﴿And you will never succeed then, ever.﴾

Allah the Exalted says: "And thus We caused them to be discovered" (wa-kadhalika a'thar-na 'alayhim), meaning: We let the people become aware of them, "that they might know that the promise of Allah is true and that the Hour, there is no doubt in it" (li-ya'lamu anna wa'da Allahi haqqun wa-anna as-sa'ata la rayba fiha).

Many of the early scholars (al-salaf) mentioned that among the people of that era there had arisen doubt about the resurrection and the matter of the Day of Judgment. 'Ikrimah said: Among them was a group who said, "Spirits will be resurrected, but bodies will not be resurrected." So Allah raised up the People of the Cave as a proof (hujjah), a sign (dalalah) and an indication (ayah) of that.

They mentioned that when one of them wished to go out to the city to buy some food for them to eat, he disguised himself and went out walking off the main road, until he reached the city. They mentioned that its name was Diqsus (also given as Daqus), and he thought he was still recently near it, for the people had changed generation after generation, era after era, and nation after nation, and the lands and those upon them had changed, as the poet said:

"As for the abodes, they are like their abodes, but I see the men of the tribe are not their men..."

So he began not to recognize any of the landmarks of the town that he knew, nor did he recognize anyone from its people, neither its elite nor its common folk. So he began to be bewildered within himself and to say: "Perhaps there is madness in me, or possession, or perhaps I am dreaming." And he would say: "By Allah, there is nothing wrong with me of that sort, and my last time in this town was yesterday evening, not in this condition." Then he said: "Hastening out from here would be better for me." Then he went to a man who sold food, handed him the money he had with him, and asked him to sell him food with it. When that man saw the money he denied it and denied its minting, so he passed it to his neighbour, and they began passing it around among themselves, saying: "Perhaps this man has found a treasure." They asked him about his affair, and from where he had this expense. "Perhaps he found it from a treasure." And "Who are you?" So he began to say: "I am from the people of this city, and my last time in it was yesterday evening, and in it was Decius (Daqyanus)." So they attributed him to madness, and took him to their ruler, who asked him about his circumstances and his affair until he informed them of his matter, while he was bewildered about his state and what he was in. When he informed them of that, the governor of the town and its people set out with him to the cave, until they reached it with him. He said: "Leave me until I go ahead of you into the entrance, to inform my companions," and it is said that they did not know how he went into it, for Allah concealed his news from them. It is also said: "Rather, they entered upon them, saw them, and the king greeted them and embraced them, and he was a Muslim, as it is said, and his name was Tidusisus (Tiderisin, Bidusis)." So they rejoiced at him and made him at ease by speaking with him, then they bade him farewell and greeted him, and returned to their resting places, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, caused them to die. And Allah knows best.

Qatadah said: Ibn 'Abbas campaigned with Habib ibn Maslamah, and they passed by a cave in the lands of the Romans, and they saw in it bones. Someone said: "These are the bones of the People of the Cave?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "Their bones have decayed for more than three hundred years." Narrated by Ibn Jarir.

* *

His saying: "And thus We caused them to be discovered" (a'thar-na) [in one manuscript: "a'thar-nahum", which is an error] means: just as We put them to sleep and woke them with their condition, We made the people of that time aware of them, "that they might know that the promise of Allah is true and that the Hour, there is no doubt in it, when they disputed among themselves concerning their affair" (idh yatanaza'una baynahum amrahum), meaning: concerning the matter of the Resurrection, some affirming it and some denying it. So Allah made their discovery a proof for them and against them, the People of the Cave. "Then they said: Build over them a structure; their Lord knows best about them" (fa-qalu ibnu 'alayhim bunyanan rabbuhum a'lamu bihim), meaning: seal the entrance of their cave and leave them in their state. "Those who prevailed over their affair said: We will surely take over them a place of worship" (qala alladhina ghalabu 'ala amrihim la-nattakhidhanna 'alayhim masjidan).

Ibn Jarir reports two opinions regarding those who said that: one is that they were from among the Muslims; the other is that they were from among the polytheists. And Allah knows best.

The apparent meaning is that those who said this were the people of influence and authority. But whether they are praiseworthy or not is open to consideration, because the Prophet ﷺ said: "May Allah curse the Jews and the Christians, who took the graves of their prophets and righteous men as places of worship," warning against what they did. (Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 1330, from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.) And it has been related to us from the Commander of the Faithful 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that when he found the grave of Daniel in his time in Iraq, he ordered that it be concealed from the people, and that the scroll they found beside it, which contained some of the prophecies of wars (al-malahim) and other matters, be buried.

Allah the Exalted says, informing about the people's disagreement concerning the number of the Companions of the Cave. He related three opinions, which indicates that there is no fourth opinion. He refuted the first two by His saying: ﴿conjecturing about the unseen﴾, meaning speaking without knowledge, like one who shoots at a place he does not know; he hardly hits it, and if he does hit it, it is by chance. Then He related the third and remained silent about it, or affirmed it by His saying: ﴿and their eighth is their dog﴾, which indicates its correctness and that it is what actually occurred.

* *

His saying: ﴿Say, "My Lord knows best their number"﴾ is a guidance that the best course in such a situation is to refer knowledge to Allah the Exalted, since there is no need to delve into such matters without knowledge. But if He informs us of something, we speak accordingly; otherwise we stop where we stop.

* *

His saying: ﴿None knows them except a few﴾ means: of the people. Qatadah said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "I am of the few whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, excepted. They were seven." Likewise Ibn Jurayj related from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from him, that he used to say: "I am among those whom Allah excepted," and he would say: "Their number was seven."

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿None knows them except a few﴾ He said: "I am of the few. They were seven."

These are sound chains of narration from Ibn 'Abbas that they were seven, and this agrees with what we have already mentioned.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "I have been told that on some of them was the bloom of their youth and the silver shine of their faces." Ibn 'Abbas said: "They remained thus, night and day, in the worship of Allah, weeping and seeking help from Allah. They were eight men: Maksalmina, who was the eldest and the one who spoke to the king on their behalf; Majsimilina and Tamlikha, Maratunas, Kashtunas, Bayruynas, Dimus, Yatunas and Qaluwush."

This is what occurs in this narration, and it is possible that this is from the words of Ibn Ishaq, or from someone between him and Ibn 'Abbas, for the authentic report from Ibn 'Abbas is that they were seven, and this is the apparent meaning of the verse. It has already been related from Shu'ayb al-Jaba'i that the name of their dog was Himran, but the soundness of naming them with these names and the name of their dog is open to doubt, and Allah knows best; for most of this is taken from the People of the Book. Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument﴾, meaning, lightly and easily, since knowing these details does not produce any great benefit. ﴿And do not seek a ruling concerning them from any of them﴾, meaning, they have no knowledge of this except what they say from their own opinions, conjecturing about the unseen, that is, without relying on an infallible speech. And there has come to you, O Muhammad, the truth about which there is no doubt or uncertainty, which is the one that prevails over and judges all the books and sayings that preceded it.

This is an instruction from Allah to His Messenger ﷺ regarding etiquette when he resolves to do something in the future: that he should attach the matter to the will of Allah, 'Azza wa Jall, the Knower of the unseen, who knows what has been and what will be, and what would have been had it been, how it would have been. This is as established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both, said: "Tonight I will go round to seventy women" — and in another narration ninety women, and in another narration a hundred women — "each of whom will bear a boy who will fight in the way of Allah." Then it was said to him — and in another narration, the angel said to him — "Say: If Allah wills." But he did not say it, so he went round to them, and none of them bore a child except one woman, who bore half a man." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, had he said, 'If Allah wills,' he would not have broken his oath, and it would have been a fulfilment of his need." And in another narration: "And they would have fought in the way of Allah as horsemen, all of them." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5242 for the narration of the hundred, and no. 6720 for the narration of the ninety; Sahih Muslim, no. 1654.)

It has already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah the cause of the revelation of this verse, in the words of the Prophet ﷺ when he was asked about the story of the People of the Cave: "Tomorrow I will answer you." Then the revelation was delayed for fifteen days. We have mentioned it in full at the beginning of the surah, so there is no need to repeat it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾, it is said: its meaning is, when you forget the exception (istithna'), then make the exception when you remember it. This was said by Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Hasan al-Basri.

Hushaym said, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning a man who swears an oath: he said, "He may make the exception even after a year." He would recite: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾ in this regard. It was said to al-A'mash: "Did you hear this from Mujahid?" He said: "Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated it to me, and I think my cloak went with it" (i.e., he was joking about his memory).

Al-Tabarani also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, with the same chain.

The meaning of Ibn 'Abbas's statement, "He may make the exception even after a year," is: if he forgot to say "If Allah wills" in his oath or his speech, and then remembered, even after a year, then the Sunnah for him is to say it, so that he has acted upon the Sunnah of the exception, even if that is after the breaking of the oath. Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said, and explicitly stated this: it does not mean that this (exception) lifts the breaking of the oath or cancels the expiation. This which Ibn Jarir said, may Allah have mercy on him, is the correct view, and it is the most fitting way to understand the words of Ibn 'Abbas, and Allah knows best.

'Ikrimah said: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾ means: when you become angry. This is an explanation by a necessary consequence (tafsir bil-lazim).

Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Hulwani narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And never say of anything, "I will certainly do that tomorrow," unless [adding] "If Allah wills." And remember your Lord when you forget﴾ — meaning, that you say: "If Allah wills." This is an explanation by a necessary consequence.

Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn al-Harith al-Jubayli narrated to us, Safwan ibn Salih narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Husayn, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And never say of anything, "I will certainly do that tomorrow," unless [adding] "If Allah wills." And remember your Lord when you forget﴾ — that you say: "If Allah wills."

Al-Tabarani also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾ — the exception: "make the exception when you remember." And he said: it is specific to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it is not for any of us to make an exception except in connection with his oath. Then he said: al-Walid alone narrated it, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Husayn.

There is another possible meaning of the verse: that Allah, 'Azza wa Jall, guided the one who forgets something in his speech to the remembrance of Allah the Exalted, because forgetfulness originates from Satan, as the young man of Musa said: ﴿And none made me forget it except Satan, that I should mention it﴾ [al-Kahf: 63]. And the remembrance of Allah the Exalted drives away Satan, and when Satan departs, forgetfulness departs. So the remembrance of Allah is a cause of remembering; for this reason He said: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿And say: "It may be that my Lord will guide me to what is nearer to right guidance than this"﴾, meaning: when you are asked about something you do not know, ask Allah concerning it, and turn to Him that He may grant you success in what is correct and rightly guided. [Something else has been said in its interpretation besides this, and Allah knows best.]

This is an instruction from Allah to His Messenger ﷺ regarding etiquette when he resolves to do something in the future: that he should attach the matter to the will of Allah, 'Azza wa Jall, the Knower of the unseen, who knows what has been and what will be, and what would have been had it been, how it would have been. This is as established in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both, said: "Tonight I will go round to seventy women" — and in another narration ninety women, and in another narration a hundred women — "each of whom will bear a boy who will fight in the way of Allah." Then it was said to him — and in another narration, the angel said to him — "Say: If Allah wills." But he did not say it, so he went round to them, and none of them bore a child except one woman, who bore half a man." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, had he said, 'If Allah wills,' he would not have broken his oath, and it would have been a fulfilment of his need." And in another narration: "And they would have fought in the way of Allah as horsemen, all of them." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5242 for the narration of the hundred, and no. 6720 for the narration of the ninety; Sahih Muslim, no. 1654.)

It has already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah the cause of the revelation of this verse, in the words of the Prophet ﷺ when he was asked about the story of the People of the Cave: "Tomorrow I will answer you." Then the revelation was delayed for fifteen days. We have mentioned it in full at the beginning of the surah, so there is no need to repeat it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾, it is said: its meaning is, when you forget the exception (istithna'), then make the exception when you remember it. This was said by Abu al-'Aliyah and al-Hasan al-Basri.

Hushaym said, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning a man who swears an oath: he said, "He may make the exception even after a year." He would recite: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾ in this regard. It was said to al-A'mash: "Did you hear this from Mujahid?" He said: "Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated it to me, and I think my cloak went with it" (i.e., he was joking about his memory).

Al-Tabarani also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, with the same chain.

The meaning of Ibn 'Abbas's statement, "He may make the exception even after a year," is: if he forgot to say "If Allah wills" in his oath or his speech, and then remembered, even after a year, then the Sunnah for him is to say it, so that he has acted upon the Sunnah of the exception, even if that is after the breaking of the oath. Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, said, and explicitly stated this: it does not mean that this (exception) lifts the breaking of the oath or cancels the expiation. This which Ibn Jarir said, may Allah have mercy on him, is the correct view, and it is the most fitting way to understand the words of Ibn 'Abbas, and Allah knows best.

'Ikrimah said: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾ means: when you become angry. This is an explanation by a necessary consequence (tafsir bil-lazim).

Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Hulwani narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from 'Abbad ibn al-'Awwam, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, from Jabir ibn Zayd, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And never say of anything, "I will certainly do that tomorrow," unless [adding] "If Allah wills." And remember your Lord when you forget﴾ — meaning, that you say: "If Allah wills." This is an explanation by a necessary consequence.

Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad ibn al-Harith al-Jubayli narrated to us, Safwan ibn Salih narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Husayn, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And never say of anything, "I will certainly do that tomorrow," unless [adding] "If Allah wills." And remember your Lord when you forget﴾ — that you say: "If Allah wills."

Al-Tabarani also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾ — the exception: "make the exception when you remember." And he said: it is specific to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it is not for any of us to make an exception except in connection with his oath. Then he said: al-Walid alone narrated it, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn al-Husayn.

There is another possible meaning of the verse: that Allah, 'Azza wa Jall, guided the one who forgets something in his speech to the remembrance of Allah the Exalted, because forgetfulness originates from Satan, as the young man of Musa said: ﴿And none made me forget it except Satan, that I should mention it﴾ [al-Kahf: 63]. And the remembrance of Allah the Exalted drives away Satan, and when Satan departs, forgetfulness departs. So the remembrance of Allah is a cause of remembering; for this reason He said: ﴿And remember your Lord when you forget﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿And say: "It may be that my Lord will guide me to what is nearer to right guidance than this"﴾, meaning: when you are asked about something you do not know, ask Allah concerning it, and turn to Him that He may grant you success in what is correct and rightly guided. [Something else has been said in its interpretation besides this, and Allah knows best.]

This is a report from Allah, the Exalted, to His Messenger ﷺ about the length of time the People of the Cave remained in their cave, from the time Allah put them to sleep until He resurrected them and the people of that era came upon them. Its duration was three hundred [years] [[added from manuscript A.]] and nine years according to the lunar calendar (al-Hilaliyyah), which is three hundred years according to the solar calendar (al-Shamsiyyah), since the difference between every hundred [years] [[added from manuscript F.]] of lunar reckoning and solar reckoning is three years. For this reason He said, after the three hundred: ﴿And they added nine﴾.

And His saying: ﴿Say, "Allah knows best how long they stayed"﴾ means: if you are asked about the length of their stay, and you have no knowledge of it nor any divine revelation (tawqif) from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then do not advance anything about it. Rather, say regarding such matters: ﴿Allah knows best how long they stayed. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: none knows that except Him, or whomever Allah has informed of it from among His creation. This that we have stated is the view of more than one of the scholars of tafsir, such as Mujahid, and more than one of the early (salaf) and later (khalaf) scholars.

Qatadah said regarding His saying: ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾: "This is the statement of the People of the Scripture, and Allah has refuted it by His saying: ﴿Say, 'Allah knows best how long they stayed.'" He said: "And in the recitation of Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: 'And they said: And they remained...'" meaning that people said it.

Likewise said, as Qatadah said, Mutarrif ibn Abdullah.

There is scrutiny in what Qatadah claimed, for what is in the hands of the People of the Book is that they remained three hundred years without the nine, meaning by the solar calendar. Had Allah related their statement, He would not have said: ﴿And they added nine﴾. The apparent meaning of the verse is only a report from Allah, not a relating of their words. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him. The narration of Qatadah regarding the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud is discontinuous (munqati'ah), and further it is shadh (irregular) in relation to the recitation of the majority, so it cannot be used as evidence. And Allah knows best.

And His saying: ﴿Observe Him and hear Him﴾ means: indeed He is All-Seeing of them and All-Hearing of them.

Ibn Jarir said: This is in the sense of emphasis in praise, as if it were said: how seeing He is and how hearing He is. The meaning of the statement is: how seeing Allah is of every existing thing, and how hearing He is of every sound; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

Then it was related from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿Observe Him and hear Him﴾: "No one is more seeing than Allah, nor more hearing."

Ibn Zayd said: ﴿Observe Him and hear Him﴾ — He sees their deeds and hears them from them, [being] All-Hearing, All-Seeing.

And His saying: ﴿They have not, besides Him, any protector, and He does not share His command with anyone﴾ means: He, Exalted is He, is the One to whom belong creation and command, whose judgment none can reverse, and who has no minister, no helper, no partner, no counselor. Exalted and sanctified is He.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 18, verses 27–28:

Allah the Exalted says, commanding His Messenger [peace be upon him] [[Addition from A.]] to recite His Mighty Book and to convey it to the people: ﴿There is none who can change His words.﴾ That is: none can alter them, distort them, or give them a false interpretation. [[In T and F: "i.e., without alteration."]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And you will not find any refuge other than Him.﴾ [From Mujahid: regarding ﴿multaḥadan﴾, he said: "a refuge." From Qatadah: "a protector, nor a patron."] [[Addition from A.]] Ibn Jarir said: "It means: O Muhammad, if you do not recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord, then there is no refuge for you from Allah." Just as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people.﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 67]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, He who imposed the Qur'an upon you will surely return you to a place of return.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 85], meaning: He will surely call you to account for what He has imposed upon you of conveying the message.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And keep yourself patient [by staying] with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face.﴾ That is: sit with those who remember Allah, declare His oneness (tahlil), praise Him, glorify Him, magnify Him, and ask Him morning and evening, from among the servants of Allah, whether they are poor or rich, strong or weak. It is said that it was revealed concerning the nobles of Quraysh, when they asked the Prophet ﷺ to sit with them alone [[In T and F: "alone with them."]] and not sit with the weak among his companions such as Bilal, 'Ammar, Suhayb, [and Khabbab] [[Addition from F.]], and Ibn Mas'ud, and that those (the weak companions) should be given a separate gathering of their own. So Allah forbade him from that, saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾ [Al-An'am: 52], [and so on] [[In T: "and so on."]], and He commanded him to restrain himself to sit with these people, saying: ﴿And keep yourself patient [by staying] with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face.﴾

Muslim said in his Sahih: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Asadi narrated to us, from Isra'il, from al-Miqdam ibn Shurayh, from his father, from Sa'd, the son of Abi Waqqas, who said: "We were with the Prophet ﷺ, six men. The polytheists said to the Prophet ﷺ: 'Drive these people away, so that they do not dare against us!' He said: 'I, Ibn Mas'ud, a man from Hudhayl, Bilal, and two men whose names I have forgotten [[In T, F: "their names."]] were [there].' So what Allah willed to occur occurred in the soul of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he spoke to himself, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic revealed: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face.﴾" Muslim alone narrated it, not al-Bukhari. [Sahih Muslim, no. 2413.]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, who said: "I heard Abu al-Ja'd narrating from Abu Umamah, who said: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to a storyteller (qass) who was telling stories, and he stopped. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Continue. Sitting from dawn until the sun rises is more beloved to me than freeing four slaves."'" [Al-Musnad 5/261.]

Imam Ahmad also said: Hashim narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn Maysarah, who said: "I heard Kurdus ibn Qays, who was the storyteller of the common people in Kufa, say: 'A man from the companions of Badr informed me that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "To sit in a gathering like this is more beloved to me than freeing four slaves."'" Shu'bah said: "I said: 'What gathering?' He said: 'It was a storyteller's gathering.'" [[In T: "a storyteller."]] [Al-Musnad 3/474. Only Ibn Hibban declared Kurdus ibn Qays trustworthy.]

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said in his Musnad: Muhammad narrated to us, Yazid ibn Aban narrated to us, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "To sit with a people who remember Allah from the dawn prayer until the sunrise is more beloved to me than what the sun rises upon. And to remember Allah from the afternoon prayer until the sunset is more beloved to me than freeing eight from the descendants of Isma'il, the blood-money (diyah) of each of them being twelve thousand." So we calculated their blood-money while we were in the gathering of Anas, and it came to ninety-six thousand. [[In T: "and seventy thousand."]] Someone here says: "Four from the descendants of Isma'il," but by Allah he only said eight, the blood-money of each of them being twelve [[In T: "twelve"(fem.).]] thousand. [Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. 2104. Yazid ibn Aban is weak.]

The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Thabit narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn al-Aqmar, from al-Aghar Abi [[In T: "i.e."]] Muslim, the one from Kufa, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a man who was reciting Surah al-Kahf. When he saw the Prophet ﷺ he stopped, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This is the gathering that I was commanded to be patient with them."

This was narrated by Abu Ahmad from 'Amr ibn Thabit, from 'Ali ibn al-Aqmar, from al-Aghar, as a mursal (a report whose chain omits a companion). [[Transmitted to us by Yahya ibn al-Mu'alla, from Mansur, who narrated to us Muhammad ibn al-Salt, who narrated to us 'Amr ibn Thabit, from 'Ali ibn al-Aqmar, from al-Aghar Abi Muslim [[In T: "al-Aghar ibn Abi Muslim."]] from Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa'id, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came while a man was reciting Surah al-Hijr or Surah al-Kahf, so he stopped, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'This is the gathering that I was commanded to be patient with them.'"]] [Musnad al-Bazzar, nos. 5232, 2326 (Kashf al-Astar). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/164): "In it is 'Amr ibn Thabit Abu al-Miqdam, who is abandoned (matruk)."]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Bakr [[In F, A: "Bukayr."]] narrated to us, Maymun al-Mar'i narrated to us, Maymun ibn Siyah narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "No people gather remembering Allah, seeking nothing but His face, except that a caller calls out to them from the heaven: 'Arise, you are forgiven, and your evil deeds have been changed into good deeds.'" [Al-Musnad 3/142. Maymun al-Mar'i is weak.] Ahmad alone narrated it, may Allah have mercy on him.

Al-Tabarani said: Isma'il ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, from Usamah ibn Zayd, [[In T: "Zaydi."]] from Abu Hazim, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, who said: "This was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was in some of his houses: ﴿And keep yourself patient [by staying] with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face.﴾ So he went out seeking them, and found a people remembering Allah the Exalted, among them one with disheveled hair, one with a rough skin, and one with a single garment. When he saw them, he sat with them and said: 'Praise be to Allah, who has placed among my community those whom Allah commanded me to be patient with.'" [[In F: "the skins."]] [[Also narrated by Ibn Mandah and Abu Nu'aym in al-Sahabah, as in Usd al-Ghabah (3/353), through the path of Abu Hazim.]]

This 'Abd al-Rahman was mentioned by Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud among the Companions. [[Ibn al-Athir rebutted him, saying: "It is not authentic. The companionship belongs only to his father and to his brother Abu Umamah, and he had a sighting (ru'yah)."]] As for his father, he is among the noble Companions, may Allah be pleased with them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not let your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "And do not go beyond them to others; that is: seeking in their place the people of nobility and wealth."

﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance﴾ That is: one who has been preoccupied with the world, away from religion and the worship of his Lord, ﴿and who follows his desire, and whose affair has been [in] excess﴾ [[Addition from F.]] That is: his deeds and actions are foolishness, negligence, and loss. Do not be obedient to him, nor a lover of his way, and do not envy him for what he is in. Just as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given to some pairs of them, the splendor of the worldly life, that We may test them therein. But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 131]

When he saw them, he sat with them and said: 'Praise be to Allah, who has placed among my community those whom Allah commanded me to be patient with.'" [[In F: "the skins."]] [[Also narrated by Ibn Mandah and Abu Nu'aym in al-Sahabah, as in Usd al-Ghabah (3/353), through the path of Abu Hazim.]]

This 'Abd al-Rahman was mentioned by Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud among the Companions. [[Ibn al-Athir rebutted him, saying: "It is not authentic. The companionship belongs only to his father and to his brother Abu Umamah, and he had a sighting (ru'yah)."]] As for his father, he is among the noble Companions, may Allah be pleased with them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not let your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "And do not go beyond them to others; that is: seeking in their place the people of nobility and wealth."

﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance﴾ That is: one who has been preoccupied with the world, away from religion and the worship of his Lord, ﴿and who follows his desire, and whose affair has been [in] excess﴾ [[Addition from F.]] That is: his deeds and actions are foolishness, negligence, and loss. Do not be obedient to him, nor a lover of his way, and do not envy him for what he is in. Just as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward what We have given to some pairs of them, the splendor of the worldly life, that We may test them therein. But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting.﴾ [Ta-Ha: 131]

Allah says to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): "And say, O Muhammad, to the people: 'This which I have brought you from your Lord is the truth, about which there is no doubt or uncertainty.' ﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾. This is in the manner of threat and severe warning. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared﴾, meaning, We have readied, ﴿for the wrongdoers﴾, who are the disbelievers in Allah, His Messenger and His Book, ﴿a Fire whose enclosure will surround them﴾, meaning, its wall."

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham [in (the manuscript) T: "Hushaym"], from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The enclosure of the Fire has four walls, the thickness of each wall being a distance of forty years."

At-Tirmidhi related it in "Sifat al-Nar" (Description of the Fire), and Ibn Jarir in his Tafsir, from the hadith of Darraj Abu al-Samh with this chain.

[Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding ﴿Its enclosure will surround them﴾: "A wall of fire."]

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Husayn ibn Nasr and al-'Abbas ibn Muhammad narrated to me, both saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Umayyah, Muhammad ibn Huyayy ibn Ya'la narrated to me, from Safwan ibn Ya'la, from Ya'la ibn Umayyah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The sea is Jahannam." It was said to him: [How is that?] Then he recited this verse, or he read this verse: ﴿a Fire whose enclosure will surround them﴾, then he said: "By Allah, I will never enter it, or: as long as I am alive, and not a drop of it will touch me."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass that scalds the faces. Wretched is the drink, and evil is the resting place﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Al-Muhl" is thick water like the dregs of oil (durdi al-zayt).

Mujahid said: It is like blood and pus. 'Ikrimah said: It is that whose heat has reached its extreme. Others said: It is everything that has been melted.

Qatadah said: Ibn Mas'ud melted some gold in a trench, and when it flowed and foamed he said: "This is the most similar thing to al-muhl."

al-Dahhak said: The water of Jahannam is black, and it (the Fire) is black and its people are black.

None of these statements negates the others, for al-muhl combines all these vile attributes: it is black, foul-smelling, thick and hot. For this reason He said: ﴿It scalds the faces﴾, meaning, because of its heat. When the disbeliever wants to drink it and brings it near his face, it scalds him until the skin of his face falls into it, as came in the hadith that Imam Ahmad related with his chain mentioned earlier in "Suradiq al-Nar", from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Water like al-muhl." He said: "Like the sediment of oil. When he brings it near himself, the skin of his face falls into it." Likewise, at-Tirmidhi related it in "Sifat al-Nar" in his Jami', from the hadith of Rishdin ibn Sa'd, from 'Amr ibn al-Harith, from Darraj, with it. Then he said: "We only know it from the hadith of Rishdin, and he has been criticised concerning his memory." Thus he said. Imam Ahmad, as mentioned earlier, related it from Hasan al-Ashyab, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Darraj. And Allah knows best.

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak and Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid said, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, from Abdullah ibn Busr, from Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying: ﴿And he will be given to drink of purulent water, which he will gulp﴾ [Ibrahim 14:16–17]: "It is brought near to him and he dislikes it; when it is brought close to him it scalds his face and the skin of his head falls off. When he drinks it, it cuts his intestines." Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass that scalds the faces; wretched is the drink.﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When the people of the Fire become hungry, they call for relief with the tree of al-Zaqqum, and they eat from it, and it strips the skin of their faces; so if a passerby were to pass by them, he would recognise them by the skin of their faces within it. Then thirst is poured upon them and they cry for relief, and they are relieved with water like al-muhl, which is one whose heat has reached its extreme. When they bring it near their mouths, the flesh of their faces, from which the skin has fallen, is roasted by its heat.

For this reason, after describing this drink with these vile and ugly attributes, Allah said: ﴿Wretched is the drink﴾, meaning, wretched is this drink, as He said in another verse: ﴿and they are given boiling water which cuts their intestines﴾ [Muhammad 47:15]. And He said: ﴿They are given to drink from a boiling spring﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 88:5], meaning, hot, as He said: ﴿between it and boiling hot water﴾ [al-Rahman 55:44]. ﴿And evil is the resting place﴾ [meaning, evil is the Fire] as a dwelling, a resting place, a gathering place, and a place of repose, as He said in another verse: ﴿Indeed, it is evil as an abode and a station﴾ [al-Furqan 25:66].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 18, verse 30–31:

When Allah mentioned the state of the wretched, He followed it with the mention of the happy ones, those who believed in Allah and confirmed the messengers in what they brought, and acted upon the righteous deeds they were commanded with. For them are ﴿Gardens of Eden﴾. "Adn" (Eden) means permanence (al-iqamah).

﴿Rivers flow beneath them﴾, i.e., beneath their chambers and dwellings. Pharaoh said: ﴿And these rivers flow beneath me﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 51].

﴿They will be adorned﴾, i.e., with adornment, ﴿therein with bracelets of gold﴾. In another place He said: ﴿and pearls, and their clothing therein is silk﴾ [Al-Hajj: 23], and He detailed it here, saying: ﴿and they will wear green garments of fine silk and brocade﴾. As for sundus, it is a thin, fine garment like shirts and what runs in their manner. As for istabraq, it is thick brocade (dibaj) and in it there is a sheen.

* *

His saying: ﴿reclining therein on couches﴾. Al-ittika' (reclining) has been said to mean lying down, and it has been said to mean sitting cross-legged. The latter is more fitting to the intended meaning here, and from it is the sound hadith: "As for me, I do not eat reclining" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5398], in which both opinions occur.

And al-ara'ik: the plural of arikah, which is a bed beneath a canopy (hajlah). The hajlah, as people in our time know it, is the "bashkhanah," and Allah knows best.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿on couches﴾, he said: they are the canopies (hijal). Ma'mar said: Others said: beds within the canopies [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (1/339)].

* *

His saying: ﴿How excellent is the reward, and how good a resting place﴾ [i.e., the Garden is an excellent reward for their deeds, ﴿and how good a resting place﴾, i.e., good as a dwelling, a place of repose and a station], as He said of the Fire: ﴿Evil is the drink, and evil a resting place﴾ [Al-Kahf: 29]. Likewise, He contrasted the two in Surah Al-Furqan in His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is evil as a settlement and a station﴾ [Al-Furqan: 66]. Then He mentioned the attributes of the believers, saying: ﴿Those will be rewarded with the lofty chamber for what they patiently endured, and they will be met therein with greeting and peace, abiding therein; excellent is it as a settlement and a station﴾ [Al-Furqan: 75–76].

The Exalted said, after mentioning the arrogant polytheists who disdained sitting with the weak and the poor among the Muslims, and who boasted over them with their wealth and their lineage, that He struck for them a parable of two men. God made ﴿for one of them two gardens﴾, that is, two orchards of grapevines, enclosed by palm trees surrounding their sides, and among them were crops. Each of the trees and crops was fruitful and productive, in the utmost abundance. Hence He said: ﴿Each of the two gardens yielded its produce﴾, that is, its fruit came forth, ﴿and did not fall short in anything﴾, that is, it did not diminish in anything. ﴿And We caused a river to gush forth within them﴾, that is, the rivers flowed through them here and there.

﴿And he had fruit﴾. It was said: what is meant by it is wealth. This was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah. It was also said: it means fruits, and this is more apparent here. It is supported by the other reading, "wa kana lahu thumurun" with a damma on the tha' and a sukun on the mim, so that it would be the plural of thamarah, like khashabah and khushub. Others read ﴿thamarun﴾ with a fatha on the tha' and the mim.

﴿He said to his companion, while he was conversing with him﴾, that is, the owner of these two gardens said to his companion, who was disputing and contending with him, boasting over him and showing off: ﴿I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in men﴾, that is, more numerous in servants, retinue, and children.

Qatadah said: "By Allah, that is the wish of the wicked: abundance of wealth and might in men."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And he entered his garden while he was wronging himself﴾, that is, by his disbelief, his rebellion, his arrogance, his tyranny, and his denial of the Return. ﴿He said: I do not think this will ever perish﴾. This was delusion on his part, when he saw in it the crops, fruits, trees, and rivers flowing through its sides and its expanses. He thought that it would never vanish, never be exhausted, never be destroyed, and never be ruined. This was due to the feebleness of his intellect, the weakness of his certainty in Allah, his admiration for the worldly life and its adornment, and his disbelief in the Hereafter. Hence He said: ﴿Nor do I think the Hour will be established﴾, that is, will come to pass. ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination﴾, that is, if there is a resurrection, a return, and a going back to Allah, I will certainly have there something better than this, because I am favoured with my Lord, and had He not held me in honour, He would not have given me this. As He said in another verse: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, indeed I shall have with Him the best﴾ [Fussilat 41:50]. He also said: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?﴾ [Maryam 19:77], that is, in the Hereafter; he swore by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, an oath. The cause of its revelation concerned al-'As ibn Wa'il, as will be explained in its proper place, if Allah the Exalted wills. And in Him is trust.
