And Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah and Hajjaj narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to me, from Asim ibn Ubaydullah, from Ubayd, mawla of Abu Ruhm, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Shall I not direct you to a treasure of the treasures of Paradise? There is no power and no might except in Allah." Ahmad alone related it [al-Musnad 2/469].

It is also established in the Sahih, from Abu Musa, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Shall I not direct you to a treasure of the treasures of Paradise? There is no power and no might except in Allah" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 6610 and Sahih Muslim no. 2704].

And Imam Ahmad said: Bakr ibn Isa narrated to us, Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Abu Balj, from Amr ibn Maymun, who said: Abu Hurayrah said: The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "O Abu Hurayrah, shall I direct you to a treasure of the treasures of Paradise beneath the Throne?" I said: "Yes, may my father and mother be your ransom." He said: "Saying: there is no power except in Allah." Abu Balj said: and I think he (ﷺ) said: "For Allah says: My servant has submitted and surrendered." He said: I said to Amr (Abu Balj said: Amr said): I said to Abu Hurayrah: "There is no might and no power except in Allah?" He said: "No, it is in Surat al-Kahf: ﴿And why, when you entered your garden, did you not say, 'What Allah wills [is so]; there is no power except in Allah'?﴾" [al-Musnad 2/335].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden﴾, that is: in the Hereafter. ﴿And He will send upon it﴾, that is: upon your garden in this world, which you thought would never perish or pass away, ﴿a calamity from the sky﴾. Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and Malik, from al-Zuhri, said: that is, a punishment from the sky.

The apparent meaning is a great, disruptive rain which uproots its crops and trees. For this reason He said: ﴿so that it becomes a barren ground, slippery﴾, that is: a bare, smooth dust, on which no foot can stand firm.

Ibn Abbas said: like a barren land that produces nothing.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Or its water becomes sunken, so you will never be able to seek it﴾, that is: sinking into the earth. It is the opposite of a spring that rises to the surface of the earth; the sunken water is sought at its depths, as Allah says: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if your water should become sunken, who would bring you flowing water?﴾ [Al-Mulk: 30], that is: flowing and running. Here He says: ﴿or its water becomes sunken, so you will never be able to seek it﴾. Al-ghawr is a verbal noun with the meaning of the active participle (ghair), and it is more intensive than it, as the poet said:

"Its swift steeds keep mourning over him, / Their reins hung on them in rows..."

meaning: wailing women over him.

The Almighty says: ﴿And his fruit was encompassed (destroyed)﴾, meaning his wealth, or, according to the other view, his fruit trees. The point is that what this disbeliever had been warned about befell him. His companion had warned him that Allah would send a calamity (al-ḥusbān, a punishment sent from heaven) upon his garden, in which he took pride and which distracted him from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿So he began to wring his hands over what he had spent on it﴾. Qatadah said: he struck his palms together in regret and anguish over the wealth that had been lost to him. ﴿And he said, "Would that I had not associated anyone with my Lord."﴾ ﴿And he had no company (fi'ah) to help him﴾, meaning no clan or children, in whom he had boasted and whom he had relied upon. ﴿They could not help him against Allah, nor could he defend himself.﴾ ﴿There, protection belongs to Allah, the Truth.﴾

The reciters differ over this verse. Some stop at His words ﴿and he could not defend himself there﴾, meaning in that place where Allah's punishment has descended, so there is no one to rescue him from it, and then begin with ﴿protection belongs to Allah, the Truth﴾. Others stop at ﴿and he could not defend himself﴾ and begin with ﴿there, protection belongs to Allah, the Truth﴾.

They also differ over the reading of ﴿al-walayah (protection)﴾. Some read the waw with a fatha, so the meaning is: there, allegiance (al-muwalah) belongs to Allah. That is, there everyone, whether believer or disbeliever, returns to Allah, to allegiance to Him and submission to Him, when the punishment descends, as in His words: ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said: "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him."﴾ [Ghafir: 84], and as in His words reporting about Pharaoh: ﴿Until, when drowning overtook him, he said: "I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims." "Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters."﴾ [Yunus: 90–91].

Others read the waw with a kasra in ﴿al-walayah﴾, meaning: there, judgment belongs to Allah, the Truth.

Some read ﴿al-ḥaqq (the Truth)﴾ with a ḍamma, as an attribute of ﴿al-walayah﴾, as in His words: ﴿The dominion that Day belongs to the Most Merciful, and it will be a difficult day for the disbelievers﴾ [al-Furqan: 26].

Others read the qaf with a kasra, as an attribute of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, as in His words: ﴿Then they are returned to Allah, their true Lord. Unquestionably, judgment is His, and He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾ [al-An'am: 62]. For this reason He said: ﴿He is best in reward﴾, meaning in recompense, ﴿and best in outcome﴾, meaning the deeds done for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, whose reward is best and whose final result is praiseworthy and rightly guided. All of it is good.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 18, verses 45–46 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And present to them﴾ O Muhammad, to the people, ﴿the parable of the worldly life﴾ in its passing away, its perishing, and its ending: ﴿It is like water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it﴾, meaning what is in it of seeds, so it grows and becomes lush, and blossoms, flowers and freshness cover it. Then, after all of this, ﴿it becomes dry stubble﴾, withered, ﴿which the winds scatter﴾, meaning they disperse it and cast it to the right and to the left. ﴿And Allah is ever Able over all things﴾, meaning He is capable of this state, and of this state [in the other copy: "this state and this state"]. Allah often strikes the parable of the worldly life with this example, as in Surah Yunus: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of the worldly life is as water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, [of that which men and animals eat], until when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified﴾ [Yunus 10:24], the verse. And He said in Surah az-Zumar: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth, then brings out thereby crops of varying colours, then it dries up and you see it turn yellow, then He makes it into debris? Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding﴾ [az-Zumar 39:21]. And He said in Surah al-Hadid: ﴿Know that the worldly life is only play and amusement, adornment and boasting among you, and competition in wealth and children, like the rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers, then it dries up and you see it turn yellow, then it becomes debris. And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and forgiveness from Allah and approval. And the worldly life is not but the enjoyment of delusion﴾ [al-Hadid 57:20].

And in the authentic hadith: "The world is sweet and green" [Previously cited at the commentary on the eighth verse of this surah.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Wealth and children are the adornment of the worldly life﴾, it is like His saying: ﴿Beautified for men is the love of desires: women and children, heaped-up piles of gold and silver, branded horses, cattle and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of the worldly life, but with Allah is the finest return﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:14]. And the Exalted said: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and with Allah is a great reward﴾ [at-Taghabun 64:15], meaning: devoting oneself to Him and being free for His worship is better for you than being preoccupied with them, gathering for them, and excessive compassion toward them. Therefore He said: ﴿But the enduring good deeds are better with your Lord for reward and better for hope﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and many of the early generations (salaf, the righteous predecessors) said: "The enduring good deeds" are the five daily prayers.

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas: "The enduring good deeds" are: Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah), al-hamdu lillah (praise be to Allah), la ilaha illa Allah (there is no god but Allah), and Allahu akbar (Allah is greatest).

Likewise, the Commander of the Faithful 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about "the enduring good deeds," what are they? He said: They are: la ilaha illa Allah, Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, Allahu akbar, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah (there is no power nor strength except with Allah).

Imam Ahmad narrated it:
Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' related to us: Haywah related to us: Abu 'Aqil informed us that he heard al-Harith, the freed slave of 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, say: 'Uthman sat one day and we sat with him. The muezzin came to him, so he asked for water in a vessel, which I think would hold a mudd [a measure]. He performed ablution and then said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution as I have just done, and then he said: 'Whoever performs ablution as I have just done, then stands and prays the Zuhr prayer, will be forgiven what is between it and the Subh (dawn prayer). Then if he prays the 'Asr, he will be forgiven what is between it and the Zuhr. Then if he prays the Maghrib, he will be forgiven what is between it and the 'Asr. Then if he prays the 'Isha', he will be forgiven what is between it and the Maghrib. Then perhaps he sleeps the night rolling about, then if he gets up, performs ablution and prays the Subh prayer, he will be forgiven what is between it and the 'Isha'. And these are the good deeds that remove the bad deeds.'" They said: "These are the good deeds; so what are the enduring good deeds, O 'Uthman?" He said: "They are: la ilaha illa Allah, Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, Allahu akbar, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah." [In the copy: "billah al-'Aliyy al-'Azim" (Allah the Most High, the Mighty).] Ahmad alone narrated it. [Al-Musnad (1/71).]

Malik narrated from 'Umarah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Sayyad [in another copy: "Jiyad"], from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: "The enduring good deeds" are: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.

Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan said, from 'Umarah, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib asked me about "the enduring good deeds," and I said: "Prayer and fasting." He said: "You are not right." I said: "Zakat and Hajj." He said: "You are not right. Rather, they are the five words: la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah."

Ibn Jurayj said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khutaym informed me, from Nafi', from Sarjas, that he informed him that he asked Ibn 'Umar about: ﴿the enduring good deeds﴾. He said: la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, [Subhan Allah, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah]. Ibn Jurayj said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said the same. [Addition from the copy: Mujahid said: ﴿the enduring good deeds﴾ are Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar.]

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan and Qatadah regarding His saying: "The enduring good deeds." He said: La ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, al-hamdu lillah, Subhan Allah; they are the enduring good deeds.

Ibn Jarir said: I found in my book, from al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar, from Abu Nasr al-Tammar, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muslim, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar are among the enduring good deeds." [Tafsir al-Tabari (15/167).]

He said: And Yunus related to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed us that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Ibn al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Increase in the enduring good deeds." It was said: "And what are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The religion (al-millah)." It was said: "And what are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Takbir (Allahu akbar), tahlil (la ilaha illa Allah), tasbih (Subhan Allah), al-hamdu lillah, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah."

Thus Ahmad also narrated it, from the hadith of Darraj, with the same chain. [Tafsir al-Tabari (15/167) and al-Musnad (3/75).]

Ibn Wahb also said: Abu Sakhr informed me that 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, the freed slave of Salim ibn 'Abd Allah, narrated to him, saying: Salim sent me to Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and said: "Tell him: meet me at the corner of the graveyard, for I have a need of you." He said: So they met, and one of them greeted the other. Then Salim said: "What do you count as the enduring good deeds?" He said: "La ilaha illa Allah, Subhan Allah, Allahu akbar, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah." Salim said to him: "Since when have you included 'la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' in them?" He said: "I have always included it." He said: So he returned to him two or three times, but he did not retract. Salim said: "Indeed, Abu Ayyub al-Ansari told me that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'I was taken up to the heaven, and I was shown Ibrahim, peace be upon him. He said: "O Jibril, who is this with you?" He said: "Muhammad." So he welcomed me and greeted me warmly. Then he said: "Command your nation to plant much of the plants of Paradise, for its soil is good and its land is spacious." I said: "And what are the plants of Paradise?" He said: "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah."'" [Tafsir al-Tabari (15/166).]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Yazid related to us, from al-'Awwam, [who said]: A man from the Ansar, from the family of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, told me: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us while we were in the mosque after the 'Isha' prayer. He raised his gaze to the sky, then lowered it, until we thought something had happened in the sky. Then he said: "Indeed, after me there will be rulers who lie and oppress. Whoever believes their lies and supports them in their oppression is not of me and I am not of him. Whoever does not believe their lies and does not support them is of me and I am of him. Verily, 'Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar,' these are the enduring good deeds." [Al-Musnad (4/267).]

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Affan related to us: Aban related to us: Yahya ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd, from Abu Sallam, a freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Bakh, bakh (how excellent), five things, how heavy they are in the scale: la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, and a righteous child who dies and whose parent seeks reward for him." And he said: "Bakh, bakh, five things: whoever meets Allah being certain of them enters Paradise: he believes in Allah, the Last Day, Paradise and Hell, resurrection after death, and the reckoning." [Al-Musnad (4/237). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/88): "Its men are the men of the authentic [collections]."]

Imam Ahmad also said: Rawh related to us: al-Awza'i related to us, from Hassan ibn 'Atiyyah, who said: Shaddad ibn Aws, may Allah be pleased with him, [was on a journey,] and he stopped at a station and said to his servant: "Bring us the knife, let us play with it." I objected to this, so he said: "I have not spoken a word since I embraced Islam except that I restrain it and control it, except this word of mine. So do not hold it against me, but remember what I say to you: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'When people hoard gold and silver, then hoard these words: Allahumma inni as'aluka al-thabata fi al-amr, wa al-'azimata 'ala al-rushd, wa as'aluka shukra ni'matika, wa as'aluka husna 'ibadatika, wa as'aluka qalban salīman, wa as'aluka lisanan sadiqan, wa as'aluka min khayri ma ta'lamu, wa a'udhu bika min sharri ma ta'lamu, wa astaghfiruka lima ta'lamu, innaka anta 'allamu al-ghuyub (O Allah, I ask You for steadfastness in the matter, and resolve upon right guidance, and I ask You to thank You for Your blessing, and I ask You for excellence in worship of You, and I ask You for a sound heart, and I ask You for a truthful tongue, and I ask You for the good of what You know, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of what You know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what You know, indeed You are the Knower of the unseen)." [Al-Musnad (4/123).]

Then al-Nasa'i also narrated it from another route, from Shaddad, with similar wording. [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 1227.]

Al-Tabarani said: Abdullah ibn Najiyah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Awfi narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Umar ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Nufay' al-Jadali, from Sa'd ibn Junadah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I was among the first people from the people of al-Ta'if to come to the Prophet (ﷺ). I left my family from al-Sarah in the morning and reached Mina at the time of 'Asr. I climbed the mountain and then came down, and I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and embraced Islam. He taught me: ﴿Say, He is Allah, the One﴾ and ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾, and he taught me these words: Glory be to Allah, all praise is due to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. And he said: 'These are the enduring good deeds (al-baqiyat al-salihat).'" And with this same chain: "Whoever rises at night, performs wudu and rinses his mouth, then says: Glory be to Allah one hundred times, all praise is due to Allah one hundred times, Allah is the Greatest one hundred times, and there is no god but Allah one hundred times, his sins will be forgiven, except for blood, for it is not nullified." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/51), in which al-Husayn al-Awfi is weak.]

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿And the enduring good deeds﴾, that he said: "They are the remembrance of Allah: saying 'There is no god but Allah', 'Allah is the Greatest', 'Glory be to Allah', 'All praise is due to Allah', 'Blessed is Allah', 'There is no power and no strength except with Allah', 'I seek forgiveness from Allah', 'May Allah send blessings upon the Messenger of Allah', fasting, prayer, Hajj, charity, freeing slaves, jihad, maintaining family ties, and all good deeds. These are the enduring good deeds, which remain for their people in Paradise for as long as the heavens and the earth endure."

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: "They are good speech."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "They are all righteous deeds." Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, preferred this view.

Then, after all of this, ﴿it becomes dry stubble﴾, withered, ﴿which the winds scatter﴾, meaning they disperse it and cast it to the right and to the left. ﴿And Allah is ever Able over all things﴾, meaning He is capable of this state, and of this state [in the other copy: "this state and this state"]. Allah often strikes the parable of the worldly life with this example, as in Surah Yunus: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of the worldly life is as water which We send down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it, [of that which men and animals eat], until when the earth takes on its adornment and is beautified﴾ [Yunus 10:24], the verse. And He said in Surah az-Zumar: ﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky and makes it flow as springs in the earth, then brings out thereby crops of varying colours, then it dries up and you see it turn yellow, then He makes it into debris? Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding﴾ [az-Zumar 39:21]. And He said in Surah al-Hadid: ﴿Know that the worldly life is only play and amusement, adornment and boasting among you, and competition in wealth and children, like the rain whose vegetation pleases the disbelievers, then it dries up and you see it turn yellow, then it becomes debris. And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and forgiveness from Allah and approval. And the worldly life is not but the enjoyment of delusion﴾ [al-Hadid 57:20].

And in the authentic hadith: "The world is sweet and green" [Previously cited at the commentary on the eighth verse of this surah.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Wealth and children are the adornment of the worldly life﴾, it is like His saying: ﴿Beautified for men is the love of desires: women and children, heaped-up piles of gold and silver, branded horses, cattle and tilled land. That is the enjoyment of the worldly life, but with Allah is the finest return﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:14]. And the Exalted said: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and with Allah is a great reward﴾ [at-Taghabun 64:15], meaning: devoting oneself to Him and being free for His worship is better for you than being preoccupied with them, gathering for them, and excessive compassion toward them. Therefore He said: ﴿But the enduring good deeds are better with your Lord for reward and better for hope﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and many of the early generations (salaf, the righteous predecessors) said: "The enduring good deeds" are the five daily prayers.

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas: "The enduring good deeds" are: Subhan Allah (Glory be to Allah), al-hamdu lillah (praise be to Allah), la ilaha illa Allah (there is no god but Allah), and Allahu akbar (Allah is greatest).

Likewise, the Commander of the Faithful 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about "the enduring good deeds," what are they? He said: They are: la ilaha illa Allah, Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, Allahu akbar, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah (there is no power nor strength except with Allah).

Imam Ahmad narrated it:
Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri' related to us: Haywah related to us: Abu 'Aqil informed us that he heard al-Harith, the freed slave of 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, say: 'Uthman sat one day and we sat with him. The muezzin came to him, so he asked for water in a vessel, which I think would hold a mudd [a measure]. He performed ablution and then said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ perform ablution as I have just done, and then he said: 'Whoever performs ablution as I have just done, then stands and prays the Zuhr prayer, will be forgiven what is between it and the Subh (dawn prayer). Then if he prays the 'Asr, he will be forgiven what is between it and the Zuhr. Then if he prays the Maghrib, he will be forgiven what is between it and the 'Asr. Then if he prays the 'Isha', he will be forgiven what is between it and the Maghrib. Then perhaps he sleeps the night rolling about, then if he gets up, performs ablution and prays the Subh prayer, he will be forgiven what is between it and the 'Isha'. And these are the good deeds that remove the bad deeds.'" They said: "These are the good deeds; so what are the enduring good deeds, O 'Uthman?" He said: "They are: la ilaha illa Allah, Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, Allahu akbar, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah." [In the copy: "billah al-'Aliyy al-'Azim" (Allah the Most High, the Mighty).] Ahmad alone narrated it. [Al-Musnad (1/71).]

Malik narrated from 'Umarah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Sayyad [in another copy: "Jiyad"], from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: "The enduring good deeds" are: Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.

Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan said, from 'Umarah, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib asked me about "the enduring good deeds," and I said: "Prayer and fasting." He said: "You are not right." I said: "Zakat and Hajj." He said: "You are not right. Rather, they are the five words: la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah."

Ibn Jurayj said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khutaym informed me, from Nafi', from Sarjas, that he informed him that he asked Ibn 'Umar about: ﴿the enduring good deeds﴾. He said: la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, [Subhan Allah, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah]. Ibn Jurayj said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said the same. [Addition from the copy: Mujahid said: ﴿the enduring good deeds﴾ are Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar.]

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan and Qatadah regarding His saying: "The enduring good deeds." He said: La ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, al-hamdu lillah, Subhan Allah; they are the enduring good deeds.

Ibn Jarir said: I found in my book, from al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar, from Abu Nasr al-Tammar, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muslim, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar are among the enduring good deeds." [Tafsir al-Tabari (15/167).]

He said: And Yunus related to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed us that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Ibn al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Increase in the enduring good deeds." It was said: "And what are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The religion (al-millah)." It was said: "And what are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Takbir (Allahu akbar), tahlil (la ilaha illa Allah), tasbih (Subhan Allah), al-hamdu lillah, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah."

Thus Ahmad also narrated it, from the hadith of Darraj, with the same chain. [Tafsir al-Tabari (15/167) and al-Musnad (3/75).]

Ibn Wahb also said: Abu Sakhr informed me that 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, the freed slave of Salim ibn 'Abd Allah, narrated to him, saying: Salim sent me to Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and said: "Tell him: meet me at the corner of the graveyard, for I have a need of you." He said: So they met, and one of them greeted the other. Then Salim said: "What do you count as the enduring good deeds?" He said: "La ilaha illa Allah, Subhan Allah, Allahu akbar, and la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah." Salim said to him: "Since when have you included 'la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' in them?" He said: "I have always included it." He said: So he returned to him two or three times, but he did not retract. Salim said: "Indeed, Abu Ayyub al-Ansari told me that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'I was taken up to the heaven, and I was shown Ibrahim, peace be upon him. He said: "O Jibril, who is this with you?" He said: "Muhammad." So he welcomed me and greeted me warmly. Then he said: "Command your nation to plant much of the plants of Paradise, for its soil is good and its land is spacious." I said: "And what are the plants of Paradise?" He said: "La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah."'" [Tafsir al-Tabari (15/166).]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Yazid related to us, from al-'Awwam, [who said]: A man from the Ansar, from the family of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, told me: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us while we were in the mosque after the 'Isha' prayer. He raised his gaze to the sky, then lowered it, until we thought something had happened in the sky. Then he said: "Indeed, after me there will be rulers who lie and oppress. Whoever believes their lies and supports them in their oppression is not of me and I am not of him. Whoever does not believe their lies and does not support them is of me and I am of him. Verily, 'Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, la ilaha illa Allah, and Allahu akbar,' these are the enduring good deeds." [Al-Musnad (4/267).]

Imam Ahmad also said: 'Affan related to us: Aban related to us: Yahya ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd, from Abu Sallam, a freed slave of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Bakh, bakh (how excellent), five things, how heavy they are in the scale: la ilaha illa Allah, Allahu akbar, Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, and a righteous child who dies and whose parent seeks reward for him." And he said: "Bakh, bakh, five things: whoever meets Allah being certain of them enters Paradise: he believes in Allah, the Last Day, Paradise and Hell, resurrection after death, and the reckoning." [Al-Musnad (4/237). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/88): "Its men are the men of the authentic [collections]."]

Imam Ahmad also said: Rawh related to us: al-Awza'i related to us, from Hassan ibn 'Atiyyah, who said: Shaddad ibn Aws, may Allah be pleased with him, [was on a journey,] and he stopped at a station and said to his servant: "Bring us the knife, let us play with it." I objected to this, so he said: "I have not spoken a word since I embraced Islam except that I restrain it and control it, except this word of mine. So do not hold it against me, but remember what I say to you: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'When people hoard gold and silver, then hoard these words: Allahumma inni as'aluka al-thabata fi al-amr, wa al-'azimata 'ala al-rushd, wa as'aluka shukra ni'matika, wa as'aluka husna 'ibadatika, wa as'aluka qalban salīman, wa as'aluka lisanan sadiqan, wa as'aluka min khayri ma ta'lamu, wa a'udhu bika min sharri ma ta'lamu, wa astaghfiruka lima ta'lamu, innaka anta 'allamu al-ghuyub (O Allah, I ask You for steadfastness in the matter, and resolve upon right guidance, and I ask You to thank You for Your blessing, and I ask You for excellence in worship of You, and I ask You for a sound heart, and I ask You for a truthful tongue, and I ask You for the good of what You know, and I seek refuge in You from the evil of what You know, and I seek Your forgiveness for what You know, indeed You are the Knower of the unseen)." [Al-Musnad (4/123).]

Then al-Nasa'i also narrated it from another route, from Shaddad, with similar wording. [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 1227.]

Al-Tabarani said: Abdullah ibn Najiyah narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Awfi narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Umar ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Nufay' al-Jadali, from Sa'd ibn Junadah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I was among the first people from the people of al-Ta'if to come to the Prophet (ﷺ). I left my family from al-Sarah in the morning and reached Mina at the time of 'Asr. I climbed the mountain and then came down, and I came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and embraced Islam. He taught me: ﴿Say, He is Allah, the One﴾ and ﴿When the earth is shaken﴾, and he taught me these words: Glory be to Allah, all praise is due to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest. And he said: 'These are the enduring good deeds (al-baqiyat al-salihat).'" And with this same chain: "Whoever rises at night, performs wudu and rinses his mouth, then says: Glory be to Allah one hundred times, all praise is due to Allah one hundred times, Allah is the Greatest one hundred times, and there is no god but Allah one hundred times, his sins will be forgiven, except for blood, for it is not nullified." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (6/51), in which al-Husayn al-Awfi is weak.]

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿And the enduring good deeds﴾, that he said: "They are the remembrance of Allah: saying 'There is no god but Allah', 'Allah is the Greatest', 'Glory be to Allah', 'All praise is due to Allah', 'Blessed is Allah', 'There is no power and no strength except with Allah', 'I seek forgiveness from Allah', 'May Allah send blessings upon the Messenger of Allah', fasting, prayer, Hajj, charity, freeing slaves, jihad, maintaining family ties, and all good deeds. These are the enduring good deeds, which remain for their people in Paradise for as long as the heavens and the earth endure."

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: "They are good speech."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "They are all righteous deeds." Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, preferred this view.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Kahf, verses 47–49:

He, exalted is He, informs about the terrors of the Day of Resurrection and the great matters that will occur in it, as He says: ﴿On the day when the sky will sway violently and the mountains will move away.﴾ [al-Tur 52:9–10] That is, they will leave their places and vanish. As He says: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them fixed, while they pass like the passing of clouds.﴾ [al-Naml 27:88] He says: ﴿And the mountains will be like wool, carded.﴾ [al-Qari'ah 101:5] And He says: ﴿They ask you about the mountains. Say: My Lord will blow them away with a blowing. And He will leave them as a level plain, in which you will see no crookedness or elevation.﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:105–107]

He says: the mountains will be removed, the ground will be leveled, and the earth will remain ﴿a level plain﴾, that is, a flat surface with no crookedness in it. ﴿Nor elevation﴾, that is, no valley and no mountain. For this reason He says: ﴿And you see the earth bare﴾, that is, exposed and visible, with no landmark for anyone and no place to hide anyone. Rather, all of creation will be standing out before their Lord, and nothing about them will be hidden from Him.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: ﴿And you see the earth bare﴾ [meaning] there is no hill and no cover in it. Qatadah said: no building and no tree.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We will gather them, and We will leave out none of them﴾, that is, We will assemble them, the first and the last of them, and We will leave out none of them, neither small nor great, as He says: ﴿Say: Indeed, the former and the latter will surely be gathered for the appointed time of a known day.﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 56:49–50] And He says: ﴿That is a day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a day witnessed.﴾ [Hud 11:103]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they will be presented before your Lord in rows﴾, it may mean that all creatures will stand before Allah in one single row, as He says: ﴿On the day when the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows; none will speak except those whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is correct.﴾ [al-Naba' 78:38] It may also mean that they will stand in successive rows, as He says: ﴿And your Lord will come, and the angel in rows upon rows.﴾ [al-Fajr 89:22]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿You have come to Us just as We created you the first time﴾, this is a rebuke to those who deny the Return, and a reproach to them before the witnesses. For this reason He addresses them, saying: ﴿Rather, you claimed that We would never appoint for you a time.﴾ That is, your assumption was not that this would befall you, nor that it would happen.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the Book will be placed﴾, that is, the Book of deeds, which contains the great and the small, the fine thread and the speck, and the little and the big. ﴿So you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it﴾, that is, of their evil deeds and ugly actions. ﴿And they will say: Woe to us!﴾, that is, O our regret and our woe, for what we neglected in our lives. ﴿What is this Book that leaves nothing small or great except that it has counted it?﴾ That is, it leaves out no sin, small or great, and no deed, however small. ﴿Except that it has counted it﴾, that is, it has recorded it and preserved it.

Al-Tabarani narrated, with his chain mentioned earlier in the previous verse, from Sa'd ibn Junadah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the battle of Hunayn, we stopped in a barren part of the land where there was nothing. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Gather, let whoever finds a stick bring it, and whoever finds firewood or anything else bring it." He said: Not long passed before we made it a heap. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you see this? Likewise, sins accumulate upon one of you just as you have gathered this. So let a man fear Allah and not commit a sin, small or great, for it will be counted against him." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir 6/52]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they will find what they did present﴾, that is, of good or evil, as He says: ﴿On the day every soul will find what it did of good brought forward, and what it did of evil, it will wish that between it and that there were a great distance.﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:30] He says: ﴿On that day man will be informed of what he sent ahead and left behind.﴾ [al-Qiyamah 75:13] And He says: ﴿On the day when hidden things are exposed.﴾ [al-Tariq 86:9] That is, what is concealed and what is hidden in the hearts will be made manifest.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "For every treacherous person there will be a banner on the Day of Resurrection [by which he will be recognized]."

It is related in the two Sahihs, and in a wording: "On the Day of Resurrection, a banner will be raised for every treacherous person at his buttocks, according to the extent of his treachery. It will be said: This is the treachery of so-and-so, son of so-and-so." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3186; Sahih Muslim no. 1737]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾, that is, He judges among His servants in all their deeds, and He does not wrong any of His creation. Rather, He pardons, overlooks, and shows mercy, and He punishes whom He wills, by His power, wisdom, and justice. He fills Hell with the disbelievers and the people of sin, then He rescues the people of sin, and the disbelievers remain in it forever. He is the Judge who does not oppress and does not wrong. Allah says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:40] And He says: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged at all. And if there is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it. And sufficient are We as reckoners.﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:47] The verses on this are many.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Hammam ibn Yahya informed us, from al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Wahid al-Makki, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: A hadith reached me from a man who heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so I bought a camel and tightened my saddle upon it, and I traveled on it for a month until I reached him in Syria. There was 'Abd Allah ibn Unays. I said to the doorkeeper: Tell him: Jabir is at the door. He said: The son of 'Abd Allah? I said: Yes. So he came out dragging his garment, and he embraced me and I embraced him. I said: A hadith has reached me that you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning retaliation, and I feared that you would die or I would die before I hear it. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection, or he said: the servants, naked, uncircumcised, and unmixed." I said: What is "unmixed"? He said: "They will have nothing with them. Then He will call to them with a voice that those far away hear just as those near hear: I am the King, I am the Judge. No one of the people of the Fire should enter the Fire while he has a claim against one of the people of Paradise, until I settle it with him. And no one of the people of Paradise should enter Paradise while he has a claim against one of the people of the Fire, until I settle it with him, even a slap." He said: We said: How, when we come to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, and unmixed? He said: "By good deeds and evil deeds." [Musnad 3/495]

And from Shu'bah, from al-'Awwam ibn Muzahim, from Abu 'Uthman, from 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the hornless sheep will take retribution from the horned on the Day of Resurrection." Narrated by 'Abd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad, and it has witnesses from other routes, which we mentioned at His saying: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged at all﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:47], and at His saying: ﴿Not a creature on earth, nor a bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book. Then to their Lord they will be gathered.﴾ [al-An'am 6:38]

Allah says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom; and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:40] And He says: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged at all. And if there is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it. And sufficient are We as reckoners.﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:47] The verses on this are many.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Hammam ibn Yahya informed us, from al-Qasim ibn 'Abd al-Wahid al-Makki, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: A hadith reached me from a man who heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so I bought a camel and tightened my saddle upon it, and I traveled on it for a month until I reached him in Syria. There was 'Abd Allah ibn Unays. I said to the doorkeeper: Tell him: Jabir is at the door. He said: The son of 'Abd Allah? I said: Yes. So he came out dragging his garment, and he embraced me and I embraced him. I said: A hadith has reached me that you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning retaliation, and I feared that you would die or I would die before I hear it. He said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection, or he said: the servants, naked, uncircumcised, and unmixed." I said: What is "unmixed"? He said: "They will have nothing with them. Then He will call to them with a voice that those far away hear just as those near hear: I am the King, I am the Judge. No one of the people of the Fire should enter the Fire while he has a claim against one of the people of Paradise, until I settle it with him. And no one of the people of Paradise should enter Paradise while he has a claim against one of the people of the Fire, until I settle it with him, even a slap." He said: We said: How, when we come to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, and unmixed? He said: "By good deeds and evil deeds." [Musnad 3/495]

And from Shu'bah, from al-'Awwam ibn Muzahim, from Abu 'Uthman, from 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the hornless sheep will take retribution from the horned on the Day of Resurrection." Narrated by 'Abd Allah ibn al-Imam Ahmad, and it has witnesses from other routes, which we mentioned at His saying: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged at all﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:47], and at His saying: ﴿Not a creature on earth, nor a bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book. Then to their Lord they will be gathered.﴾ [al-An'am 6:38]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah al-Kahf, verses 47–49:

He, exalted is He, informs about the terrors of the Day of Resurrection and the great matters that will occur in it, as He says: ﴿On the day when the sky will sway violently and the mountains will move away.﴾ [al-Tur 52:9–10] That is, they will leave their places and vanish. As He says: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them fixed, while they pass like the passing of clouds.﴾ [al-Naml 27:88] He says: ﴿And the mountains will be like wool, carded.﴾ [al-Qari'ah 101:5] And He says: ﴿They ask you about the mountains. Say: My Lord will blow them away with a blowing. And He will leave them as a level plain, in which you will see no crookedness or elevation.﴾ [Ta-Ha 20:105–107]

He says: the mountains will be removed, the ground will be leveled, and the earth will remain ﴿a level plain﴾, that is, a flat surface with no crookedness in it. ﴿Nor elevation﴾, that is, no valley and no mountain. For this reason He says: ﴿And you see the earth bare﴾, that is, exposed and visible, with no landmark for anyone and no place to hide anyone. Rather, all of creation will be standing out before their Lord, and nothing about them will be hidden from Him.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: ﴿And you see the earth bare﴾ [meaning] there is no hill and no cover in it. Qatadah said: no building and no tree.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We will gather them, and We will leave out none of them﴾, that is, We will assemble them, the first and the last of them, and We will leave out none of them, neither small nor great, as He says: ﴿Say: Indeed, the former and the latter will surely be gathered for the appointed time of a known day.﴾ [al-Waqi'ah 56:49–50] And He says: ﴿That is a day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a day witnessed.﴾ [Hud 11:103]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they will be presented before your Lord in rows﴾, it may mean that all creatures will stand before Allah in one single row, as He says: ﴿On the day when the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows; none will speak except those whom the Most Merciful permits, and he will say what is correct.﴾ [al-Naba' 78:38] It may also mean that they will stand in successive rows, as He says: ﴿And your Lord will come, and the angel in rows upon rows.﴾ [al-Fajr 89:22]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿You have come to Us just as We created you the first time﴾, this is a rebuke to those who deny the Return, and a reproach to them before the witnesses. For this reason He addresses them, saying: ﴿Rather, you claimed that We would never appoint for you a time.﴾ That is, your assumption was not that this would befall you, nor that it would happen.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the Book will be placed﴾, that is, the Book of deeds, which contains the great and the small, the fine thread and the speck, and the little and the big. ﴿So you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it﴾, that is, of their evil deeds and ugly actions. ﴿And they will say: Woe to us!﴾, that is, O our regret and our woe, for what we neglected in our lives. ﴿What is this Book that leaves nothing small or great except that it has counted it?﴾ That is, it leaves out no sin, small or great, and no deed, however small. ﴿Except that it has counted it﴾, that is, it has recorded it and preserved it.

Al-Tabarani narrated, with his chain mentioned earlier in the previous verse, from Sa'd ibn Junadah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the battle of Hunayn, we stopped in a barren part of the land where there was nothing. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Gather, let whoever finds a stick bring it, and whoever finds firewood or anything else bring it." He said: Not long passed before we made it a heap. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do you see this? Likewise, sins accumulate upon one of you just as you have gathered this. So let a man fear Allah and not commit a sin, small or great, for it will be counted against him." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir 6/52]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they will find what they did present﴾, that is, of good or evil, as He says: ﴿On the day every soul will find what it did of good brought forward, and what it did of evil, it will wish that between it and that there were a great distance.﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:30] He says: ﴿On that day man will be informed of what he sent ahead and left behind.﴾ [al-Qiyamah 75:13] And He says: ﴿On the day when hidden things are exposed.﴾ [al-Tariq 86:9] That is, what is concealed and what is hidden in the hearts will be made manifest.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "For every treacherous person there will be a banner on the Day of Resurrection [by which he will be recognized]."

It is related in the two Sahihs, and in a wording: "On the Day of Resurrection, a banner will be raised for every treacherous person at his buttocks, according to the extent of his treachery. It will be said: This is the treachery of so-and-so, son of so-and-so." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3186; Sahih Muslim no. 1737]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾, that is, He judges among His servants in all their deeds, and He does not wrong any of His creation. Rather, He pardons, overlooks, and shows mercy, and He punishes whom He wills, by His power, wisdom, and justice. **Ibn Kathir's commentary (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 18, verse 50:**

He, exalted is He, says, warning the children of Adam about the enmity of Iblis toward them and toward their father before them, and rebuking those among them who followed him, opposed their Creator and Master, who brought them into being and originated them, and who provided for them and nourished them with His kindnesses. Then, after all this, he allied himself with Iblis and became hostile to Allah. So He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And when We said to the angels﴾, meaning all the angels, as was explained earlier at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah [[On the commentary of verse 34.]].

﴿Prostrate to Adam﴾, meaning a prostration of honour, reverence and glorification, as He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay from black mud altered. So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul, then fall down to him in prostration."﴾ [al-Hijr 15:28-29].

As for His saying ﴿So they prostrated, except Iblis; he was of the jinn﴾, meaning his origin betrayed him. He was created from a smokeless fire (marij min nar), whereas the origin of the creation of the angels is light. It is established in Sahih Muslim, from 'A'ishah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "The angels were created from light, Iblis was created from smokeless fire, and Adam was created from what has been described to you" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2996).]]. When the time of need comes, every vessel releases what is in it, and his nature betrayed him at the time of need. That is because he had adopted the characteristics of the angels and imitated them, and he worshipped and devoted himself to asceticism. For this reason he was included in their address, but he disobeyed by opposing it.

Here He, exalted is He, points out that he was ﴿of the jinn﴾, meaning that he was created from fire, as He says: ﴿"I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾ [al-A'raf 7:12; Sad 38:76].

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Iblis was never one of the angels for even the blink of an eye. He was the origin of the jinn, just as Adam, peace be upon him, was the origin of mankind." Narrated by Ibn Jarir with a sahih chain [from him] [[Addition from F, A.]] [[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/170).]].

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Iblis was from one of the living groups of the angels, called the jinn, who were created from the scorching fire of samum among the angels." He said: "His name was al-Harith, and he was one of the guardians of Paradise. The angels were created from light, other than this group." He said: "And the jinn mentioned in the Qur'an were created from a smokeless fire (marij min nar), which is the tongue of fire that appears at its edge when it blazes."

Al-Dahhak also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Iblis was one of the most noble of the angels and the most honourable of them in lineage. He was a guardian over the gardens, and he had authority over the lowest heaven and over the earth. Among the things his self beguiled him with, by Allah's decree, was that he saw that this gave him a distinction over the people of heaven. So pride entered his heart, a pride that none knows but Allah. Allah brought out that pride from him when He commanded him to prostrate to Adam, so he became arrogant and was among the disbelievers." Ibn 'Abbas said: "His saying ﴿he was of the jinn﴾ means: of the guardians of [the gardens], just as a man is called Makki, Madani, Basri or Kufi." Ibn Jurayj narrated similarly from Ibn 'Abbas.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "He was one of the guardians of Paradise, and he used to manage the affairs of the lowest heaven." Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id, with the same wording.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "He was the chief of the angels of the lowest heaven."

Ibn Ishaq narrated, from Khalad ibn 'Ata', from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Iblis, before he committed disobedience, was among the angels. His name was 'Azazil, and he was one of the inhabitants of the earth. He was among the most diligent of the angels in worship and the most knowledgeable of them. This is what led him to pride, and he was from a group called jinn."

Ibn Jurayj narrated, from Salih, mawla of al-Tawama, and Sharik ibn Abi Namir, one or both of them, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Among the angels is a tribe of jinn, and Iblis was from them. He used to govern what was between heaven and earth. He disobeyed, so Allah became angry with him, and He transformed him into a rejected devil, cursed by Allah, transformed [in form]." He said: "When a man's sin comes from pride, do not hope for him; when his sin comes from disobedience, hope for him."

It is also narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he said: "He was one of the jannanin (gardeners/guardians of gardens), who worked in Paradise."

Many reports have been narrated on this matter from the early generation (al-salaf), most of which are from the Isra'iliyyat (narratives transmitted from Jewish and Christian sources) that are related so that they may be examined, and Allah knows best the status of many of them. Some of them can be definitively judged to be false because they contradict the truth that is in our hands. The Qur'an is sufficient in place of everything else of the earlier reports, because they are hardly free from alteration, addition and omission. Many things have been fabricated in them, and they have no reliable, exacting custodians of narrations who can remove from them the distortion of extremists and the false claims of the falsifiers, as this Ummah has in its imams and scholars, its pious masters, righteous and noble people, and its discerning critics and sound memorizers, who recorded the hadith, verified it, and distinguished its sahih from its hasan, its da'if, its munkar, its mawdu', its matruk and its makdhub. They knew the fabricators, the liars and the unknown narrators, and the other categories of narrators. All of this was to safeguard the Prophetic threshold and the Muhammadan station, the seal of the Messengers and the master of mankind [upon him be the best of blessings, prayers and greetings] [[Addition from A.]], so that no lie would be attributed to him, and nothing would be related from him that did not come from him [[Addition from F.]]. May Allah be pleased with them, make them content, and make the gardens of Firdaws their abode. And He has done so.

* *

As for His saying ﴿So he defied the command of his Lord﴾, meaning he departed from obedience to Allah, for fisq (defiance) is departure. It is said: "The date (ruṭab) defied (fasaqat) when it came out of its sheaths," and "The mouse defied (fasaqat) from its hole when it came out of it to cause corruption and mischief."

Then He, exalted is He, says, rebuking and reproaching those who followed and obeyed him: ﴿Then do you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me?﴾, meaning as substitutes for Me. For this reason He said: ﴿Wretched is it as a substitute for the wrongdoers.﴾

This situation is like His saying, after mentioning the Day of Resurrection, its terrors, and the destinations of each of the two groups, the blessed and the wretched, in Surah Ya-Sin: ﴿"And stand apart today, you criminals. Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. And that you worship Me; this is a straight path. And he had already led astray from among you a great throng. Did you not then use reason?"﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:59-62].

Ibn Kathir said: Allah the Exalted says: "Those whom you have taken as protectors besides Me are servants like you. They possess nothing, and I did not make them witnesses to the creation of the heavens [[In manuscripts F and A: "khalq al-samawat".]] and the earth, nor were they present at that time." Allah the Exalted says: I alone am the One who independently creates all things, and who alone manages and decrees them. There is no partner with Me in that, no minister, no counselor, and no equal.

As He said: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claimed besides Allah. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, nor do they have any share in them, nor does He have among them any helper. And intercession with Him does not benefit except for one whom He has permitted﴾ [Saba' 34:22–23]. For this reason He said: ﴿And I would not take the misleaders as helpers﴾. Mālik said: "Helpers."

Allah the Exalted says, informing of what He will say to the polytheists on the Day of Resurrection, before all the witnesses, as a rebuke and reproach to them: ﴿Call upon My partners whom you used to claim﴾. That is, in the abode of this world. ﴿Call upon them today, and they will rescue you from what you are in,﴾ as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time, and you have left behind what We bestowed upon you. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed to be partners [with Allah]. The bonds between you have been severed, and what you used to claim has departed from you﴾ [al-An'am 6:94].

* *

And His saying: ﴿So they called upon them, but they did not respond to them﴾. As He said: ﴿And it will be said, "Call upon your partners," so they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them. And they will see the punishment. If only they had been guided!﴾ [al-Qasas 28:64]. And He said: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, while they are unaware of their supplication? And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [al-Ahqaf 46:5-6]. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they have taken gods other than Allah that they might be for them a source of honor. No! They will deny their worship of them and will become opponents to them﴾ [Maryam 19:81-82].

* *

And His saying: ﴿And We made between them a mawbiq﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and others said: a place of destruction (mahlik).

Qatadah said: It has been mentioned to us that 'Amr al-Bakali narrated from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: It is a deep valley, by which, on the Day of Resurrection, the people of guidance are separated from the people of misguidance.

Qatadah said: ﴿Mawbiq﴾ is a valley in Hell.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Yazid ibn Dirham narrated to us, I heard Anas ibn Malik say, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We made between them a mawbiq﴾: He said: It is a valley in Hell, of pus and blood.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿Mawbiq﴾: enmity.

The apparent meaning from the context here is that it is the place of destruction. It may also be a valley in Hell or something else. However, Allah the Exalted informed that there is no way for these polytheists, nor any access for them, to their gods whom they claimed in the world, and that He separates them from those gods in the Hereafter, so there is no escape for either group to the other. Rather, between them is a place of destruction, a great terror and a grave matter.

As for if the pronoun in His saying ﴿between them﴾ is taken to refer to the believers and the disbelievers, as 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said, that He separates between the people of guidance and the people of misguidance by it, then it is like His saying: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, that Day they will be separated﴾ [al-Rum 30:14], and He said: ﴿That Day they will be split apart﴾ [al-Rum 30:43], and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And separate yourselves today, O criminals﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:59], and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the Day We gather them all, then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, "Stay in your place, you and your partners." Then We will separate them, and their partners will say, "You did not used to worship us. And sufficient is Allah as a witness between us and you; we were certainly unaware of your worship." There every soul will know what it has put forth, and they will be returned to Allah, their true Master, and what they used to fabricate will have departed from them﴾ [Yunus 10:28-30].

* *

And His saying: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are to fall therein, and they will not find from it any escape﴾. That is: when they witness Hell, which will be brought forth, led by seventy thousand bridles, with each bridle held by seventy thousand angels, when the criminals see the Fire, they will be certain beyond doubt that they are to fall into it. This is by way of hastening grief and sorrow upon them, for the anticipation of punishment and fear of it before it occurs is itself an immediate punishment.

﴿And they will not find from it any escape﴾: that is, there is no path for them that turns them away from it, and they must enter it.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed the disbeliever sees Hell, and he thinks that it is about to fall upon him from a distance of forty years."

[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/173). Darraj from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The disbeliever will be made to stand for a period equal to fifty thousand years, though he did no work in the world. And indeed the disbeliever sees Hell, and thinks that it is about to fall upon him from a distance of forty years."

[Al-Musnad (3/75).]

However, Allah the Exalted informed that there is no way for these polytheists, nor any access for them, to their gods whom they claimed in the world, and that He separates them from those gods in the Hereafter, so there is no escape for either group to the other. Rather, between them is a place of destruction, a great terror and a grave matter.

As for if the pronoun in His saying ﴿between them﴾ is taken to refer to the believers and the disbelievers, as 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr said, that He separates between the people of guidance and the people of misguidance by it, then it is like His saying: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, that Day they will be separated﴾ [al-Rum 30:14], and He said: ﴿That Day they will be split apart﴾ [al-Rum 30:43], and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And separate yourselves today, O criminals﴾ [Ya-Sin 36:59], and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the Day We gather them all, then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, "Stay in your place, you and your partners." Then We will separate them, and their partners will say, "You did not used to worship us. And sufficient is Allah as a witness between us and you; we were certainly unaware of your worship." There every soul will know what it has put forth, and they will be returned to Allah, their true Master, and what they used to fabricate will have departed from them﴾ [Yunus 10:28-30].

* *

And His saying: ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are to fall therein, and they will not find from it any escape﴾. That is: when they witness Hell, which will be brought forth, led by seventy thousand bridles, with each bridle held by seventy thousand angels, when the criminals see the Fire, they will be certain beyond doubt that they are to fall into it. This is by way of hastening grief and sorrow upon them, for the anticipation of punishment and fear of it before it occurs is itself an immediate punishment.

﴿And they will not find from it any escape﴾: that is, there is no path for them that turns them away from it, and they must enter it.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed the disbeliever sees Hell, and he thinks that it is about to fall upon him from a distance of forty years."

[Tafsir al-Tabari (15/173). Darraj from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The disbeliever will be made to stand for a period equal to fifty thousand years, though he did no work in the world. And indeed the disbeliever sees Hell, and thinks that it is about to fall upon him from a distance of forty years."

[Al-Musnad (3/75).]

God the Exalted says: "And We have certainly explained to the people in this Qur'an, and clarified the matters for them, and detailed them, so that they would not go astray from the truth and depart from the path of guidance. Yet despite this clarification and this criterion, man is very much given to disputation, contention, and opposing the truth with falsehood, except those whom Allah guides and gives insight to the path of salvation."

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn informed me that Husayn ibn Ali informed him that Ali ibn Abi Talib informed him that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to him and Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), one night, and said: "Will you not pray?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, our souls are in the hand of Allah; if He wills to raise us, He will raise us." So he turned away when I said that, and did not respond to me with anything. Then I heard him as he was leaving, striking his thigh and saying: ﴿But man is ever most of anything given to disputation﴾. Both al-Bukhari and Muslim recorded it in their Sahihs.

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 18, verses 55–56:

Allah informs us about the rebelliousness of the disbelievers, in ancient times and in later times, and about their denial of the clear and manifest truth, despite the signs and the evident proofs that they witnessed. He states that what prevented them from following that truth was nothing but their demand to see the punishment with which they had been threatened, face to face (ʿayānan), just as those people said to their prophet: ﴿So drop upon us fragments from the sky, if you are of the truthful﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:187]. Others said: ﴿Bring us the punishment of Allah, if you are of the truthful﴾ [al-'Ankabut 29:29]. Quraysh said: ﴿O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾ [al-Anfal 8:32]. And: ﴿They said, "O you to whom the Reminder has been revealed, indeed you are mad. Why do you not bring us the angels, if you are of the truthful?"﴾ [al-Hijr 15:6–7], and beyond that from the verses that indicate this.

Then He said: ﴿Except that the way of the former peoples should come upon them﴾, meaning their being overtaken by the punishment and their being seized entirely, ﴿or the punishment should come to them face to face﴾, meaning they see it directly and in confrontation. Then He said: ﴿We send the messengers only as bringers of good news and warners. And those who disbelieve dispute by falsehood in order to refute thereby the truth, and they take My signs and what they are warned of in mockery﴾, meaning: before the punishment, as bringers of good news to whoever believes them and affirms them, and as warners to whoever denies them and opposes them.

Then He informed about the disbelievers, that they dispute with falsehood ﴿in order to refute thereby﴾, meaning to weaken thereby ﴿the truth﴾ which the messengers brought, and that this will not be accomplished for them. ﴿And they take My signs and what they were warned of in mockery﴾, meaning they took the proofs, the arguments, and the extraordinary events with which the messengers were sent, and the threats of punishment with which the messengers warned and frightened them, as objects of ﴿mockery﴾, meaning they ridiculed them in that regard, and this is the most severe form of denial.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 18, verses 57–59:

Allah, exalted is He, says: And who is more unjust than one who is reminded of the signs of his Lord (ʾāyāt Allāh) and turns away from them? That is, he forgets them, turns away from them, does not give ear to them, and pays them no attention. ﴿And forgets what his hands have sent forward﴾, that is, of the evil deeds and foul actions. ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings﴾, that is, over the hearts of these people, ﴿lest they understand it﴾, that is, lest they comprehend this Qur'an and its clarity, ﴿and in their ears deafness﴾, that is, a figurative deafness to guidance. ﴿And even if you call them to guidance, they will never be guided, ever﴾.

And His saying: ﴿And your Lord is the Forgiving, the Possessor of mercy﴾, that is, your Lord, O Muhammad, is Forgiving, possessor of vast mercy, ﴿If He were to seize them for what they have earned, He would have hastened for them the punishment﴾. As He said: ﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for what they have earned, He would not leave upon the earth a creature moving [on it]﴾ [Fatir: 45], and He said: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing, and indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty﴾ [al-Ra'd: 6]. And the verses on this are many.

Then He informed that He is forbearing, concealing and forgiving, and perhaps He guides some of them from error to right guidance. And whoever among them persists, for him is a Day in which the youth will turn white-haired and every pregnant woman will lay down her burden. Therefore He said: ﴿Rather, for them is an appointed time from which they will find no refuge (mawʾil) other than it﴾, that is, they have no escape (mahīd), no way out (maḥīṣ), and no alternative (maʿdil) from it.

And His saying: ﴿And those cities — We destroyed them when they wronged﴾, that is, the past nations and the bygone generations: We destroyed them because of their disbelief and obstinacy. ﴿And We made for their destruction an appointed time﴾, that is, We set it for a known duration and a specified time, neither increasing nor decreasing. That is, likewise you, O polytheists, beware lest there befall you what befell them, for you have denied the most noble Messenger and the greatest Prophet (ﷺ), and you are not more honored by Us than they were. So fear My punishment and warnings.

That is, likewise you, O polytheists, beware lest there befall you what befell them, for you have denied the most noble Messenger and the greatest Prophet (ﷺ), and you are not more honored by Us than they were. So fear My punishment and warnings.

The cause of Musa's [peace be upon him] [[Addition from MS F, A.]] saying this statement to his young man, Yusha' ibn Nun, was that he was told that a servant of Allah's servants at the Meeting Place of the Two Seas had knowledge that Musa did not comprehend, so he wished to go to him. He said to his young man: ﴿I will not stop until I reach the meeting place of the two seas﴾, meaning, I will not cease travelling until I reach this place where the two seas meet. Al-Farazdaq said: "They did not cease until their women swayed / in the open ground of Dhi Qar, perfume-bags laden." [[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (15/176).]]

Qatadah and others said: the two seas are the Sea of Persia on the east side, and the Sea of Rome on the west side.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: the meeting place of the two seas is at Tangier, meaning at the farthest region of the Maghrib. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿or I will journey for a long period﴾, meaning: even if I travel for a long period of time.

Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari], may Allah have mercy on him, said: some scholars of the Arabic language mentioned that *huquban* in the dialect of Qays [[In F, A: "the Arabs".]] means a year. It was also narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr that he said: *huquban* is eighty years. Mujahid said: seventy autumns. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿or I will journey for a long period﴾ that he said: an age. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said the same.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So when they reached the meeting place between them, they forgot their fish﴾, the reason was that he had been commanded to take a salted fish with him, and it was said to him: wherever you lose the fish, that is where [the one you seek] is. So they travelled until they reached the meeting place of the two seas. There was a spring there called "the Spring of Life," so they slept there. Some of the water spray from that spring reached the fish, and it began to stir, and it leapt out of the basket into the sea. Yusha' [peace be upon him] woke up, and the fish fell into the sea and began to move through it, while the water stood over it like an arch that did not close again behind it. This is why He said: ﴿and it took its way into the sea, a tunnel﴾, meaning, like a tunnel in the earth.

Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: its track remained like a stone.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: the fish did not touch any part of the sea without it drying up until it became a rock.

Muhammad [i.e. Muhammad] ibn Ishaq said, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah, from Ibn Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, when he related the account of that: "No water has parted since people existed except this water, which stood still in the place of the fish, and it parted like a window until Musa returned to it and saw its path." Then [Musa] said: ﴿That is what we were seeking﴾.

Qatadah said: a tunnel from the land, until it reached the sea; then it entered it, and whatever path it took in it became solid water.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then when they had passed on﴾, meaning, past the place where they had forgotten the fish. The forgetting is attributed to both of them, although it was Yusha' who forgot it, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿From them come forth pearls and coral﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 22], whereas they come forth only from the salt water, according to one of the two opinions.

When they had gone on from the place where they had forgotten it a stage, ﴿Musa said﴾ to ﴿his young man: Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed suffered fatigue from this journey of ours﴾ [i.e. the part of the journey] where they had passed beyond the place, ﴿fatigue﴾, meaning, weariness. He said: ﴿Do you see? When we took refuge at the rock, I forgot the fish—and none but Satan made me forget to mention it﴾. Qatadah said: Ibn Mas'ud recited: "and none but Satan made me forget it, that I should mention it." This is why He said: ﴿and it took its way into the sea in a marvellous manner﴾, meaning, its path. ﴿He said: That is what we were seeking﴾, meaning, this is what we were looking for. ﴿So they went back, retracing their footsteps﴾, meaning, they returned ﴿along their track﴾, meaning, their path, ﴿retracing﴾, meaning, following their own footprints and tracing their trail.

﴿Then they found a servant of Our servants, whom We had given mercy from Us and taught knowledge from Us﴾. This is al-Khidr [peace be upon him], as indicated by the authentic hadiths from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Bukhari said regarding this:

Al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Amr ibn Dinar narrated to us, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr informed me that he said: I said to Ibn Abbas: Nawf al-Bakali claims that Musa, the companion of al-Khidr, is not Musa the companion of the Children of Israel. Ibn Abbas said: The enemy of Allah lied. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Musa stood up to address the Children of Israel, and he was asked: Who is the most knowledgeable of people? He said: I am. Allah reproached him because he did not attribute knowledge to Him. So Allah revealed to him: Indeed, I have a servant at the meeting place of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you. Musa said: O Lord, how can I reach him? He said: Take a fish with you in a basket, and wherever you lose the fish, he is there. So he took a fish and put it in a basket, then set out, and his young man Yusha' ibn Nun, peace be upon them both, went with him, until when they came to the rock, they laid down their heads and slept. The fish stirred in the basket, came out of it, fell into the sea and took its path into the sea as a tunnel, and Allah withheld the flow of the water from the fish, so it became over it like an arch. When [Musa] awoke, his companion forgot to inform him about the fish, so they continued for the rest of their day and night. When it was the next day, Musa said to his young man: ﴿Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed suffered fatigue from this journey of ours﴾, and Musa did not feel the fatigue until they had passed the place Allah had commanded him to reach. His young man said to him: ﴿Do you see? When we took refuge at the rock, I forgot the fish—and none but Satan made me forget to mention it, and it took its way into the sea in a marvellous manner﴾." He said: "So it was a tunnel for the fish, and a marvel for Musa and his young man." He [Musa] said: ﴿That is what we were seeking﴾, so they went back, retracing their footsteps. He said: "They returned, tracing their trail, until they reached the rock, and there was a man covered with a garment. Musa greeted him, and al-Khidr said: And how is there greeting in your land? He said: I am Musa. He said: Musa of the Children of Israel? He said: Yes, I have come to you that you may teach me of what you have been taught of right guidance. ﴿He said: Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me﴾, O Musa, I have a knowledge from Allah's knowledge which He taught me, which you do not know; and you have a knowledge from Allah's knowledge which Allah taught you, which I do not know." Musa said: ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter﴾. Al-Khidr said to him: ﴿If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you﴾."

They went on walking along the seashore. A ship passed by, and they asked the people to carry them, and they recognised al-Khidr, so they carried them without a fare. When they boarded the ship, suddenly al-Khidr had pulled out a plank from the ship's planks with an axe. Musa said to him: "They carried us without a fare, and you purposely went to their ship and damaged it in order to drown its people? You have indeed done a grievous thing." ﴿He said: Did I not say that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾ * ﴿He said: Do not hold me to account for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair﴾ [[In F, A: "I did say to you", which is an error.]] He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first [objection] from Musa was forgetfulness." He said: A sparrow came and alighted on the edge of the ship and pecked once or twice in the sea [[Addition from MS A.]].
