Al-Khidr said to him: "My knowledge and your knowledge, in the knowledge of Allah, are no more than what this sparrow has taken from this sea."

Then they got out of the ship, and while they were walking along the shore, al-Khidr saw a boy playing with other boys. Al-Khidr took his head [with his hand] [[Addition from MSS F, A.]] and pulled it off with his hand and killed him. Musa said to him: ﴿Have you killed a pure soul, not in retaliation for another soul? You have indeed done a dreadful thing﴾ ﴿He said: Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾?! [[In F, A: "pure".]] He said: "This is worse than the first," ﴿He said: If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep me company; you have already received an excuse from me﴾. * [[In F: "you have reached from me" which is an error.]] So they went on until, when they came to the people of a town and asked its people for food, they refused to host them. They found in it a wall about to collapse [[In T: "collapsing, so he set it up".]] ﴿—He said: leaning. Al-Khidr with his hand: "So he set it up"﴾. Musa said: "A people we came to, and they did not feed us or host us, ﴿If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it﴾." ﴿He said: This is the parting between me and you; I will inform you of the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "We wished that Musa had been patient until Allah told us more of their story."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn Abbas used to recite: "And there was a king behind them who seized every good ship by force," and he used to recite: "As for the boy, he was a disbeliever, and his parents were believers" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4725.]].

Then al-Bukhari narrated it from Qutaybah, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah ... and he mentioned something similar, and in it: "Musa went out with his young man Yusha' ibn Nun, and with them the fish, until they reached the rock, and they alighted beside it. He said: Musa laid his head down and slept. Sufyan said: and in a narration other than that of Amr, he said: At the base of the rock there is a spring called al-Hayat [Life], none of whose water touches anything without it being brought to life. So the fish was touched by the water of that spring; he said: it moved and slipped out of the basket and entered the sea. When [Musa] awoke, Musa said to his young man: ﴿Bring us our morning meal﴾." Thus he said, and he related the hadith [continuing]. "A sparrow alighted on the edge of the ship and dipped its beak in the sea, and al-Khidr said to Musa: My knowledge and your knowledge and the knowledge of all creatures, in the knowledge of Allah, is no more than the amount this sparrow has dipped its beak into [the sea]." He mentioned its full text in similar terms [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4727.]].

Al-Bukhari also said: Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to us, that Ibn Jurayj informed them, saying: Ya'la ibn Muslim and 'Amr ibn Dinar informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr (one of them adds to the other), and others besides them, whom I heard narrating from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "We were with Ibn 'Abbas in his house when he said: 'Ask me.' I said: 'O Abu 'Abbas, may Allah make me your ransom, in Kufa there is a storyteller called Nawf, who claims that he is not Musa of the Children of Israel.' As for 'Amr, he said to me: 'The enemy of Allah has lied!' As for Ya'la, he said to me: 'Ibn 'Abbas said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b narrated to me, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Musa, the Messenger of Allah, once reminded the people, until the eyes overflowed with tears and the hearts softened. He turned to leave, and a man caught up with him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you?' He said: 'No.' So Allah rebuked him, because he had not referred the knowledge to Allah. It was said to him: 'Yes.' He said: 'O Lord, where is he?' It was said: 'At the meeting place of the two seas.' He said: 'O Lord, give me a sign by which I may know it.'"'" 'Amr said to me: "He said: 'Where the fish leaves you.'" And Ya'la said to me: "Take a dead fish, and where life is breathed into it, that is the place." So he took a fish and placed it in a basket, and he said to his servant: "I will not burden you except that you tell me where the fish leaves you." He said: "You have not burdened me greatly." This is His saying: ﴿And when Musa said to his servant﴾, namely Yusha' ibn Nun, which is not in the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr. He said: "While he was in the shade of a rock in a place of moisture, the fish moved while Musa was sleeping. His servant said: 'I will not wake him.' When he awoke, he forgot to tell him. The fish leapt until it entered the sea, and Allah stopped the flow of water from it, so that its trace was like a trace on a stone." [He said: 'Amr said to me: "Like this, its trace was as if on a stone,"] and he made a circle with his thumb and the finger next to it. ﴿Indeed we have suffered much fatigue from this journey of ours﴾. He said: "Allah has removed the fatigue from you." (This is not in the narration of Sa'id.) He informed him, and they returned and found a Khidr. He said: 'Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman said: "On a green carpet on the bank of the sea." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "He was covered with a garment, having placed one end under his feet and the other end under his head. Musa greeted him, and he uncovered his face and said: 'Is there peace on this earth? Who are you?' He said: 'I am Musa.' He said: 'Musa of the Children of Israel?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'What is your matter?' He said: 'I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught, as right guidance.' He said: 'Is the Torah not sufficient for you in your hand, and that revelation comes to you? O Musa, I have knowledge that it is not fitting for you to know, and you have knowledge that it is not fitting for me to know.' Then a bird took with its beak from the sea [and said: 'By Allah, my knowledge and your knowledge, in comparison with the knowledge of Allah, are no more than what this bird has taken with its beak from the sea'], until they boarded the ship and found small ferries carrying the people of this shore to the other shore. They recognised him and said: 'The righteous servant of Allah?' He said: 'We said to Sa'id: Khidr?' He said: 'Yes. We will not carry him for a fee.' Then he tore the ship and drove a peg into it." Musa said: ﴿Have you torn it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing﴾. Mujahid said: "Munkaran (a grave matter)." He said: ﴿Did I not say that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾ The first was forgetfulness, the middle was a condition, and the third was deliberate. ﴿He said: Do not take me to task for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair.﴾ ﴿So they set out﴾, until they met a boy and he killed him. Ya'la said: Sa'id said: "He found boys playing, and he seized a disbelieving, handsome boy, laid him down, then slaughtered him with a knife." He said: ﴿Have you killed an innocent soul?﴾ (who had not done wrong). Ibn 'Abbas read it as ﴿zakiyyatan﴾ ("zakiyya" meaning Muslim), like your saying: "a pure boy (ghulaman zakiyyan)." ﴿So they set out, until they found a wall about to collapse, and he set it upright.﴾ Sa'id said with his hand like this, and raised his hand, and it stood straight. Ya'la said: "I think Sa'id said: 'He wiped it with his hand and it stood straight.'" He said: ﴿If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it.﴾ Sa'id said: "A wage we could eat." ﴿And there was behind them a king﴾, and it was "in front of them." Ibn 'Abbas read it: "Amamahum malik" (in front of them a king). They claim, apart from Sa'id, that he was Hudad ibn Budad, and the boy who was killed, his name, they claim, was Jaysur. ﴿A king who seizes every ship by force﴾. So I wished, when it passed by him, that he would leave it because of its defect, and when they passed him they would repair it and benefit from it. Some of them say: they sealed it with a bottle, and some say: with pitch. ﴿As for the boy, his parents were believers﴾, while he was a disbeliever. ﴿We feared that he would burden them with transgression and disbelief﴾: that his love for him would lead them to follow him in his religion. ﴿So we wished that their Lord would give them in exchange one better than him in purity and nearer in compassion﴾, like His saying: ﴿Have you killed an innocent soul?﴾ and ﴿nearer in compassion﴾: they were more merciful to that one than to the first whom Khidr killed. Other than Sa'id ibn Jubayr claimed that they were given in exchange a girl. As for Dawud ibn Abi 'Asim, he said, from more than one: it was a girl.

Al-Bukhari, hadith no. (4726).

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Musa, peace be upon him, addressed the Children of Israel and said: "No one is more knowledgeable of Allah and His command than I am." So he was commanded to meet this man. He then mentioned something similar to what has preceded, with some addition and omission. (Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq, 1/341, 342.) And Allah knows best.

And Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from al-Hasan ibn 'Umarah, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah[[In F and A: "'Uyaynah".]], from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I sat with Ibn 'Abbas, and with him was a group of People of the Book. Some of them said: "O Abu al-'Abbas, Nawf, the son of Ka'b's wife, claims on Ka'b's authority that Musa the prophet who sought the knowledge is only Musa ibn Mitha." Sa'id said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Does Nawf say this?" Sa'id said: I replied: "Yes, I heard Nawf say that." He said: "Did you hear it yourself, O Sa'id?" He said: I said: "Yes." He said: "Nawf has lied." Then Ibn 'Abbas said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b narrated to me, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Musa, the one of the Children of Israel, asked his Lord and said: 'O Lord, if there is anyone among Your servants who is more knowledgeable than me, guide me to him.' He said to him: 'Yes, among My servants there is one who is more knowledgeable than you.' Then He described his place to him and permitted him to meet him. So Musa set out, and with him was his young servant, and with him was a fish, salted[[Mulayh: a fish that has been salted or preserved.]]. It had been said to him: 'When this fish comes back to life in a place, your companion is there, and you will have attained your need.' So Musa set out, and with him was his young servant, and with him was that fish, and they carried it. He traveled until the journey exhausted him, and he reached the rock and that water, and that water was the water of life; whoever drinks from it becomes immortal, and nothing dead comes near it without coming back to life. When they dismounted and the fish touched the water, it came back to life, ﴿and it took its way into the sea, making a tunnel﴾. Then they set off, and when he had passed the place where they had stopped, Musa said to his young servant: ﴿Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed suffered fatigue from this journey of ours.﴾ The young man said, and he mentioned: ﴿Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none caused me to forget it except Satan, that I should mention it. And it took its way into the sea in an amazing manner.﴾" Ibn 'Abbas said: Musa climbed up onto the rock until, when they reached it, there was a man wrapped in his cloak. Musa greeted him, and the scholar returned the greeting, then said to him: "What brought you here? If you have concerns among your people..." Musa said to him: "I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught, as guidance." ﴿He said: "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾ He was a man who knew the knowledge of the unseen, having been taught that. Musa said: "Yes." He said: ﴿"And how can you be patient about that which you do not encompass in knowledge?"﴾ That is: you only know the outward appearance of what you see of justice, and you have not encompassed from the knowledge of the unseen what I know. ﴿He said: "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter."﴾ Even if I see what opposes me. He said: ﴿"So if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you."﴾ [And even if you deny it][[Added from F, A, and al-Tabari.]] ﴿until I make a mention of it to you.﴾ So they set out walking along the seashore, seeking people who would carry them, until a new, sturdy ship passed by them, and no ship better, more complete, or more secure than it had passed by them. They asked its people to carry them, and they carried them. When they had settled in it and it had sailed away with its people, he took out a chisel and a mallet, then went to one side of it and struck it with the chisel until he made a hole in it. Then he took a plank and fitted it over the hole, then sat on it, patching it. Musa said to him, seeing a matter more grievous to him: ﴿"Have you made a hole in it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing."﴾ ﴿He said: "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ ﴿He said: "Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not impose upon me difficulty in my affair."﴾ That is: for what you left out of your covenant. Then they both left the ship and went on until, when they came to the people of a town, they found boys playing outside it, and among them was a boy; there was no boy more handsome, more radiant, or more beautiful than him. He took him by the hand, took a stone, struck his head with it until he split it open, and killed him. He said: Musa saw a terrible matter, which he could not bear: a small child whom he had killed though he had committed no wrong. He said: ﴿"Have you killed a pure soul, not in retaliation for another soul? You have certainly done an abominable thing."﴾ That is: a young child. ﴿He said: "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?" He said: "If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep me as your companion; you have indeed reached an excuse from me."﴾ That is: you have made me excused regarding my affair. ﴿So they went on until, when they came to the people of a town and asked its people for food, they refused to host them. And they found within it a wall about to collapse.﴾ So he (al-Khadir) repaired it and then started to build it up. Musa was impatient at what he saw him doing of the burden, and what he could not bear. He said: ﴿"If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it."﴾ That is: we asked them for food and they did not feed us, we asked them to host us and they did not host us, then you sat and worked without any benefit, and if you had wished you could have been given a wage for your work. He said: ﴿"This is the parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that which you could not bear with patience. As for the ship, it belonged to needy people who worked on the sea, and I wanted to damage it, for there was behind them a king who seized every ship by force."﴾ [And in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "every good ship"][[Qira'ah: a recognized variant reading of the Qur'an.]]. I damaged it only so that I might turn him away from it, and it was saved when he saw the defect that I had made in it. ﴿As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them with tyranny and disbelief. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer in compassion.﴾ ﴿As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord intended that they reach their maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord.﴾ That is: I did not do it from my own self. ﴿That is the interpretation of that which you could not bear with patience.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas used to say: The treasure was nothing but knowledge.[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/180).]]

And al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Musa and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people there. When they had settled in the dwelling, Allah revealed: "Remind them of the days of Allah." So he addressed his people and mentioned what Allah had given them of good and blessings, and reminded them when Allah saved them from the family of Pharaoh, and reminded them of the destruction of their enemy, and of how Allah had made them successors on the earth. He said: "Allah spoke to your prophet directly, and chose me for Himself, and placed upon me love from Him, and Allah has given you of everything you asked for. Your prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah." He did not leave out any blessing that He had bestowed upon them without informing them of it. A man from the Children of Israel said to him: "It is so, O Prophet of Allah; we have known what you say. Is there anyone on the earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "No." So Allah sent Jibril to Musa, peace be upon them both, and he said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And what makes you know where I place My knowledge? Rather, there is on the shore of the sea a man who is more knowledgeable than you.'" Ibn 'Abbas said: He is al-Khidr. So Musa asked his Lord to show him him. Allah revealed to him: "Go to the sea, for you will find on the shore of the sea a fish. Take it and give it to your young servant. Then keep to the shore of the sea, and when you lose the fish and it is gone from you, there you will find the righteous servant you are seeking." When Musa, the prophet of Allah, had a long journey and was exhausted by it, he asked his young servant about the fish. His young servant, who was his attendant, said to him: ﴿"Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none caused me to forget it except Satan, that I should mention it."﴾ The young man said: "I saw the fish when it took its way into the sea, making a tunnel." This amazed Musa, so he returned until he reached the rock, and he found the fish. The fish began to move in the sea and Musa followed it, and Musa was advancing his staff, parting the water with it as he followed the fish. The fish did not touch anything of the sea without it becoming dry, until it became like a rock. The prophet of Allah marveled at that, until the fish brought him to an island among the islands of the sea, where he met al-Khidr and greeted him. Al-Khidr said: "And upon you be peace. How can there be peace in this land? Who are you?" He said: "I am Musa." Al-Khidr said: "The Musa of the Children of Israel?" [He said: "Yes."][[Added from F, A, and al-Tabari.]] He welcomed him and said: "What brought you?" He said: "I have come to you ﴿so that you may teach me from what you have been taught, as guidance.﴾" ﴿He said: "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾ That is: you cannot endure that. Musa said: ﴿"You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter."﴾ He said: So he took him along, and said to him: "Do not ask me about anything I do until I explain its matter to you." That is His saying: ﴿"until I make a mention of it to you."﴾

And al-Zuhri said, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he disputed with al-Hurr ibn Qays ibn Hisn al-Fazari about the companion of Musa. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He is al-Khidr." Then Ubayy ibn Ka'b passed by them, and Ibn 'Abbas called him and said: "I and this companion of mine have disputed about the companion of Musa, who sought the way to meet him. Have you heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mention his matter?" He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: 'While Musa was among an assembly of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: "Do you know of a man more knowledgeable than you?" He said: "No." So Allah revealed to Musa: "Yes, Our servant al-Khidr." So Musa asked the way to meet him, and Allah made the fish a sign for him, and it was said to him: "When you lose the fish, it is there, so return, for you will meet him." So Musa followed the trail of the fish in the sea.' Then the young servant of Musa said to Musa: ﴿"Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish."﴾ Musa said: ﴿"That is what we were seeking." So they returned, retracing their footsteps.﴾ They found Our servant al-Khidr, and what happened between them is what Allah has recounted in His Book."[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/183).]]

The cause of Musa's [peace be upon him] [[Addition from MS F, A.]] saying this statement to his young man, Yusha' ibn Nun, was that he was told that a servant of Allah's servants at the Meeting Place of the Two Seas had knowledge that Musa did not comprehend, so he wished to go to him. He said to his young man: ﴿I will not stop until I reach the meeting place of the two seas﴾, meaning, I will not cease travelling until I reach this place where the two seas meet. Al-Farazdaq said: "They did not cease until their women swayed / in the open ground of Dhi Qar, perfume-bags laden." [[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (15/176).]]

Qatadah and others said: the two seas are the Sea of Persia on the east side, and the Sea of Rome on the west side.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: the meeting place of the two seas is at Tangier, meaning at the farthest region of the Maghrib. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿or I will journey for a long period﴾, meaning: even if I travel for a long period of time.

Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari], may Allah have mercy on him, said: some scholars of the Arabic language mentioned that *huquban* in the dialect of Qays [[In F, A: "the Arabs".]] means a year. It was also narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr that he said: *huquban* is eighty years. Mujahid said: seventy autumns. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿or I will journey for a long period﴾ that he said: an age. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said the same.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So when they reached the meeting place between them, they forgot their fish﴾, the reason was that he had been commanded to take a salted fish with him, and it was said to him: wherever you lose the fish, that is where [the one you seek] is. So they travelled until they reached the meeting place of the two seas. There was a spring there called "the Spring of Life," so they slept there. Some of the water spray from that spring reached the fish, and it began to stir, and it leapt out of the basket into the sea. Yusha' [peace be upon him] woke up, and the fish fell into the sea and began to move through it, while the water stood over it like an arch that did not close again behind it. This is why He said: ﴿and it took its way into the sea, a tunnel﴾, meaning, like a tunnel in the earth.

Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: its track remained like a stone.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: the fish did not touch any part of the sea without it drying up until it became a rock.

Muhammad [i.e. Muhammad] ibn Ishaq said, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah, from Ibn Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, when he related the account of that: "No water has parted since people existed except this water, which stood still in the place of the fish, and it parted like a window until Musa returned to it and saw its path." Then [Musa] said: ﴿That is what we were seeking﴾.

Qatadah said: a tunnel from the land, until it reached the sea; then it entered it, and whatever path it took in it became solid water.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then when they had passed on﴾, meaning, past the place where they had forgotten the fish. The forgetting is attributed to both of them, although it was Yusha' who forgot it, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿From them come forth pearls and coral﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 22], whereas they come forth only from the salt water, according to one of the two opinions.

When they had gone on from the place where they had forgotten it a stage, ﴿Musa said﴾ to ﴿his young man: Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed suffered fatigue from this journey of ours﴾ [i.e. the part of the journey] where they had passed beyond the place, ﴿fatigue﴾, meaning, weariness. He said: ﴿Do you see? When we took refuge at the rock, I forgot the fish—and none but Satan made me forget to mention it﴾. Qatadah said: Ibn Mas'ud recited: "and none but Satan made me forget it, that I should mention it." This is why He said: ﴿and it took its way into the sea in a marvellous manner﴾, meaning, its path. ﴿He said: That is what we were seeking﴾, meaning, this is what we were looking for. ﴿So they went back, retracing their footsteps﴾, meaning, they returned ﴿along their track﴾, meaning, their path, ﴿retracing﴾, meaning, following their own footprints and tracing their trail.

﴿Then they found a servant of Our servants, whom We had given mercy from Us and taught knowledge from Us﴾. This is al-Khidr [peace be upon him], as indicated by the authentic hadiths from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Bukhari said regarding this:

Al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Amr ibn Dinar narrated to us, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr informed me that he said: I said to Ibn Abbas: Nawf al-Bakali claims that Musa, the companion of al-Khidr, is not Musa the companion of the Children of Israel. Ibn Abbas said: The enemy of Allah lied. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Musa stood up to address the Children of Israel, and he was asked: Who is the most knowledgeable of people? He said: I am. Allah reproached him because he did not attribute knowledge to Him. So Allah revealed to him: Indeed, I have a servant at the meeting place of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you. Musa said: O Lord, how can I reach him? He said: Take a fish with you in a basket, and wherever you lose the fish, he is there. So he took a fish and put it in a basket, then set out, and his young man Yusha' ibn Nun, peace be upon them both, went with him, until when they came to the rock, they laid down their heads and slept. The fish stirred in the basket, came out of it, fell into the sea and took its path into the sea as a tunnel, and Allah withheld the flow of the water from the fish, so it became over it like an arch. When [Musa] awoke, his companion forgot to inform him about the fish, so they continued for the rest of their day and night. When it was the next day, Musa said to his young man: ﴿Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed suffered fatigue from this journey of ours﴾, and Musa did not feel the fatigue until they had passed the place Allah had commanded him to reach. His young man said to him: ﴿Do you see? When we took refuge at the rock, I forgot the fish—and none but Satan made me forget to mention it, and it took its way into the sea in a marvellous manner﴾." He said: "So it was a tunnel for the fish, and a marvel for Musa and his young man." He [Musa] said: ﴿That is what we were seeking﴾, so they went back, retracing their footsteps. He said: "They returned, tracing their trail, until they reached the rock, and there was a man covered with a garment. Musa greeted him, and al-Khidr said: And how is there greeting in your land? He said: I am Musa. He said: Musa of the Children of Israel? He said: Yes, I have come to you that you may teach me of what you have been taught of right guidance. ﴿He said: Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me﴾, O Musa, I have a knowledge from Allah's knowledge which He taught me, which you do not know; and you have a knowledge from Allah's knowledge which Allah taught you, which I do not know." Musa said: ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter﴾. Al-Khidr said to him: ﴿If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you﴾."

They went on walking along the seashore. A ship passed by, and they asked the people to carry them, and they recognised al-Khidr, so they carried them without a fare. When they boarded the ship, suddenly al-Khidr had pulled out a plank from the ship's planks with an axe. Musa said to him: "They carried us without a fare, and you purposely went to their ship and damaged it in order to drown its people? You have indeed done a grievous thing." ﴿He said: Did I not say that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾ * ﴿He said: Do not hold me to account for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair﴾ [[In F, A: "I did say to you", which is an error.]] He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first [objection] from Musa was forgetfulness." He said: A sparrow came and alighted on the edge of the ship and pecked once or twice in the sea [[Addition from MS A.]]. Al-Khidr said to him: "My knowledge and your knowledge, in the knowledge of Allah, are no more than what this sparrow has taken from this sea."

Then they got out of the ship, and while they were walking along the shore, al-Khidr saw a boy playing with other boys. Al-Khidr took his head [with his hand] [[Addition from MSS F, A.]] and pulled it off with his hand and killed him. Musa said to him: ﴿Have you killed a pure soul, not in retaliation for another soul? You have indeed done a dreadful thing﴾ ﴿He said: Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾?! [[In F, A: "pure".]] He said: "This is worse than the first," ﴿He said: If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep me company; you have already received an excuse from me﴾. * [[In F: "you have reached from me" which is an error.]] So they went on until, when they came to the people of a town and asked its people for food, they refused to host them. They found in it a wall about to collapse [[In T: "collapsing, so he set it up".]] ﴿—He said: leaning. Al-Khidr with his hand: "So he set it up"﴾. Musa said: "A people we came to, and they did not feed us or host us, ﴿If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it﴾." ﴿He said: This is the parting between me and you; I will inform you of the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "We wished that Musa had been patient until Allah told us more of their story."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn Abbas used to recite: "And there was a king behind them who seized every good ship by force," and he used to recite: "As for the boy, he was a disbeliever, and his parents were believers" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4725.]].

Then al-Bukhari narrated it from Qutaybah, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah ... and he mentioned something similar, and in it: "Musa went out with his young man Yusha' ibn Nun, and with them the fish, until they reached the rock, and they alighted beside it. He said: Musa laid his head down and slept. Sufyan said: and in a narration other than that of Amr, he said: At the base of the rock there is a spring called al-Hayat [Life], none of whose water touches anything without it being brought to life. So the fish was touched by the water of that spring; he said: it moved and slipped out of the basket and entered the sea. When [Musa] awoke, Musa said to his young man: ﴿Bring us our morning meal﴾." Thus he said, and he related the hadith [continuing]. "A sparrow alighted on the edge of the ship and dipped its beak in the sea, and al-Khidr said to Musa: My knowledge and your knowledge and the knowledge of all creatures, in the knowledge of Allah, is no more than the amount this sparrow has dipped its beak into [the sea]." He mentioned its full text in similar terms [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4727.]].

Al-Bukhari also said: Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to us, that Ibn Jurayj informed them, saying: Ya'la ibn Muslim and 'Amr ibn Dinar informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr (one of them adds to the other), and others besides them, whom I heard narrating from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "We were with Ibn 'Abbas in his house when he said: 'Ask me.' I said: 'O Abu 'Abbas, may Allah make me your ransom, in Kufa there is a storyteller called Nawf, who claims that he is not Musa of the Children of Israel.' As for 'Amr, he said to me: 'The enemy of Allah has lied!' As for Ya'la, he said to me: 'Ibn 'Abbas said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b narrated to me, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Musa, the Messenger of Allah, once reminded the people, until the eyes overflowed with tears and the hearts softened. He turned to leave, and a man caught up with him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you?' He said: 'No.' So Allah rebuked him, because he had not referred the knowledge to Allah. It was said to him: 'Yes.' He said: 'O Lord, where is he?' It was said: 'At the meeting place of the two seas.' He said: 'O Lord, give me a sign by which I may know it.'"'" 'Amr said to me: "He said: 'Where the fish leaves you.'" And Ya'la said to me: "Take a dead fish, and where life is breathed into it, that is the place." So he took a fish and placed it in a basket, and he said to his servant: "I will not burden you except that you tell me where the fish leaves you." He said: "You have not burdened me greatly." This is His saying: ﴿And when Musa said to his servant﴾, namely Yusha' ibn Nun, which is not in the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr. He said: "While he was in the shade of a rock in a place of moisture, the fish moved while Musa was sleeping. His servant said: 'I will not wake him.' When he awoke, he forgot to tell him. The fish leapt until it entered the sea, and Allah stopped the flow of water from it, so that its trace was like a trace on a stone." [He said: 'Amr said to me: "Like this, its trace was as if on a stone,"] and he made a circle with his thumb and the finger next to it. ﴿Indeed we have suffered much fatigue from this journey of ours﴾. He said: "Allah has removed the fatigue from you." (This is not in the narration of Sa'id.) He informed him, and they returned and found a Khidr. He said: 'Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman said: "On a green carpet on the bank of the sea." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "He was covered with a garment, having placed one end under his feet and the other end under his head. Musa greeted him, and he uncovered his face and said: 'Is there peace on this earth? Who are you?' He said: 'I am Musa.' He said: 'Musa of the Children of Israel?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'What is your matter?' He said: 'I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught, as right guidance.' He said: 'Is the Torah not sufficient for you in your hand, and that revelation comes to you? O Musa, I have knowledge that it is not fitting for you to know, and you have knowledge that it is not fitting for me to know.' Then a bird took with its beak from the sea [and said: 'By Allah, my knowledge and your knowledge, in comparison with the knowledge of Allah, are no more than what this bird has taken with its beak from the sea'], until they boarded the ship and found small ferries carrying the people of this shore to the other shore. They recognised him and said: 'The righteous servant of Allah?' He said: 'We said to Sa'id: Khidr?' He said: 'Yes. We will not carry him for a fee.' Then he tore the ship and drove a peg into it." Musa said: ﴿Have you torn it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing﴾. Mujahid said: "Munkaran (a grave matter)." He said: ﴿Did I not say that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾ The first was forgetfulness, the middle was a condition, and the third was deliberate. ﴿He said: Do not take me to task for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair.﴾ ﴿So they set out﴾, until they met a boy and he killed him. Ya'la said: Sa'id said: "He found boys playing, and he seized a disbelieving, handsome boy, laid him down, then slaughtered him with a knife." He said: ﴿Have you killed an innocent soul?﴾ (who had not done wrong). Ibn 'Abbas read it as ﴿zakiyyatan﴾ ("zakiyya" meaning Muslim), like your saying: "a pure boy (ghulaman zakiyyan)." ﴿So they set out, until they found a wall about to collapse, and he set it upright.﴾ Sa'id said with his hand like this, and raised his hand, and it stood straight. Ya'la said: "I think Sa'id said: 'He wiped it with his hand and it stood straight.'" He said: ﴿If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it.﴾ Sa'id said: "A wage we could eat." ﴿And there was behind them a king﴾, and it was "in front of them." Ibn 'Abbas read it: "Amamahum malik" (in front of them a king). They claim, apart from Sa'id, that he was Hudad ibn Budad, and the boy who was killed, his name, they claim, was Jaysur. ﴿A king who seizes every ship by force﴾. So I wished, when it passed by him, that he would leave it because of its defect, and when they passed him they would repair it and benefit from it. Some of them say: they sealed it with a bottle, and some say: with pitch. ﴿As for the boy, his parents were believers﴾, while he was a disbeliever. ﴿We feared that he would burden them with transgression and disbelief﴾: that his love for him would lead them to follow him in his religion. ﴿So we wished that their Lord would give them in exchange one better than him in purity and nearer in compassion﴾, like His saying: ﴿Have you killed an innocent soul?﴾ and ﴿nearer in compassion﴾: they were more merciful to that one than to the first whom Khidr killed. Other than Sa'id ibn Jubayr claimed that they were given in exchange a girl. As for Dawud ibn Abi 'Asim, he said, from more than one: it was a girl.

Al-Bukhari, hadith no. (4726).

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Musa, peace be upon him, addressed the Children of Israel and said: "No one is more knowledgeable of Allah and His command than I am." So he was commanded to meet this man. He then mentioned something similar to what has preceded, with some addition and omission. (Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq, 1/341, 342.) And Allah knows best.

And Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from al-Hasan ibn 'Umarah, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah[[In F and A: "'Uyaynah".]], from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I sat with Ibn 'Abbas, and with him was a group of People of the Book. Some of them said: "O Abu al-'Abbas, Nawf, the son of Ka'b's wife, claims on Ka'b's authority that Musa the prophet who sought the knowledge is only Musa ibn Mitha." Sa'id said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Does Nawf say this?" Sa'id said: I replied: "Yes, I heard Nawf say that." He said: "Did you hear it yourself, O Sa'id?" He said: I said: "Yes." He said: "Nawf has lied." Then Ibn 'Abbas said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b narrated to me, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Musa, the one of the Children of Israel, asked his Lord and said: 'O Lord, if there is anyone among Your servants who is more knowledgeable than me, guide me to him.' He said to him: 'Yes, among My servants there is one who is more knowledgeable than you.' Then He described his place to him and permitted him to meet him. So Musa set out, and with him was his young servant, and with him was a fish, salted[[Mulayh: a fish that has been salted or preserved.]]. It had been said to him: 'When this fish comes back to life in a place, your companion is there, and you will have attained your need.' So Musa set out, and with him was his young servant, and with him was that fish, and they carried it. He traveled until the journey exhausted him, and he reached the rock and that water, and that water was the water of life; whoever drinks from it becomes immortal, and nothing dead comes near it without coming back to life. When they dismounted and the fish touched the water, it came back to life, ﴿and it took its way into the sea, making a tunnel﴾. Then they set off, and when he had passed the place where they had stopped, Musa said to his young servant: ﴿Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed suffered fatigue from this journey of ours.﴾ The young man said, and he mentioned: ﴿Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none caused me to forget it except Satan, that I should mention it. And it took its way into the sea in an amazing manner.﴾" Ibn 'Abbas said: Musa climbed up onto the rock until, when they reached it, there was a man wrapped in his cloak. Musa greeted him, and the scholar returned the greeting, then said to him: "What brought you here? If you have concerns among your people..." Musa said to him: "I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught, as guidance." ﴿He said: "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾ He was a man who knew the knowledge of the unseen, having been taught that. Musa said: "Yes." He said: ﴿"And how can you be patient about that which you do not encompass in knowledge?"﴾ That is: you only know the outward appearance of what you see of justice, and you have not encompassed from the knowledge of the unseen what I know. ﴿He said: "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter."﴾ Even if I see what opposes me. He said: ﴿"So if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you."﴾ [And even if you deny it][[Added from F, A, and al-Tabari.]] ﴿until I make a mention of it to you.﴾ So they set out walking along the seashore, seeking people who would carry them, until a new, sturdy ship passed by them, and no ship better, more complete, or more secure than it had passed by them. They asked its people to carry them, and they carried them. When they had settled in it and it had sailed away with its people, he took out a chisel and a mallet, then went to one side of it and struck it with the chisel until he made a hole in it. Then he took a plank and fitted it over the hole, then sat on it, patching it. Musa said to him, seeing a matter more grievous to him: ﴿"Have you made a hole in it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing."﴾ ﴿He said: "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ ﴿He said: "Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not impose upon me difficulty in my affair."﴾ That is: for what you left out of your covenant. Then they both left the ship and went on until, when they came to the people of a town, they found boys playing outside it, and among them was a boy; there was no boy more handsome, more radiant, or more beautiful than him. He took him by the hand, took a stone, struck his head with it until he split it open, and killed him. He said: Musa saw a terrible matter, which he could not bear: a small child whom he had killed though he had committed no wrong. He said: ﴿"Have you killed a pure soul, not in retaliation for another soul? You have certainly done an abominable thing."﴾ That is: a young child. ﴿He said: "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?" He said: "If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep me as your companion; you have indeed reached an excuse from me."﴾ That is: you have made me excused regarding my affair. ﴿So they went on until, when they came to the people of a town and asked its people for food, they refused to host them. And they found within it a wall about to collapse.﴾ So he (al-Khadir) repaired it and then started to build it up. Musa was impatient at what he saw him doing of the burden, and what he could not bear. He said: ﴿"If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it."﴾ That is: we asked them for food and they did not feed us, we asked them to host us and they did not host us, then you sat and worked without any benefit, and if you had wished you could have been given a wage for your work. He said: ﴿"This is the parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that which you could not bear with patience. As for the ship, it belonged to needy people who worked on the sea, and I wanted to damage it, for there was behind them a king who seized every ship by force."﴾ [And in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "every good ship"][[Qira'ah: a recognized variant reading of the Qur'an.]]. I damaged it only so that I might turn him away from it, and it was saved when he saw the defect that I had made in it. ﴿As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them with tyranny and disbelief. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer in compassion.﴾ ﴿As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord intended that they reach their maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord.﴾ That is: I did not do it from my own self. ﴿That is the interpretation of that which you could not bear with patience.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas used to say: The treasure was nothing but knowledge.[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/180).]]

And al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Musa and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people there. When they had settled in the dwelling, Allah revealed: "Remind them of the days of Allah." So he addressed his people and mentioned what Allah had given them of good and blessings, and reminded them when Allah saved them from the family of Pharaoh, and reminded them of the destruction of their enemy, and of how Allah had made them successors on the earth. He said: "Allah spoke to your prophet directly, and chose me for Himself, and placed upon me love from Him, and Allah has given you of everything you asked for. Your prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah." He did not leave out any blessing that He had bestowed upon them without informing them of it. A man from the Children of Israel said to him: "It is so, O Prophet of Allah; we have known what you say. Is there anyone on the earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "No." So Allah sent Jibril to Musa, peace be upon them both, and he said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And what makes you know where I place My knowledge? Rather, there is on the shore of the sea a man who is more knowledgeable than you.'" Ibn 'Abbas said: He is al-Khidr. So Musa asked his Lord to show him him. Allah revealed to him: "Go to the sea, for you will find on the shore of the sea a fish. Take it and give it to your young servant. Then keep to the shore of the sea, and when you lose the fish and it is gone from you, there you will find the righteous servant you are seeking." When Musa, the prophet of Allah, had a long journey and was exhausted by it, he asked his young servant about the fish. His young servant, who was his attendant, said to him: ﴿"Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none caused me to forget it except Satan, that I should mention it."﴾ The young man said: "I saw the fish when it took its way into the sea, making a tunnel." This amazed Musa, so he returned until he reached the rock, and he found the fish. The fish began to move in the sea and Musa followed it, and Musa was advancing his staff, parting the water with it as he followed the fish. The fish did not touch anything of the sea without it becoming dry, until it became like a rock. The prophet of Allah marveled at that, until the fish brought him to an island among the islands of the sea, where he met al-Khidr and greeted him. Al-Khidr said: "And upon you be peace. How can there be peace in this land? Who are you?" He said: "I am Musa." Al-Khidr said: "The Musa of the Children of Israel?" [He said: "Yes."][[Added from F, A, and al-Tabari.]] He welcomed him and said: "What brought you?" He said: "I have come to you ﴿so that you may teach me from what you have been taught, as guidance.﴾" ﴿He said: "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾ That is: you cannot endure that. Musa said: ﴿"You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter."﴾ He said: So he took him along, and said to him: "Do not ask me about anything I do until I explain its matter to you." That is His saying: ﴿"until I make a mention of it to you."﴾

And al-Zuhri said, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he disputed with al-Hurr ibn Qays ibn Hisn al-Fazari about the companion of Musa. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He is al-Khidr." Then Ubayy ibn Ka'b passed by them, and Ibn 'Abbas called him and said: "I and this companion of mine have disputed about the companion of Musa, who sought the way to meet him. Have you heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mention his matter?" He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: 'While Musa was among an assembly of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: "Do you know of a man more knowledgeable than you?" He said: "No." So Allah revealed to Musa: "Yes, Our servant al-Khidr." So Musa asked the way to meet him, and Allah made the fish a sign for him, and it was said to him: "When you lose the fish, it is there, so return, for you will meet him." So Musa followed the trail of the fish in the sea.' Then the young servant of Musa said to Musa: ﴿"Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish."﴾ Musa said: ﴿"That is what we were seeking." So they returned, retracing their footsteps.﴾ They found Our servant al-Khidr, and what happened between them is what Allah has recounted in His Book."[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/183).]]

The cause of Musa's [peace be upon him] [[Addition from MS F, A.]] saying this statement to his young man, Yusha' ibn Nun, was that he was told that a servant of Allah's servants at the Meeting Place of the Two Seas had knowledge that Musa did not comprehend, so he wished to go to him. He said to his young man: ﴿I will not stop until I reach the meeting place of the two seas﴾, meaning, I will not cease travelling until I reach this place where the two seas meet. Al-Farazdaq said: "They did not cease until their women swayed / in the open ground of Dhi Qar, perfume-bags laden." [[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (15/176).]]

Qatadah and others said: the two seas are the Sea of Persia on the east side, and the Sea of Rome on the west side.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: the meeting place of the two seas is at Tangier, meaning at the farthest region of the Maghrib. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿or I will journey for a long period﴾, meaning: even if I travel for a long period of time.

Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari], may Allah have mercy on him, said: some scholars of the Arabic language mentioned that *huquban* in the dialect of Qays [[In F, A: "the Arabs".]] means a year. It was also narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr that he said: *huquban* is eighty years. Mujahid said: seventy autumns. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿or I will journey for a long period﴾ that he said: an age. Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said the same.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So when they reached the meeting place between them, they forgot their fish﴾, the reason was that he had been commanded to take a salted fish with him, and it was said to him: wherever you lose the fish, that is where [the one you seek] is. So they travelled until they reached the meeting place of the two seas. There was a spring there called "the Spring of Life," so they slept there. Some of the water spray from that spring reached the fish, and it began to stir, and it leapt out of the basket into the sea. Yusha' [peace be upon him] woke up, and the fish fell into the sea and began to move through it, while the water stood over it like an arch that did not close again behind it. This is why He said: ﴿and it took its way into the sea, a tunnel﴾, meaning, like a tunnel in the earth.

Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: its track remained like a stone.

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: the fish did not touch any part of the sea without it drying up until it became a rock.

Muhammad [i.e. Muhammad] ibn Ishaq said, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah, from Ibn Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, when he related the account of that: "No water has parted since people existed except this water, which stood still in the place of the fish, and it parted like a window until Musa returned to it and saw its path." Then [Musa] said: ﴿That is what we were seeking﴾.

Qatadah said: a tunnel from the land, until it reached the sea; then it entered it, and whatever path it took in it became solid water.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then when they had passed on﴾, meaning, past the place where they had forgotten the fish. The forgetting is attributed to both of them, although it was Yusha' who forgot it, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿From them come forth pearls and coral﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 22], whereas they come forth only from the salt water, according to one of the two opinions.

When they had gone on from the place where they had forgotten it a stage, ﴿Musa said﴾ to ﴿his young man: Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed suffered fatigue from this journey of ours﴾ [i.e. the part of the journey] where they had passed beyond the place, ﴿fatigue﴾, meaning, weariness. He said: ﴿Do you see? When we took refuge at the rock, I forgot the fish—and none but Satan made me forget to mention it﴾. Qatadah said: Ibn Mas'ud recited: "and none but Satan made me forget it, that I should mention it." This is why He said: ﴿and it took its way into the sea in a marvellous manner﴾, meaning, its path. ﴿He said: That is what we were seeking﴾, meaning, this is what we were looking for. ﴿So they went back, retracing their footsteps﴾, meaning, they returned ﴿along their track﴾, meaning, their path, ﴿retracing﴾, meaning, following their own footprints and tracing their trail.

﴿Then they found a servant of Our servants, whom We had given mercy from Us and taught knowledge from Us﴾. This is al-Khidr [peace be upon him], as indicated by the authentic hadiths from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Bukhari said regarding this:

Al-Humaydi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Amr ibn Dinar narrated to us, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr informed me that he said: I said to Ibn Abbas: Nawf al-Bakali claims that Musa, the companion of al-Khidr, is not Musa the companion of the Children of Israel. Ibn Abbas said: The enemy of Allah lied. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Musa stood up to address the Children of Israel, and he was asked: Who is the most knowledgeable of people? He said: I am. Allah reproached him because he did not attribute knowledge to Him. So Allah revealed to him: Indeed, I have a servant at the meeting place of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you. Musa said: O Lord, how can I reach him? He said: Take a fish with you in a basket, and wherever you lose the fish, he is there. So he took a fish and put it in a basket, then set out, and his young man Yusha' ibn Nun, peace be upon them both, went with him, until when they came to the rock, they laid down their heads and slept. The fish stirred in the basket, came out of it, fell into the sea and took its path into the sea as a tunnel, and Allah withheld the flow of the water from the fish, so it became over it like an arch. When [Musa] awoke, his companion forgot to inform him about the fish, so they continued for the rest of their day and night. When it was the next day, Musa said to his young man: ﴿Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed suffered fatigue from this journey of ours﴾, and Musa did not feel the fatigue until they had passed the place Allah had commanded him to reach. His young man said to him: ﴿Do you see? When we took refuge at the rock, I forgot the fish—and none but Satan made me forget to mention it, and it took its way into the sea in a marvellous manner﴾." He said: "So it was a tunnel for the fish, and a marvel for Musa and his young man." He [Musa] said: ﴿That is what we were seeking﴾, so they went back, retracing their footsteps. He said: "They returned, tracing their trail, until they reached the rock, and there was a man covered with a garment. Musa greeted him, and al-Khidr said: And how is there greeting in your land? He said: I am Musa. He said: Musa of the Children of Israel? He said: Yes, I have come to you that you may teach me of what you have been taught of right guidance. ﴿He said: Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me﴾, O Musa, I have a knowledge from Allah's knowledge which He taught me, which you do not know; and you have a knowledge from Allah's knowledge which Allah taught you, which I do not know." Musa said: ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter﴾. Al-Khidr said to him: ﴿If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you﴾."

They went on walking along the seashore. A ship passed by, and they asked the people to carry them, and they recognised al-Khidr, so they carried them without a fare. When they boarded the ship, suddenly al-Khidr had pulled out a plank from the ship's planks with an axe. Musa said to him: "They carried us without a fare, and you purposely went to their ship and damaged it in order to drown its people? You have indeed done a grievous thing." ﴿He said: Did I not say that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾ * ﴿He said: Do not hold me to account for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair﴾ [[In F, A: "I did say to you", which is an error.]] He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first [objection] from Musa was forgetfulness." He said: A sparrow came and alighted on the edge of the ship and pecked once or twice in the sea [[Addition from MS A.]]. Al-Khidr said to him: "My knowledge and your knowledge, in the knowledge of Allah, are no more than what this sparrow has taken from this sea."

Then they got out of the ship, and while they were walking along the shore, al-Khidr saw a boy playing with other boys. Al-Khidr took his head [with his hand] [[Addition from MSS F, A.]] and pulled it off with his hand and killed him. Musa said to him: ﴿Have you killed a pure soul, not in retaliation for another soul? You have indeed done a dreadful thing﴾ ﴿He said: Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾?! [[In F, A: "pure".]] He said: "This is worse than the first," ﴿He said: If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep me company; you have already received an excuse from me﴾. * [[In F: "you have reached from me" which is an error.]] So they went on until, when they came to the people of a town and asked its people for food, they refused to host them. They found in it a wall about to collapse [[In T: "collapsing, so he set it up".]] ﴿—He said: leaning. Al-Khidr with his hand: "So he set it up"﴾. Musa said: "A people we came to, and they did not feed us or host us, ﴿If you wished, you could have taken a wage for it﴾." ﴿He said: This is the parting between me and you; I will inform you of the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "We wished that Musa had been patient until Allah told us more of their story."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn Abbas used to recite: "And there was a king behind them who seized every good ship by force," and he used to recite: "As for the boy, he was a disbeliever, and his parents were believers" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4725.]].

Then al-Bukhari narrated it from Qutaybah, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah ... and he mentioned something similar, and in it: "Musa went out with his young man Yusha' ibn Nun, and with them the fish, until they reached the rock, and they alighted beside it. He said: Musa laid his head down and slept. Sufyan said: and in a narration other than that of Amr, he said: At the base of the rock there is a spring called al-Hayat [Life], none of whose water touches anything without it being brought to life. So the fish was touched by the water of that spring; he said: it moved and slipped out of the basket and entered the sea. When [Musa] awoke, Musa said to his young man: ﴿Bring us our morning meal﴾." Thus he said, and he related the hadith [continuing]. "A sparrow alighted on the edge of the ship and dipped its beak in the sea, and al-Khidr said to Musa: My knowledge and your knowledge and the knowledge of all creatures, in the knowledge of Allah, is no more than the amount this sparrow has dipped its beak into [the sea]." He mentioned its full text in similar terms [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4727.]].

Al-Bukhari also said: Ibrahim ibn Musa narrated to us, Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to us, that Ibn Jurayj informed them, saying: Ya'la ibn Muslim and 'Amr ibn Dinar informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr (one of them adds to the other), and others besides them, whom I heard narrating from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "We were with Ibn 'Abbas in his house when he said: 'Ask me.' I said: 'O Abu 'Abbas, may Allah make me your ransom, in Kufa there is a storyteller called Nawf, who claims that he is not Musa of the Children of Israel.' As for 'Amr, he said to me: 'The enemy of Allah has lied!' As for Ya'la, he said to me: 'Ibn 'Abbas said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b narrated to me, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Musa, the Messenger of Allah, once reminded the people, until the eyes overflowed with tears and the hearts softened. He turned to leave, and a man caught up with him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you?' He said: 'No.' So Allah rebuked him, because he had not referred the knowledge to Allah. It was said to him: 'Yes.' He said: 'O Lord, where is he?' It was said: 'At the meeting place of the two seas.' He said: 'O Lord, give me a sign by which I may know it.'"'" 'Amr said to me: "He said: 'Where the fish leaves you.'" And Ya'la said to me: "Take a dead fish, and where life is breathed into it, that is the place." So he took a fish and placed it in a basket, and he said to his servant: "I will not burden you except that you tell me where the fish leaves you." He said: "You have not burdened me greatly." This is His saying: ﴿And when Musa said to his servant﴾, namely Yusha' ibn Nun, which is not in the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr. He said: "While he was in the shade of a rock in a place of moisture, the fish moved while Musa was sleeping. His servant said: 'I will not wake him.' When he awoke, he forgot to tell him. The fish leapt until it entered the sea, and Allah stopped the flow of water from it, so that its trace was like a trace on a stone." [He said: 'Amr said to me: "Like this, its trace was as if on a stone,"] and he made a circle with his thumb and the finger next to it. ﴿Indeed we have suffered much fatigue from this journey of ours﴾. He said: "Allah has removed the fatigue from you." (This is not in the narration of Sa'id.) He informed him, and they returned and found a Khidr. He said: 'Uthman ibn Abi Sulayman said: "On a green carpet on the bank of the sea." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "He was covered with a garment, having placed one end under his feet and the other end under his head. Musa greeted him, and he uncovered his face and said: 'Is there peace on this earth? Who are you?' He said: 'I am Musa.' He said: 'Musa of the Children of Israel?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'What is your matter?' He said: 'I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught, as right guidance.' He said: 'Is the Torah not sufficient for you in your hand, and that revelation comes to you? O Musa, I have knowledge that it is not fitting for you to know, and you have knowledge that it is not fitting for me to know.' Then a bird took with its beak from the sea [and said: 'By Allah, my knowledge and your knowledge, in comparison with the knowledge of Allah, are no more than what this bird has taken with its beak from the sea'], until they boarded the ship and found small ferries carrying the people of this shore to the other shore. They recognised him and said: 'The righteous servant of Allah?' He said: 'We said to Sa'id: Khidr?' He said: 'Yes. We will not carry him for a fee.' Then he tore the ship and drove a peg into it." Musa said: ﴿Have you torn it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing﴾. Mujahid said: "Munkaran (a grave matter)." He said: ﴿Did I not say that you would not be able to have patience with me?﴾ The first was forgetfulness, the middle was a condition, and the third was deliberate. ﴿He said: Do not take me to task for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair.﴾ ﴿So they set out﴾, until they met a boy and he killed him. Ya'la said: Sa'id said: "He found boys playing, and he seized a disbelieving, handsome boy, laid him down, then slaughtered him with a knife." He said: ﴿Have you killed an innocent soul?﴾ (who had not done wrong). Ibn 'Abbas read it as ﴿zakiyyatan﴾ ("zakiyya" meaning Muslim), like your saying: "a pure boy (ghulaman zakiyyan)." ﴿So they set out, until they found a wall about to collapse, and he set it upright.﴾ Sa'id said with his hand like this, and raised his hand, and it stood straight. Ya'la said: "I think Sa'id said: 'He wiped it with his hand and it stood straight.'" He said: ﴿If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it.﴾ Sa'id said: "A wage we could eat." ﴿And there was behind them a king﴾, and it was "in front of them." Ibn 'Abbas read it: "Amamahum malik" (in front of them a king). They claim, apart from Sa'id, that he was Hudad ibn Budad, and the boy who was killed, his name, they claim, was Jaysur. ﴿A king who seizes every ship by force﴾. So I wished, when it passed by him, that he would leave it because of its defect, and when they passed him they would repair it and benefit from it. Some of them say: they sealed it with a bottle, and some say: with pitch. ﴿As for the boy, his parents were believers﴾, while he was a disbeliever. ﴿We feared that he would burden them with transgression and disbelief﴾: that his love for him would lead them to follow him in his religion. ﴿So we wished that their Lord would give them in exchange one better than him in purity and nearer in compassion﴾, like His saying: ﴿Have you killed an innocent soul?﴾ and ﴿nearer in compassion﴾: they were more merciful to that one than to the first whom Khidr killed. Other than Sa'id ibn Jubayr claimed that they were given in exchange a girl. As for Dawud ibn Abi 'Asim, he said, from more than one: it was a girl.

Al-Bukhari, hadith no. (4726).

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Musa, peace be upon him, addressed the Children of Israel and said: "No one is more knowledgeable of Allah and His command than I am." So he was commanded to meet this man. He then mentioned something similar to what has preceded, with some addition and omission. (Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq, 1/341, 342.) And Allah knows best.

And Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from al-Hasan ibn 'Umarah, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah[[In F and A: "'Uyaynah".]], from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I sat with Ibn 'Abbas, and with him was a group of People of the Book. Some of them said: "O Abu al-'Abbas, Nawf, the son of Ka'b's wife, claims on Ka'b's authority that Musa the prophet who sought the knowledge is only Musa ibn Mitha." Sa'id said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "Does Nawf say this?" Sa'id said: I replied: "Yes, I heard Nawf say that." He said: "Did you hear it yourself, O Sa'id?" He said: I said: "Yes." He said: "Nawf has lied." Then Ibn 'Abbas said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b narrated to me, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Musa, the one of the Children of Israel, asked his Lord and said: 'O Lord, if there is anyone among Your servants who is more knowledgeable than me, guide me to him.' He said to him: 'Yes, among My servants there is one who is more knowledgeable than you.' Then He described his place to him and permitted him to meet him. So Musa set out, and with him was his young servant, and with him was a fish, salted[[Mulayh: a fish that has been salted or preserved.]]. It had been said to him: 'When this fish comes back to life in a place, your companion is there, and you will have attained your need.' So Musa set out, and with him was his young servant, and with him was that fish, and they carried it. He traveled until the journey exhausted him, and he reached the rock and that water, and that water was the water of life; whoever drinks from it becomes immortal, and nothing dead comes near it without coming back to life. When they dismounted and the fish touched the water, it came back to life, ﴿and it took its way into the sea, making a tunnel﴾. Then they set off, and when he had passed the place where they had stopped, Musa said to his young servant: ﴿Bring us our morning meal; we have indeed suffered fatigue from this journey of ours.﴾ The young man said, and he mentioned: ﴿Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none caused me to forget it except Satan, that I should mention it. And it took its way into the sea in an amazing manner.﴾" Ibn 'Abbas said: Musa climbed up onto the rock until, when they reached it, there was a man wrapped in his cloak. Musa greeted him, and the scholar returned the greeting, then said to him: "What brought you here? If you have concerns among your people..." Musa said to him: "I have come to you so that you may teach me of what you have been taught, as guidance." ﴿He said: "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾ He was a man who knew the knowledge of the unseen, having been taught that. Musa said: "Yes." He said: ﴿"And how can you be patient about that which you do not encompass in knowledge?"﴾ That is: you only know the outward appearance of what you see of justice, and you have not encompassed from the knowledge of the unseen what I know. ﴿He said: "You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter."﴾ Even if I see what opposes me. He said: ﴿"So if you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you."﴾ [And even if you deny it][[Added from F, A, and al-Tabari.]] ﴿until I make a mention of it to you.﴾ So they set out walking along the seashore, seeking people who would carry them, until a new, sturdy ship passed by them, and no ship better, more complete, or more secure than it had passed by them. They asked its people to carry them, and they carried them. When they had settled in it and it had sailed away with its people, he took out a chisel and a mallet, then went to one side of it and struck it with the chisel until he made a hole in it. Then he took a plank and fitted it over the hole, then sat on it, patching it. Musa said to him, seeing a matter more grievous to him: ﴿"Have you made a hole in it to drown its people? You have certainly done a dreadful thing."﴾ ﴿He said: "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ ﴿He said: "Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not impose upon me difficulty in my affair."﴾ That is: for what you left out of your covenant. Then they both left the ship and went on until, when they came to the people of a town, they found boys playing outside it, and among them was a boy; there was no boy more handsome, more radiant, or more beautiful than him. He took him by the hand, took a stone, struck his head with it until he split it open, and killed him. He said: Musa saw a terrible matter, which he could not bear: a small child whom he had killed though he had committed no wrong. He said: ﴿"Have you killed a pure soul, not in retaliation for another soul? You have certainly done an abominable thing."﴾ That is: a young child. ﴿He said: "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?" He said: "If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep me as your companion; you have indeed reached an excuse from me."﴾ That is: you have made me excused regarding my affair. ﴿So they went on until, when they came to the people of a town and asked its people for food, they refused to host them. And they found within it a wall about to collapse.﴾ So he (al-Khadir) repaired it and then started to build it up. Musa was impatient at what he saw him doing of the burden, and what he could not bear. He said: ﴿"If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it."﴾ That is: we asked them for food and they did not feed us, we asked them to host us and they did not host us, then you sat and worked without any benefit, and if you had wished you could have been given a wage for your work. He said: ﴿"This is the parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that which you could not bear with patience. As for the ship, it belonged to needy people who worked on the sea, and I wanted to damage it, for there was behind them a king who seized every ship by force."﴾ [And in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "every good ship"][[Qira'ah: a recognized variant reading of the Qur'an.]]. I damaged it only so that I might turn him away from it, and it was saved when he saw the defect that I had made in it. ﴿As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them with tyranny and disbelief. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer in compassion.﴾ ﴿As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord intended that they reach their maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord.﴾ That is: I did not do it from my own self. ﴿That is the interpretation of that which you could not bear with patience.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas used to say: The treasure was nothing but knowledge.[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/180).]]

And al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Musa and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people there. When they had settled in the dwelling, Allah revealed: "Remind them of the days of Allah." So he addressed his people and mentioned what Allah had given them of good and blessings, and reminded them when Allah saved them from the family of Pharaoh, and reminded them of the destruction of their enemy, and of how Allah had made them successors on the earth. He said: "Allah spoke to your prophet directly, and chose me for Himself, and placed upon me love from Him, and Allah has given you of everything you asked for. Your prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah." He did not leave out any blessing that He had bestowed upon them without informing them of it. A man from the Children of Israel said to him: "It is so, O Prophet of Allah; we have known what you say. Is there anyone on the earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "No." So Allah sent Jibril to Musa, peace be upon them both, and he said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And what makes you know where I place My knowledge? Rather, there is on the shore of the sea a man who is more knowledgeable than you.'" Ibn 'Abbas said: He is al-Khidr. So Musa asked his Lord to show him him. Allah revealed to him: "Go to the sea, for you will find on the shore of the sea a fish. Take it and give it to your young servant. Then keep to the shore of the sea, and when you lose the fish and it is gone from you, there you will find the righteous servant you are seeking." When Musa, the prophet of Allah, had a long journey and was exhausted by it, he asked his young servant about the fish. His young servant, who was his attendant, said to him: ﴿"Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none caused me to forget it except Satan, that I should mention it."﴾ The young man said: "I saw the fish when it took its way into the sea, making a tunnel." This amazed Musa, so he returned until he reached the rock, and he found the fish. The fish began to move in the sea and Musa followed it, and Musa was advancing his staff, parting the water with it as he followed the fish. The fish did not touch anything of the sea without it becoming dry, until it became like a rock. The prophet of Allah marveled at that, until the fish brought him to an island among the islands of the sea, where he met al-Khidr and greeted him. Al-Khidr said: "And upon you be peace. How can there be peace in this land? Who are you?" He said: "I am Musa." Al-Khidr said: "The Musa of the Children of Israel?" [He said: "Yes."][[Added from F, A, and al-Tabari.]] He welcomed him and said: "What brought you?" He said: "I have come to you ﴿so that you may teach me from what you have been taught, as guidance.﴾" ﴿He said: "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾ That is: you cannot endure that. Musa said: ﴿"You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter."﴾ He said: So he took him along, and said to him: "Do not ask me about anything I do until I explain its matter to you." That is His saying: ﴿"until I make a mention of it to you."﴾

And al-Zuhri said, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he disputed with al-Hurr ibn Qays ibn Hisn al-Fazari about the companion of Musa. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He is al-Khidr." Then Ubayy ibn Ka'b passed by them, and Ibn 'Abbas called him and said: "I and this companion of mine have disputed about the companion of Musa, who sought the way to meet him. Have you heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mention his matter?" He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: 'While Musa was among an assembly of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: "Do you know of a man more knowledgeable than you?" He said: "No." So Allah revealed to Musa: "Yes, Our servant al-Khidr." So Musa asked the way to meet him, and Allah made the fish a sign for him, and it was said to him: "When you lose the fish, it is there, so return, for you will meet him." So Musa followed the trail of the fish in the sea.' Then the young servant of Musa said to Musa: ﴿"Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish."﴾ Musa said: ﴿"That is what we were seeking." So they returned, retracing their footsteps.﴾ They found Our servant al-Khidr, and what happened between them is what Allah has recounted in His Book."[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/183).]]

The cause of Musa's [peace be upon him] [[Addition from MS F, A.]] saying this statement to his young man, Yusha' ibn Nun, was that he was told that a servant of Allah's servants at the Meeting Place of the Two Seas had knowledge that Musa did not comprehend, so he wished to go to him. He said to his young man: ﴿I will not stop until I reach the meeting place of the two seas﴾, meaning, I will not cease travelling until I reach this place where the two seas meet. Al-Farazdaq said: "They did not cease until their women swayed / in the open ground of Dhi Qar, perfume-bags laden." [[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (15/176).]]

Qatadah and others said: the two seas are the Sea of Persia on the east side, and the Sea of Rome on the west side.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: the meeting place of the two seas is at Tangier, meaning at the farthest region of the Maghrib. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿or I will journey for a long period﴾, meaning: even if I travel for a long period of time.
