He said: ﴿"If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it."﴾ That is: we asked them for food and they did not feed us, we asked them to host us and they did not host us, then you sat and worked without any benefit, and if you had wished you could have been given a wage for your work. He said: ﴿"This is the parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that which you could not bear with patience. As for the ship, it belonged to needy people who worked on the sea, and I wanted to damage it, for there was behind them a king who seized every ship by force."﴾ [And in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "every good ship"][[Qira'ah: a recognized variant reading of the Qur'an.]]. I damaged it only so that I might turn him away from it, and it was saved when he saw the defect that I had made in it. ﴿As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them with tyranny and disbelief. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer in compassion.﴾ ﴿As for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them, and their father had been righteous. So your Lord intended that they reach their maturity and extract their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord.﴾ That is: I did not do it from my own self. ﴿That is the interpretation of that which you could not bear with patience.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas used to say: The treasure was nothing but knowledge.[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/180).]]

And al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Musa and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people there. When they had settled in the dwelling, Allah revealed: "Remind them of the days of Allah." So he addressed his people and mentioned what Allah had given them of good and blessings, and reminded them when Allah saved them from the family of Pharaoh, and reminded them of the destruction of their enemy, and of how Allah had made them successors on the earth. He said: "Allah spoke to your prophet directly, and chose me for Himself, and placed upon me love from Him, and Allah has given you of everything you asked for. Your prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah." He did not leave out any blessing that He had bestowed upon them without informing them of it. A man from the Children of Israel said to him: "It is so, O Prophet of Allah; we have known what you say. Is there anyone on the earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of Allah?" He said: "No." So Allah sent Jibril to Musa, peace be upon them both, and he said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And what makes you know where I place My knowledge? Rather, there is on the shore of the sea a man who is more knowledgeable than you.'" Ibn 'Abbas said: He is al-Khidr. So Musa asked his Lord to show him him. Allah revealed to him: "Go to the sea, for you will find on the shore of the sea a fish. Take it and give it to your young servant. Then keep to the shore of the sea, and when you lose the fish and it is gone from you, there you will find the righteous servant you are seeking." When Musa, the prophet of Allah, had a long journey and was exhausted by it, he asked his young servant about the fish. His young servant, who was his attendant, said to him: ﴿"Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish, and none caused me to forget it except Satan, that I should mention it."﴾ The young man said: "I saw the fish when it took its way into the sea, making a tunnel." This amazed Musa, so he returned until he reached the rock, and he found the fish. The fish began to move in the sea and Musa followed it, and Musa was advancing his staff, parting the water with it as he followed the fish. The fish did not touch anything of the sea without it becoming dry, until it became like a rock. The prophet of Allah marveled at that, until the fish brought him to an island among the islands of the sea, where he met al-Khidr and greeted him. Al-Khidr said: "And upon you be peace. How can there be peace in this land? Who are you?" He said: "I am Musa." Al-Khidr said: "The Musa of the Children of Israel?" [He said: "Yes."][[Added from F, A, and al-Tabari.]] He welcomed him and said: "What brought you?" He said: "I have come to you ﴿so that you may teach me from what you have been taught, as guidance.﴾" ﴿He said: "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me."﴾ That is: you cannot endure that. Musa said: ﴿"You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter."﴾ He said: So he took him along, and said to him: "Do not ask me about anything I do until I explain its matter to you." That is His saying: ﴿"until I make a mention of it to you."﴾

And al-Zuhri said, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he disputed with al-Hurr ibn Qays ibn Hisn al-Fazari about the companion of Musa. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He is al-Khidr." Then Ubayy ibn Ka'b passed by them, and Ibn 'Abbas called him and said: "I and this companion of mine have disputed about the companion of Musa, who sought the way to meet him. Have you heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mention his matter?" He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah, may the peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, say: 'While Musa was among an assembly of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: "Do you know of a man more knowledgeable than you?" He said: "No." So Allah revealed to Musa: "Yes, Our servant al-Khidr." So Musa asked the way to meet him, and Allah made the fish a sign for him, and it was said to him: "When you lose the fish, it is there, so return, for you will meet him." So Musa followed the trail of the fish in the sea.' Then the young servant of Musa said to Musa: ﴿"Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? Indeed, I forgot the fish."﴾ Musa said: ﴿"That is what we were seeking." So they returned, retracing their footsteps.﴾ They found Our servant al-Khidr, and what happened between them is what Allah has recounted in His Book."[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (15/183).]]

Ibn Kathir said, on the commentary of Surah al-Kahf, verses 66–70:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us of what Musa (peace be upon him) said to that [man] [[Added from MS A.]] the scholar, who was al-Khidr. Allah had given him a knowledge that He had not disclosed to Musa, just as He had given Musa a knowledge that He had not given al-Khidr. ﴿Musa said to him: May I follow you﴾. This was a request made with gentleness, not as a demand or a compulsion. This is how a student's request to a scholar should be. His words ﴿follow you﴾ mean: accompany you and travel with you. ﴿On condition that you teach me of what you have been taught, rightly guided﴾, that is: of what Allah has taught you, something by which I may be guided in my affair, of beneficial knowledge and righteous action.

So ﴿he said﴾, al-Khidr said to Musa: ﴿Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me﴾, that is: you cannot keep company with me, because of what you will see of actions that contradict your Law. I have knowledge from the knowledge of Allah which Allah taught me, and you have knowledge from the knowledge of Allah which Allah taught you. Each of us is charged with matters from Allah that differ from those of his companion, and you cannot bear my company.

﴿And how can you have patience about that which you do not encompass in knowledge?﴾ I know that you will object to what I do, though you are excused in it, but you have not been informed of its wisdom and its hidden benefit, which I have been informed of without you.

﴿He said﴾ to him [[In MS A: "that is"]] Musa: ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, patient﴾, that is: concerning what I see of your affairs. ﴿And I will not disobey you in any order﴾, that is: I will not oppose you in anything. Then al-Khidr made a condition with him: ﴿He said: If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything﴾, that is: do not begin to ask, ﴿until I myself mention it to you﴾, that is: until I begin to tell you about it before you ask me.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub narrated to us, from Harun ibn 'Antara [[In MS F: "'Anara"]], from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Musa asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic is He, and said: "My Lord, which of Your servants is most beloved to You?" He said: "The one who remembers Me and does not forget Me." He said: "Which of Your servants is the most just in judgment?" He said: "The one who judges by the truth and does not follow desire." He said: "My Lord, which of Your servants is the most knowledgeable?" He said: "The one who seeks the knowledge of people for his own knowledge, perhaps he will hear a word that guides him to guidance or turns him away from ruin." He said: "My Lord, is there anyone on Your earth who is more knowledgeable than me?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Who is he?" He said: "al-Khidr." He said: "Where shall I seek him?" He said: "On the shore, at the rock where the fish will slip away." So Musa went out seeking him, until what Allah mentioned happened, and Musa reached him at the rock, and each of them greeted the other. Musa said to him: "I wish that you accompany me." He said: "Indeed, you will not be able to bear my company." He said: "Yes, I will." He said: "If you keep my company, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you." He said: So he journeyed with him in the sea until he reached the meeting place of the seas [[In MS F and A: "the two seas"]], and there was no place on earth with more water than it. He said: Allah sent the swallow, which began to drink from it with its beak. He said to Musa: "How much do you think this swallow has taken from this water?" He said: "How little it has taken!" He said: "O Musa, my knowledge and your knowledge, compared to the knowledge of Allah, are like the amount this swallow has drawn from this water." Musa had been saying to himself, or had spoken, that there was no one more knowledgeable than him; for this reason he was commanded to go to al-Khidr. He mentioned the full narration concerning the breaking of the ship, the killing of the boy, the repair of the wall, and his explanation of those things.

Ibn Kathir said, on the commentary of Surah al-Kahf, verses 66–70:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us of what Musa (peace be upon him) said to that [man] [[Added from MS A.]] the scholar, who was al-Khidr. Allah had given him a knowledge that He had not disclosed to Musa, just as He had given Musa a knowledge that He had not given al-Khidr. ﴿Musa said to him: May I follow you﴾. This was a request made with gentleness, not as a demand or a compulsion. This is how a student's request to a scholar should be. His words ﴿follow you﴾ mean: accompany you and travel with you. ﴿On condition that you teach me of what you have been taught, rightly guided﴾, that is: of what Allah has taught you, something by which I may be guided in my affair, of beneficial knowledge and righteous action.

So ﴿he said﴾, al-Khidr said to Musa: ﴿Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me﴾, that is: you cannot keep company with me, because of what you will see of actions that contradict your Law. I have knowledge from the knowledge of Allah which Allah taught me, and you have knowledge from the knowledge of Allah which Allah taught you. Each of us is charged with matters from Allah that differ from those of his companion, and you cannot bear my company.

﴿And how can you have patience about that which you do not encompass in knowledge?﴾ I know that you will object to what I do, though you are excused in it, but you have not been informed of its wisdom and its hidden benefit, which I have been informed of without you.

﴿He said﴾ to him [[In MS A: "that is"]] Musa: ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, patient﴾, that is: concerning what I see of your affairs. ﴿And I will not disobey you in any order﴾, that is: I will not oppose you in anything. Then al-Khidr made a condition with him: ﴿He said: If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything﴾, that is: do not begin to ask, ﴿until I myself mention it to you﴾, that is: until I begin to tell you about it before you ask me.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub narrated to us, from Harun ibn 'Antara [[In MS F: "'Anara"]], from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Musa asked his Lord, Mighty and Majestic is He, and said: "My Lord, which of Your servants is most beloved to You?" He said: "The one who remembers Me and does not forget Me." He said: "Which of Your servants is the most just in judgment?" He said: "The one who judges by the truth and does not follow desire." Ibn Jarir [[In manuscript A: "Jurayj".]] narrated from Ibn Sirin that it was al-Aylah [[In manuscript T: "al-Aykah".]]. There is also a hadith: "Until, when they came to the people of a town, base (la'iman) people," [[Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/119) through Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] meaning: stingy. ﴿So they refused to entertain them. And they found within it a wall about to collapse﴾. Attributing the "desire" here to the wall is a figure of speech (isti'arah, metaphor), since desire in inanimate things means inclination. And al-infidad (collapse) is: falling down.

* *

His saying: ﴿So he restored it﴾, meaning he returned it to a state of straightness. It has already been mentioned in the hadith that he restored it with his hands, and propped it up until he straightened its lean. This was an extraordinary act. At that point Musa said to him: ﴿If you had wished, you could have taken for it a payment﴾, meaning: since they did not entertain us, it would have been fitting that you not work for them for free. [[In manuscript T: "ittakhadta", which is an error.]] [[In manuscript T: "ya'mal majjanan".]]

﴿He said: "This is the parting between me and you."﴾ [Meaning: because you stipulated, when the boy was killed, that if you asked me about anything after that, you would not accompany me. So this is the parting between me and you.] [[Addition from manuscripts F and A.]] ﴿I will inform you of the interpretation﴾, meaning: the explanation of ﴿that over which you could not have patience﴾.

This is the explanation of the matter that had troubled Musa (peace be upon him), and whose outward appearance he had disapproved of. Allah revealed to al-Khidr (peace be upon him) its inner wisdom, so he said: "As for the boat, I damaged it only because I wanted to make it defective, [because they used to pass by a king of the oppressors who ﴿seizes every boat﴾ that was sound, i.e., good, ﴿by force﴾, so I wanted to make it defective] so that he would turn away from it because of its defect, and its owners, the poor, who had nothing else to benefit from, could benefit from it. It has been said that they were orphans."

It was narrated by Ibn Jurayj, from Wahb ibn Sulayman, from Shu'ayb al-Jiba'i, that the name of that king was Hudad ibn Budad. This was also mentioned earlier in the narration of al-Bukhari, and it is mentioned in the Torah among the descendants of "Al-Ays ibn Ishaq," and he is one of the kings specified in the Torah. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir's commentary (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 18, verses 80–81:

It has already been mentioned that this boy's name was Jaysur. In a hadith related from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "The boy whom al-Khidr killed was sealed (as a disbeliever) on the day he was sealed, a disbeliever." Ibn Jarir related it through the hadith of Ibn Ishaq, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas, with the same wording. For this reason Allah said: ﴿And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them with tyranny and disbelief﴾.

That is, his love would drive them to follow him into disbelief.

Qatadah said: His parents rejoiced at his birth, and they grieved over him when he was killed. Had he lived, his presence would have brought about their ruin. So let a person be content with the decree of Allah, for Allah's decree concerning the believer in what he dislikes is better for him than His decree concerning what he loves.

It is authentically related in a hadith: "Allah does not decree a decree for the believer except that it is good for him." And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿But it may be that you dislike a thing and it is good for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 216].

* *

And His saying [Exalted is He] ﴿so we intended that their Lord should replace him for them with one better than him in purity and nearer in mercy﴾. That is: a child more pure than this one, and they would be more merciful toward him than toward this one. This was said by Ibn Jurayj.

Qatadah said: More dutiful to his parents.

It has already been mentioned that they were given a daughter in exchange. It was also said that when al-Khidr killed him, his mother was pregnant with a Muslim boy. This was said by Ibn Jurayj.

Ibn Kathir's commentary (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 18, verses 80–81:

It has already been mentioned that this boy's name was Jaysur. In a hadith related from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "The boy whom al-Khidr killed was sealed (as a disbeliever) on the day he was sealed, a disbeliever." Ibn Jarir related it through the hadith of Ibn Ishaq, from Sa'id, from Ibn 'Abbas, with the same wording. For this reason Allah said: ﴿And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them with tyranny and disbelief﴾.

That is, his love would drive them to follow him into disbelief.

Qatadah said: His parents rejoiced at his birth, and they grieved over him when he was killed. Had he lived, his presence would have brought about their ruin. So let a person be content with the decree of Allah, for Allah's decree concerning the believer in what he dislikes is better for him than His decree concerning what he loves.

It is authentically related in a hadith: "Allah does not decree a decree for the believer except that it is good for him." And Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿But it may be that you dislike a thing and it is good for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 216].

* *

And His saying [Exalted is He] ﴿so we intended that their Lord should replace him for them with one better than him in purity and nearer in mercy﴾. That is: a child more pure than this one, and they would be more merciful toward him than toward this one. This was said by Ibn Jurayj.

Qatadah said: More dutiful to his parents.

It has already been mentioned that they were given a daughter in exchange. It was also said that when al-Khidr killed him, his mother was pregnant with a Muslim boy. This was said by Ibn Jurayj.

In this verse there is evidence that the word *qaryah* (town) can be applied to a city, since He said first, ﴿until, when they came upon the people of a town﴾ (al-Kahf 77), and here He said, ﴿and it belonged to two orphan boys in the city﴾. This is like His saying, ﴿And how many a town was stronger in might than your town which expelled you﴾ (Muhammad 13), and His saying, ﴿And they said, "Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man of the two towns?"﴾ (al-Zukhruf 31), meaning Makkah and al-Ta'if.

The meaning of the verse is that this wall was repaired only because it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them.

Ikrimah, Qatadah and others said: beneath it was buried wealth belonging to them. This is the apparent meaning of the context of the verse, and it is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him.

Al-Awfi reported from Ibn Abbas: beneath it was a treasure of knowledge. Sa'id ibn Jubayr also said this. Mujahid said: it was pages in which there was knowledge. A marfu' hadith (one traced back to the Prophet ﷺ) has also been transmitted that strengthens this view. The Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Abd al-Khaliq al-Bazzar said in his well-known Musnad: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, Bishr ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, al-Harith ibn Abd Allah al-Yahsabi narrated to us, from Ayyash ibn Abbas al-Qitbani, from Ibn Hujayrah, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who traced it back [to the Prophet ﷺ], who said: "Indeed the treasure that Allah mentioned in His Book is a sheet of solid gold on which is written: 'I am amazed at the one who has certainty in divine decree, why does he toil? I am amazed at the one who remembers the Fire, why does he laugh? I am amazed at the one who remembers death, why is he heedless? There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.'" (Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2229, Kashf al-Astar. It was also transmitted as a mawquf (attributed to a companion) through several chains from Ibn Abbas and Ali, may Allah be pleased with them, but their chains are weak.)

Bishr ibn al-Mundhir here is called the judge of al-Massisah. The Hafiz Abu Ja'far al-Uqayli said: "There is an error in his hadith." (Mizan al-I'tidal, 2/325.)

Reports from the early generations (al-Salaf) have also been narrated on this matter. Ibn Jarir said in his Tafsir: Ya'qub narrated to me, al-Hasan ibn Habib ibn Nudbah narrated to us, Salamah narrated to us, from Nu'aym al-Anbari, who was one of the companions of al-Hasan, who said: I heard al-Hasan (meaning al-Basri) say concerning His saying, ﴿and it belonged to two orphan boys﴾: "It was a sheet of gold on which was written: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. I am amazed at the one who believes in divine decree, how does he grieve? I am amazed at the one who is certain of death, how does he rejoice? I am amazed at the one who knows the world and its turning with its people, how does he feel at ease with it? There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

Yunus also narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us, Abd Allah ibn Ayyash informed me, from Umar, the client of Ghafrah, who said: "Indeed the treasure that Allah mentioned in the surah in which He mentions the Cave, ﴿and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them﴾, was a sheet of solid gold on which was written: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Wonder at the one who knows the Fire and then laughs! Wonder at the one who has certainty in divine decree and then toils! Wonder at the one who is certain of death and then feels secure! I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger."

Ahmad ibn Hazim al-Ghifari narrated to me: Hannadah bint Malik al-Shaybaniyyah narrated to us, saying: I heard my companion Hammad ibn al-Walid al-Thaqafi say: I heard Ja'far ibn Muhammad say concerning the saying of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them﴾: "It was a page of a line and a half, the third line was not completed: I am amazed at the one who is certain of provision, how does he toil? I am amazed at the one who is certain of the Reckoning, how does he neglect? I am amazed at the one who is certain of death, how does he rejoice?" And Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿And if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth, and sufficient are We as reckoners﴾ (al-Anbiya' 47). She said: It was mentioned that they were protected because of the righteousness of their father, and no righteousness of theirs was mentioned. Between them and the father through whom they were protected there were seven generations, and he was a weaver.

What these imams have mentioned, and the hadith previously cited, even if it is authentic, does not contradict the view of Ikrimah that it was wealth, because they mentioned that it was a sheet of gold, and gold contains great wealth. What they added at most is that knowledge was deposited in it, namely wisdom and admonitions. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿and their father was righteous﴾ contains evidence that a righteous man is protected in his offspring, and the blessing of his worship for them reaches them in this world and the Hereafter, through his intercession for them and raising their ranks to the highest level in Paradise, so that his eye may be comforted by them, as has come in the Qur'an and as the Sunnah has also reported. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn Abbas: They were protected because of the righteousness of their father, and no righteousness of theirs was mentioned, and it has preceded that he was the seventh father. [And Allah knows best.]

* *

His saying: ﴿So your Lord intended that they should reach their maturity and extract their treasure﴾: Here He attributed the intention to Allah, the Exalted, because their reaching puberty (al-hulm) is something none can bring about except Allah. And concerning the boy He said: ﴿So We intended that their Lord should replace him for them with one better than him﴾, and concerning the ship He said: ﴿So I intended to damage it﴾. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿a mercy from your Lord, and I did not do it of my own accord﴾ means: what I did in these three situations was only from the mercy of Allah toward those we have mentioned: the people of the ship, the two parents of the boy, and the two sons of the righteous man. ﴿And I did not do it of my own accord﴾: rather, I was commanded to do it and I was made to stand over it. This contains an indication for those who hold that al-Khidr, peace be upon him, was a prophet, in addition to his saying previously: ﴿and they found a servant of Our servants whom We had given mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Us﴾.

Others said: he was a messenger. And it was said: rather, he was a king. Al-Mawardi reported this in his Tafsir.

Many scholars held that he was not a prophet, but rather a saint (wali). And Allah knows best.

Ibn Qutaybah mentioned in al-Ma'arif that the name of al-Khidr was Balya ibn Malkan ibn Falikh ibn Amir ibn Shalikh ibn Arfakhshadh ibn Sam ibn Nuh, peace be upon him. (al-Ma'arif, p. 42.)

They said: he was called Abu al-Abbas, and was given the epithet al-Khidr, and he was one of the sons of kings. Al-Nawawi mentioned this in Tahdhib al-Asma'. He and others related two opinions about whether he remains alive until now and until the Day of Resurrection. He and Ibn al-Salah inclined toward his survival. They mentioned stories and reports about this from the early generations and others, and his mention has come in some hadiths. But none of that is authentic, and the most famous of them is the hadith of condolence, whose chain is weak.

Others among the later scholars and others preferred the opposite view and argued with His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We did not grant immortality to any human before you﴾ (al-Anbiya' 34), and with the saying of the Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Badr: "O Allah, if this band is destroyed, You will not be worshipped on earth" (narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 1763, from the hadith of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him). They also argued that it was not reported that he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, nor that he was present with him, nor that he fought alongside him. Had he been alive, he would have been among the followers of the Prophet ﷺ and his companions, because he, peace be upon him, was sent to both the two worlds, jinn and mankind. And he ﷺ said: "If Musa and Isa were alive, they would have had no choice but to follow me" (mentioned by Ibn Abi al-Izz in his commentary on al-Tahawiyyah in its context, and Shaykh Nasir al-Albani commented on it in his takhrij of al-Tahawiyyah, saying: "So it is in the original, and it seems he is pointing to the hadith mentioned by his shaykh Ibn Kathir in the Tafsir of Surat al-Kahf, with the wording: 'If Musa and Isa were alive, they would have had no choice but to follow me.' It is a preserved hadith, without the mention of 'Isa' in it. For it is munkar in my view; I have not seen it in any of its chains, and it is traced in Irwa' al-Ghalil, no. 1589.) And a little before his death he informed that no one living on the face of the earth would remain after a hundred years from that night, not even a blink of an eye, among other proofs.

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning al-Khidr, that he said: "He was only named 'al-Khidr' because he sat on a white fur, and behold, beneath him it was trembling and green." (Musnad, 2/312.)

He also transmitted it from Abd al-Razzaq. And it is also established in Sahih al-Bukhari, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "He was only named al-Khidr because he sat on a fur, and behold, it was trembling green from behind him." (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3402.)

What is meant here by *farwah* (fur) is dry grass, that is, dry stubble of plants. This was said by Abd al-Razzaq. It was also said: what is meant by this is the surface of the earth.

* *

His saying: ﴿That is the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience﴾ means: this is the explanation of what caused you distress and what you did not have the patience to wait for me to tell you about from the start. When he explained it to him, clarified it, made it plain and removed the difficulty, he said: ﴿what you could not bear﴾ (ma lam tasta'). Before that, the difficulty had been strong and heavy, so he said: ﴿I will inform you of the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience﴾. Thus he matched the heavier with the heavier and the lighter with the lighter, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So they could not scale it, nor could they make a hole in it﴾ (al-Kahf 97). Scaling it means climbing to its top, and making a hole in it is more difficult than that. So He matched each with what suits it in wording and meaning. And Allah knows best.

If it is asked: what about the young man of Musa, who was mentioned at the beginning of the story and then was not mentioned after that?

The answer is: the purpose of the context is only the story of Musa with al-Khidr and the mention of what passed between them. The young man of Musa was a follower with him. It has been stated explicitly in the hadiths previously cited, in the Sahih collections and others, that he was Yusha' ibn Nun, who governed the Children of Israel after Musa, peace be upon them both. This indicates the weakness of what Ibn Jarir reported in his Tafsir, where he said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Salamah narrated to us, Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, from al-Hasan ibn Umarah, from his father, from Ikrimah, who said: It was said to Ibn Abbas: Why do we not hear any mention of the young man of Musa, though he was with him? Ibn Abbas said, concerning what is related about the young man: He drank some of the water [so he became immortal, and the scholar took him], and he attached him to a ship, then released him into the sea, and it keeps surging with him until the Day of Resurrection. That is because he was not allowed to drink from it, but he drank. (Tafsir al-Tabari, 15/182.)

This is a weak chain. Al-Hasan is abandoned (matruk), and his father is unknown.

**Ibn Kathir's Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim (Commentary on Surah 18, Verses 83–84)**

Allah, exalted is He, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿They ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn (the Two-Horned One)﴾. O Muhammad, that is, about his story. We have already mentioned that the disbelievers of Makkah sent people to the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) to ask them about things with which they could test the Prophet (ﷺ). They said: "Ask him about a man who travelled throughout the earth, about a group of youths whose fate is unknown, and about the Spirit (al-Ruh)." So Surah al-Kahf was revealed.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) and al-Umawi in his Maghazi have cited here a narration whose chain he attributed (asnada) and which is weak, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, that a group of Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) asking about Dhul-Qarnayn, and he informed them of what they had come for at the outset. Among what he told them was: "He was a young man (shabban) from the Romans, he built Alexandria, a angel ascended with him into the sky and took him to the Barrier (al-Sadd), and he saw peoples whose faces were like the faces of dogs." There is in it great length and strangeness (nakarah), its attribution to the Prophet (ﷺ) is not sound, and at most it is among the reports of the Children of Israel (Isra'iliyyat, narratives transmitted from Jewish and Christian sources). It is remarkable that Abu Zur'ah al-Razi, despite his high standing, narrated it in full in his book Dala'il al-Nubuwwah, and this is strange of him. There is also strangeness in it that he was from the Romans. The one from the Romans was in fact Alexander the Second, son of Philip the Macedonian, from whom the Romans reckon their dating. As for the first, al-Azraqi and others have mentioned that he circumambulated the House with Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil), peace be upon him, when he first built it, and believed in him and followed him, and al-Khidr, peace be upon him, was with him. As for the second, he is Iskandar son of Philip the Macedonian the Greek, whose vizier was Aristotle (Aristatalis), the famous philosopher. And Allah knows best. It was this one from whose kingdom the Roman religious community (millat al-Rum) dates its era. He lived about three hundred years before the Messiah, peace be upon him. As for the first one mentioned in the Qur'an, he lived in the time of the Friend (Abraham), as al-Azraqi and others have mentioned, and he circumambulated the Ancient House with the Friend when Abraham, peace be upon him, built it, and he offered a sacrifice to Allah. We have mentioned a portion of his reports in our book al-Bidayah wal-Nihayah, with what is sufficient in it, and to Allah belongs all praise.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: He was a king, and he was only named Dhul-Qarnayn because the two sides of his head were of copper. He said: Some of the People of the Book said: It is because he was king of the Romans and the Persians. And some of them said: There was on his head something resembling two horns.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about Dhul-Qarnayn, and he said: He was a servant who was sincere to Allah, and Allah was sincere to him. He called his people to Allah, and they struck him on his horn (qarn), and he died. Then Allah revived him, and he called his people to Allah, and they struck him on his horn, and he died. So he was named Dhul-Qarnayn.

Shu'bah similarly narrated it from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Abu al-Tufayl, who heard Ali saying that.

It is also said that he was only named Dhul-Qarnayn because he reached the easts and the wests, from where the horn of the sun rises and sets.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, We established him in the earth﴾, that is, We gave him a great and firmly established kingdom, in which he had all the means that kings are given, of power, armies, implements of war and sieges. For this reason he ruled the easts and wests of the earth, the lands submitted to him, the kings of the servants submitted to him, and nations served him, both Arabs and non-Arabs. For this reason some of them mentioned that he was only named Dhul-Qarnayn because he reached the two horns of the sun, its rising and its setting.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We gave him from every thing a means﴾: Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, al-Suddi, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others said: That means knowledge.

Qatadah also said concerning His saying ﴿And We gave him from every thing a means﴾: The regions of the earth and its landmarks.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said concerning His saying ﴿And We gave him from every thing a means﴾: The teaching of languages. He would not invade a people without speaking to them in their language.

Ibn Lahi'ah said: Salim ibn Ghaylan narrated to me from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, that Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: You say that Dhul-Qarnayn used to tie his horses to the Pleiades (al-Thurayya)? Ka'b said to him: If I said that, then indeed Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We gave him from every thing a means﴾.

What Mu'awiyah, may Allah be pleased with him, rejected from Ka'b al-Ahbar is the correct view, and the truth is with Mu'awiyah in the rejection. Mu'awiyah used to say of Ka'b: "We used to test him with lies," meaning in what he transmitted, not that he deliberately transmitted what was not in his scripture (sahifah). But the matter concerning his scripture is that it is among the Isra'iliyyat, most of which are altered, distorted, corrupted and fabricated. We have no need at all, alongside the report of Allah and the report of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for anything from them, for a great deal of evil and widespread corruption has entered the people through them. Ka'b's interpretation of Allah's saying ﴿And We gave him from every thing a means﴾, and his citing as evidence for it what he finds in his scripture, that he used to tie his horses to the Pleiades, is neither sound nor consistent, for there is no way for a human being to reach anything of that, nor to ascend into the heavens' means. Allah has said concerning Bilqis: ﴿And she has been given of everything﴾ [al-Naml: 23], that is, of what is given to the likes of her among kings. Likewise, Dhul-Qarnayn, Allah made the means easy for him, that is, the ways and instruments for conquering regions, districts, lands and territories, breaking enemies, subduing the kings of the earth and humbling the people of polytheism. He was given from every thing that such a man needs a means, and Allah knows best.

In al-Mukhtarah by the hadith scholar Diya' al-Maqdisi, through the route of Qutaybah, from Abu 'Awanah, from Simak ibn Harb, from Habib ibn Himaz, who said: I was with Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, when a man asked him about Dhul-Qarnayn: How did he reach the easts and the wests? He said: Glory be to Allah! He subjected the clouds to him, decreed the means for him, and extended the hand to him.

He called his people to Allah, and they struck him on his horn (qarn), and he died. Then Allah revived him, and he called his people to Allah, and they struck him on his horn, and he died. So he was named Dhul-Qarnayn.

Shu'bah similarly narrated it from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Abu al-Tufayl, who heard Ali saying that.

It is also said that he was only named Dhul-Qarnayn because he reached the easts and the wests, from where the horn of the sun rises and sets.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, We established him in the earth﴾, that is, We gave him a great and firmly established kingdom, in which he had all the means that kings are given, of power, armies, implements of war and sieges. For this reason he ruled the easts and wests of the earth, the lands submitted to him, the kings of the servants submitted to him, and nations served him, both Arabs and non-Arabs. For this reason some of them mentioned that he was only named Dhul-Qarnayn because he reached the two horns of the sun, its rising and its setting.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We gave him from every thing a means﴾: Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, al-Suddi, Qatadah, al-Dahhak and others said: That means knowledge.

Qatadah also said concerning His saying ﴿And We gave him from every thing a means﴾: The regions of the earth and its landmarks.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said concerning His saying ﴿And We gave him from every thing a means﴾: The teaching of languages. He would not invade a people without speaking to them in their language.

Ibn Lahi'ah said: Salim ibn Ghaylan narrated to me from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, that Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: You say that Dhul-Qarnayn used to tie his horses to the Pleiades (al-Thurayya)? Ka'b said to him: If I said that, then indeed Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We gave him from every thing a means﴾.

What Mu'awiyah, may Allah be pleased with him, rejected from Ka'b al-Ahbar is the correct view, and the truth is with Mu'awiyah in the rejection. Mu'awiyah used to say of Ka'b: "We used to test him with lies," meaning in what he transmitted, not that he deliberately transmitted what was not in his scripture (sahifah). But the matter concerning his scripture is that it is among the Isra'iliyyat, most of which are altered, distorted, corrupted and fabricated. We have no need at all, alongside the report of Allah and the report of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for anything from them, for a great deal of evil and widespread corruption has entered the people through them. Ka'b's interpretation of Allah's saying ﴿And We gave him from every thing a means﴾, and his citing as evidence for it what he finds in his scripture, that he used to tie his horses to the Pleiades, is neither sound nor consistent, for there is no way for a human being to reach anything of that, nor to ascend into the heavens' means. Allah has said concerning Bilqis: ﴿And she has been given of everything﴾ [al-Naml: 23], that is, of what is given to the likes of her among kings. Likewise, Dhul-Qarnayn, Allah made the means easy for him, that is, the ways and instruments for conquering regions, districts, lands and territories, breaking enemies, subduing the kings of the earth and humbling the people of polytheism. He was given from every thing that such a man needs a means, and Allah knows best.

In al-Mukhtarah by the hadith scholar Diya' al-Maqdisi, through the route of Qutaybah, from Abu 'Awanah, from Simak ibn Harb, from Habib ibn Himaz, who said: I was with Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, when a man asked him about Dhul-Qarnayn: How did he reach the easts and the wests? He said: Glory be to Allah! He subjected the clouds to him, decreed the means for him, and extended the hand to him.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿So he followed a way﴾, meaning: with the means that had been provided. Mujahid said: ﴿So he followed a way﴾ means a provision and a path between the east and the west.

It is also reported from Mujahid, regarding ﴿a way﴾, that he said: a path on the earth.

Qatadah said: that is, he followed the dwelling places of the earth and its landmarks.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿So he followed a way﴾ means the dwellings.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying ﴿So he followed a way﴾, said: knowledge. Ikrimah, 'Ubayd ibn Ya'la and al-Suddi said the same.

Mattar said: landmarks and traces that existed before that.

* *

Most of that is from the fabrications of the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab), and the inventions and lies of their heretics.

* *

As for His saying ﴿But as for whoever believes﴾, that is: whoever follows us in what we call him to, the worship of Allah alone, with no partner ﴿will have the best reward﴾, that is: in the Hereafter, with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And we will speak to him of our command with ease﴾. Mujahid said: with kindness.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿So he followed a way﴾, meaning: with the means that had been provided. Mujahid said: ﴿So he followed a way﴾ means a provision and a path between the east and the west.

It is also reported from Mujahid, regarding ﴿a way﴾, that he said: a path on the earth.

Qatadah said: that is, he followed the dwelling places of the earth and its landmarks.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿So he followed a way﴾ means the dwellings.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying ﴿So he followed a way﴾, said: knowledge. Ikrimah, 'Ubayd ibn Ya'la and al-Suddi said the same.

Mattar said: landmarks and traces that existed before that.

* *

As for His saying ﴿until, when he reached the setting-place of the sun﴾, that is: he took a path until he arrived at the furthest point of the earth that one can travel to on the western side, which is the western limit of the earth. As for reaching the setting-place of the sun in the sky, that is impossible. What the storytellers and reporters mention, that he travelled across the earth for a period while the sun set behind him, is something without any reality. Most of that is from the fabrications of the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab), and the inventions and lies of their heretics.

* *

As for His saying ﴿he found it setting in a spring of black mud﴾, that is: he saw the sun, from his vantage point, setting in the Atlantic Ocean. This is the case with everyone who reaches its shore: he sees it as though it sets into it, although it never leaves the fourth heaven in which it is fixed.

The word ḥami'ah (black mud) is derived, according to one of the two recitations (qira'at, variant readings), from al-ḥam'ah, which is mud, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, I am creating a human from clay from black, altered mud﴾ [al-Hijr: 28], that is, smooth mud. Its explanation has already been given.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus narrated to me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Nafi' ibn Abi Nu'aym narrated to me: I heard 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj say: Ibn 'Abbas used to recite ﴿in a spring of black mud﴾, then explain it: "possessing mud." Nafi' said: Ka'b al-Ahbar was asked about it and he said: "You are more knowledgeable of the Qur'an than I am, but I find it in the Book that it sets in a black clay."

Similarly, others narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and Mujahid and others said likewise.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Muhammad ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Aws, from Misda', from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited to him ﴿ḥami'ah﴾.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas: "he found it setting in a spring that is hot (ḥamiyah)", meaning: warm. al-Hasan al-Basri also said the same.

Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that they are two well-known recitations, and whichever one the reciter uses, he is correct.

I say: there is no contradiction between their two meanings, for it may be warm because it is adjacent to the heat of the sun at its setting and because the rays meet it without any barrier, while it is ḥami'ah, in water and black mud, as Ka'b al-Ahbar and others said.

Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, al-Awwam informed us, a client of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr narrated to me, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at the sun when it set and said: "In the hot fire of Allah. Were it not for what restrains it by the command of Allah, it would burn what is upon the earth."

I say: Imam Ahmad also narrated it from Yazid ibn Harun. There is doubt about the attribution of this hadith to the Prophet (ﷺ), and perhaps it is from the words of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, from his two saddlebags which he found on the day of Yarmouk. And Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hajjaj ibn Hamzah narrated to us, Muhammad, meaning Ibn Bishr, narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Maymun narrated to us, Ibn Hadir informed us: it was mentioned to Ibn 'Abbas that Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan recited the verse in Surat al-Kahf as "sets in a hot spring." Ibn 'Abbas said to Mu'awiyah: "We do not recite it except as ﴿ḥami'ah﴾." Mu'awiyah asked 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr how he recited it. 'Abdullah said: "As I recited it." Ibn 'Abbas said: "I said to Mu'awiyah: 'Was the Qur'an revealed in my house?'" So he sent for Ka'b, and said to him: "Where do you find the sun setting in the Torah?" Ka'b said to him: "Ask the people of the Arabic language, for they know it better. As for me, I find the sun setting in the Torah in water and mud." And he pointed with his hand to the west. Ibn Hadir said: "If I were with you both, I would give you a statement that would increase you in insight regarding ḥami'ah." Ibn 'Abbas said: "And what is it?" I said: "It is what is transmitted from the words of Tubba', regarding how he described Dhu al-Qarnayn in his acquiring knowledge and his following of it:

He reached the east and the west, seeking the means of a matter from a wise, guided one.
So he saw the setting of the sun as it set
In a spring of mud and black slime, sunk in darkness."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "What is khulb?" I said: "Mud, in their language, meaning the language of Himyar." He said: "What is tha't?" I said: "Ḥam'ah (black mud)." He said: "What is ḥarmad?" I said: "Black." Then Ibn 'Abbas called a man or a boy and said: "Write down what this man says."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: While Ibn 'Abbas was reciting Surat al-Kahf, he recited ﴿he found it setting in a spring of black mud﴾. Ka'b said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Ka'b, I have not heard anyone recite it as it was revealed in the Torah except Ibn 'Abbas, for we find it in the Torah: it sets in a black clod."

Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il narrated to us, Hisham ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: In the Tafsir of Ibn Juraij, regarding ﴿and he found beside it a people﴾, he said: "A city which has twelve thousand gates; were it not for the voices of its people, people would hear the sinking of the sun when it sinks."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and he found beside it a people﴾, that is: a nation among the nations. They mentioned that it was a great nation of the children of Adam.

As for His saying ﴿We said: O Dhu al-Qarnayn, either you punish them, or you adopt a good course concerning them﴾, the meaning of this is: Allah, the Exalted, empowered him over them, appointed him as judge over them, granted him victory over them, and gave him the choice: if he wished, he could kill and take captives, and if he wished, he could show grace or accept ransom. So his justice and his faith were recognized, in what he manifested of justice and his clarity.

Regarding His saying ﴿As for whoever does wrong﴾, that is: whoever persists in his disbelief and his polytheism toward his Lord, ﴿We will punish him﴾. Qatadah said: with execution. al-Suddi said: he would heat brass cows for them and place them in them until they melted. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: he would send the darkness upon them, and it would enter their caves and their houses and envelop them from all their directions. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment﴾, that is: severe, painful, grievous and agonizing. In this is the affirmation of the Return and of recompense.

* *

As for His saying ﴿But as for whoever believes﴾, that is: whoever follows us in what we call him to, the worship of Allah alone, with no partner ﴿will have the best reward﴾, that is: in the Hereafter, with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And we will speak to him of our command with ease﴾. Mujahid said: with kindness.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 18, verse 89–91:

He says: Then he followed a path, and he traveled from the west of the sun to its rising place.[[In one manuscript: "from the rising place of the sun to its west."]] Whenever he passed by a nation, he subdued and overpowered them and called them to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If they obeyed him, well and good; otherwise he humiliated them and rubbed their noses in the dust, plundered their wealth and their goods, and made use of every nation whatever he needed to aid him with his armies against the people of the neighboring region.[[In one manuscript: "fighting."]] It is mentioned in the reports of the Children of Israel that he lived for one thousand six hundred years, traversing the earth in its length and breadth, until he reached the easts and the wests. When he reached the place where the sun rises from the earth, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He found it rising over a people for whom We had made no shelter against it﴾

That is: a nation ﴿for whom We had made no shelter against it﴾, meaning they had no buildings to shelter them, nor trees to shade them and screen them from the heat of the sun.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They were reddish-skinned and short in stature; their dwellings were caves, and most of their sustenance was fish.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Sahl ibn Abi al-Salt narrated to us, I heard al-Hasan, when he was asked about the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿for whom We had made no shelter against it﴾, say: Indeed their land does not bear construction. When the sun rose, they would plunge into the waters, and when the sun set, they would come out grazing like animals graze. Al-Hasan said: This is the hadith of Samurah.[[Al-Tabari also narrated it in his tafsir (16/12) through the route of Ibrahim ibn al-Mustamir, from Abu Dawud with this wording.]]

Qatadah said: It has been mentioned to us that they were in a land that grows nothing for them. When the sun rose, they would enter into holes, and when the sun passed its zenith[[In one manuscript: "when the sun set."]] they would come out to their tilling and their livelihoods.

And from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, that he said: They have no coverings; when the sun rises, it rises upon them. One of them has two ears: he spreads one as a bed and wraps himself in the other.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿He found it rising over a people for whom We had made no shelter against it﴾, he said: They are the Zanj.[[Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (1/346).]]

Ibn Jurayj said regarding His words: ﴿He found it rising over a people for whom We had made no shelter against it﴾: They never built any building in it, and no building was ever built over them in it. Whenever the sun rose, they would enter holes belonging to them until the sun passed its zenith, or they would enter the sea. That is because their land has no mountain in it. An army once came to them, and its people said to them: "Do not let the sun rise on you while you are in it." They said: "We will not leave until the sun rises. What are these bones?" They were told: "These are the corpses of an army on which the sun rose here, so they died." He said: So they fled in terror across the land.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Thus, and We had full knowledge of what was with him﴾, Mujahid and al-Suddi said: knowledge. That is: We are aware of all of his circumstances and the circumstances of his army, nothing of them being hidden from Us, even if their peoples scattered and the land cut them off from one another, for indeed He, the Exalted, ﴿nothing is hidden from Him on earth or in heaven﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 5].

Allah the Exalted says, reporting about Dhul-Qarnayn: ﴿Then he followed a way﴾, that is, then he traversed a route from the eastern regions of the earth. ﴿Until, when he reached between the two barriers﴾, and they are two mountains facing each other, between which there is a gap through which Ya'juj and Ma'juj (Gog and Magog) emerge upon the lands of the Turks, and they spread corruption among them, destroying the crops and the offspring. Ya'juj and Ma'juj are from the progeny of Adam, upon him be peace, as is established in the two Sahihs: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, says: O Adam! He says: Here I am at Your service and obedience. He says: Send forth the company of the Fire. He says: What is the company of the Fire? He says: Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine to the Fire, and one to Paradise. At that time the young child will turn grey, every pregnant woman will drop her burden, and it will be said: Indeed among you are two nations, which have never been part of anything except that they increased it: Ya'juj and Ma'juj" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6530) and Sahih Muslim no. (222), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

Al-Nawawi (may Allah have mercy on him), in his commentary on Muslim, related from some people that Ya'juj and Ma'juj were created from the semen that came out of Adam and mixed with the dust, and so they were created from that. Accordingly, they would be created from Adam and not from Hawwa' (Eve). This is a very strange view, for there is no proof for it, neither from reason nor from transmission, and one may not rely here on what some of the People of the Book relate, because of the fabricated narrations they possess. And Allah knows best.

In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, from Samurah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Nuh had three sons: Sam, the father of the Arabs; Ham, the father of the black peoples; and Yafith, the father of the Turks." Some scholars said: These are from the offspring of Yafith, the father of the Turks. He said: These people were named Turks only because they were left (turikū) behind the barrier on this side; otherwise they are relatives of those (Ya'juj and Ma'juj), but among those there was transgression, corruption and audacity. Ibn Jarir has mentioned here, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, a long and marvellous report about the journey of Dhul-Qarnayn, his building of the barrier, and how what happened to him unfolded, and in it there is great length, strangeness and oddity regarding their forms and attributes, their height, the shortness of some of them, and their ears [[Tafsir al-Tabari (16/14).]]. Ibn Abi Hatim related strange hadiths on this matter whose chains are not sound. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He found, beside them, a people who could hardly understand a word﴾ [i.e.]: because their speech was incomprehensible and they were remote from people.

﴿They said: O Dhul-Qarnayn! Indeed Ya'juj and Ma'juj are corrupters in the land, so shall we pay you a tribute (kharj)?﴾ Ibn Jurayj related from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas: a great reward. The meaning is that they wished to gather for him wealth from among them, which they would give him, so that he would make a barrier between them and them. Dhul-Qarnayn said, with chastity, piety, righteousness and intent for good: ﴿What my Lord has established me in is better﴾, that is: the dominion and authority that Allah has given me is better for me than what you gather, just as Sulayman, upon him be peace, said: ﴿Will you provide me with wealth? What Allah has given me is better than what He has given you; rather, you rejoice in your gift﴾ [An-Naml: 36]. Likewise Dhul-Qarnayn said: what I am in is better than what you offer; but help me ﴿with strength﴾, that is, with your labour and building tools. ﴿I will set between you and them a barrier. Bring me blocks of iron﴾. Zubar is the plural of zubrah, which is a piece of it, as said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah. It is like a brick; it is said that each brick weighs a qintar by the Damascene measure, or more than that.

﴿Until, when he had made level between the two cliffs﴾, that is: he placed it layer upon layer from the foundation until it reached the tops of the two mountains in length and breadth. They differed over the measure of its width and length, with various opinions. ﴿He said: Blow﴾, that is: kindle the fire upon it until all of it became fire. ﴿He said: Bring me molten copper to pour over it﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: it is copper (nuhas). Some added: melted. They cite His saying: ﴿And We caused a spring of molten copper to flow for him﴾ [Saba: 12], and for this reason it is likened to striped cloth.

Ibn Jarir said: Bishr related to us, Yazid related to us, Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah who said: It was mentioned to us that a man said: O Messenger of Allah, you have seen the barrier of Ya'juj and Ma'juj. He said: "Describe it to me." He said: Like striped cloth, a black stripe and a red stripe. He said: "You have seen it." This is a mursal hadith. [[It has been transmitted with connected chains through several routes: Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir (as in the takhrij of al-Kashshaf, 2/312) through Abu al-Jamahir Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from a man, from Abu Bakrah al-Thaqafi, that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: Indeed I have seen it, and he mentioned something similar. Al-Bazzar in his Musnad (as in the takhrij of al-Kashshaf, 2/313) through 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Na'amah, from Yusuf ibn Abi Maryam, from Abu Bakrah, similar but longer. Ibn Mardawayh also related through Sufyan, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from a man of Madinah that he said to the Prophet (ﷺ), and mentioned something similar.]]

The Caliph al-Wathiq, in his reign, sent one of his amirs and dispatched with him a secret army, so that they might look at the barrier, observe it and describe it to him when they returned. They travelled from land to land and from kingdom to kingdom until they reached it, and they saw its construction of iron and copper. They mentioned that they saw in it a great gate, upon which were great locks, and they saw the remainder of the bricks and the work in a tower there. They said that near it were guards from the neighbouring kings, and that it is lofty, towering, and that neither it nor the mountains around it can be scaled. Then they returned to their country; their absence had lasted more than two years, and they witnessed terrors and wonders.

Then Allah the Exalted said:

Ibn Kathir's commentary (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah al-Kahf, verses 97–99:

He, exalted is He, says, reporting about Ya'juj and Ma'juj (Gog and Magog), that they were not able to climb up over this barrier [[In MS F and A: "yasʿadū min" (that they climb up from)]], nor were they able to breach it from its base. Since climbing over it was easier than breaching it, He answered each case with what suits it, saying: ﴿So they could not scale it, nor could they make a hole in it.﴾ This is evidence that they were unable to breach it, or any part of it.

As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad:

Rawh narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Ya'juj and Ma'juj dig through the barrier every day, until, when they nearly see the rays of the sun, the one in charge of them says: 'Go back, and you will dig through it tomorrow.' They return to it as strong as they were, until, when their term is fulfilled and Allah wills to send them against the people, [they dig until they nearly see the rays of the sun]. [[Addition from MSS F, A, and the Musnad.]] The one in charge of them says: 'Go back, and you will dig through it tomorrow, if Allah wills.' He makes the exception, and they return to it while it is in the state in which they left it. They dig through it and come out against the people, drink up the water, and the people take refuge from them in their fortresses. They shoot their arrows toward the sky, and the arrows come back stained with blood, and they say: 'We have subdued the people of the earth and overcome the people of heaven.' Then Allah sends upon them a plague [naghaf] in their necks, and it kills them with it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, the beasts of the earth will grow fat and be well nourished from their flesh and blood."

Ahmad also narrated it from Hasan, that is Ibn Musa al-Ashyab, from Sufyan, from Qatadah, with the same wording. Ibn Majah narrated it likewise, from Azhar ibn Marwan, from 'Abd al-A'la, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, who said: "Rafi' narrated [to us]." Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it through the hadith of Abu 'Awanah, from Qatadah, [[Sunan Ibn Majah no. 4080; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3153.]] and then said: "It is gharib (singular); we do not know it except through this route."

Its isnad is strong, but there is an objectionable element (nakarah) in its being traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), because the apparent meaning of the verse requires that they were unable to scale it or breach it, due to the firmness of its construction, its solidity and its strength. However, this has been reported from Ka'b al-Ahbar: that before their emergence they would come to it and lick it until only a little of it remained, and they would say: "Tomorrow we will break through it." Then they would come the next day and find it had returned as it was, so they would lick it again until only a little remained, and say the same, and in the morning it would be as it was. Then they would lick it and say: "Tomorrow we will break through it." They are inspired to say: "If Allah wills." They would then wake up to find it as they had left it, and they would break through it. This is consistent (mutta'jih), and perhaps Abu Hurayrah received it from Ka'b, for he often sat with him and talked with him. Abu Hurayrah narrated it, and some of the transmitters from him mistakenly thought it was marfu' (traced to the Prophet), so they traced it to him. And Allah knows best.

What confirms what we have said, that they were unable to breach it or any part of it, and confirms the objection to this marfu' report, is the statement of Imam Ahmad:

Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from [Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, from Habibah bint Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan, from her mother Umm Habibah, from] [[Addition from MSS F, A, and the Musnad.]] Zaynab bint Jahsh, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ). [Sufyan said: "Four women."] She said: The Prophet (ﷺ) woke up from his sleep, his face flushed, and he was saying: "There is no god but Allah! Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near! Today an opening the size of this has been made in the barrier of Ya'juj and Ma'juj." And he made a circle with his fingers. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we be destroyed while the righteous are among us?" He said: "Yes, when wickedness (khabath) increases."

Rawh narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Ya'juj and Ma'juj dig through the barrier every day, until, when they nearly see the rays of the sun, the one in charge of them says: 'Go back, and you will dig through it tomorrow.' All of this is before the Day of Resurrection and after the Dajjal, as will be explained, if Allah the Exalted wills, at His saying: ﴿Until, when Ya'juj and Ma'juj are released, and they swarm from every mound. And the true promise draws near﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 96–97]. And similarly He says here: ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another, and the Horn will be blown, and We will gather them in a gathering﴾.

Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another,﴾ "This is the beginning of the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and the Horn is blown﴾ immediately after that, ﴿and We gather them in a gathering.﴾"

Others said: rather, what is meant by His saying: ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another﴾ is that on the Day of Resurrection mankind and the jinn will mix together.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Muhammad ibn Humayd, from Ya'qub al-Qummi, from Harun ibn 'Antarah, from a shaykh of the Banu Fazarah, regarding His saying: ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another﴾ that he said: "When mankind and the jinn surge, Iblis says: 'I will show you the knowledge of this matter.' He sets off toward the east and finds the angels have covered the earth. Then he sets off toward the west and finds the angels have covered the earth, and he says: 'There is no escape.' Then he sets off right and left to the farthest parts of the earth, and finds the angels have covered the earth, and he says: 'There is no escape.' While he is in this state, a path like a thread appears to him, and he and his offspring take it. While they are on it, they come upon the Fire, and Allah sends out one of the guardians of the Fire, who says: 'O Iblis, did you not have a station with your Lord? Were you not in the Gardens?' He says: 'This is not a day for reproach. If Allah had imposed on me an obligation, I would have worshipped Him in it with a worship no one of His creation has ever performed.' The guardian says: 'Indeed Allah has imposed an obligation on you.' He says: 'What is it?' The guardian says: 'He commands you to enter the Fire.' He hesitates, so the guardian pushes him and his offspring with his wings and casts them into the Fire. The Fire then lets out a roar, and no angel brought near nor prophet sent will remain except that he falls to his knees." [[Tafsir al-Tabari 16/23.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it likewise from the hadith of Ya'qub al-Qummi. He narrated it by another route from Ya'qub, from Harun, from 'Antarah, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another﴾ He said: "The jinn and the mankind, some of them surging over others."

Al-Tabarani said: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn al-'Abbas al-Asfahani narrated to us, Abu Mas'ud Ahmad ibn al-Furat narrated to us, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated to us, al-Mughirah ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Wahb ibn Jabir, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed Ya'juj and Ma'juj are from the offspring of Adam. If they were released, they would corrupt the livelihoods of the people. No man among them dies without leaving behind a thousand or more of his offspring. And behind them are three nations: Ta'wil, Tayas, and Mansak." [[The hadith is in Musnad al-Tayalisi no. 2282. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/6): "Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Kabir and al-Awsat, and its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)." Note: al-Majma' has "Ta'wil, Tarus, and Mansak"; al-Tayalisi has "Ta'wil, Tarus, Tarlis, and Mansak"; al-Matalib al-'Aliyah has "Ta'wil, Tarus, and Nasak."]] This hadith is gharib, rather munkar and weak.

Al-Nasa'i narrated through the hadith of Shu'bah, from al-Nu'man ibn Salim, from 'Amr ibn Aws, from his father, from his grandfather Aws ibn Abi Aws, as a marfu' report: "Indeed Ya'juj and Ma'juj have women, and they have intercourse with whomever they wish, and trees, and they impregnate whatever they wish. No man among them dies without leaving behind a thousand or more of his offspring." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 11334.]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And the Horn is blown﴾: the Horn (al-sur), as it came in the hadith, is "a horn which is blown into." The one who blows into it is Israfil, peace be upon him, as has already been mentioned in the hadith at length, and the hadiths on it are numerous.

And there is a hadith from 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas and Abu Sa'id, as a marfu' report: "How can I be at ease, when the holder of the horn has put the horn to his mouth, bowed his forehead, and is listening for when he will be commanded?" They said: "How should we say?" He said: "Say: 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In Allah we have put our trust.'" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. 2431, who said: "This is a hasan hadith."]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And We gathered them in a gathering﴾ That is, We brought all of them to the reckoning. ﴿Say: Indeed the first and the last will surely be gathered for the appointed time of a known Day﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 49–50], ﴿And We gathered them, and We left none of them behind﴾ [Al-Kahf: 47].

Allah the Exalted says, informing about what He will do to the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection: "On that Day We shall present Hell to the disbelievers" (18:100). That is, He will bring it forth and make it manifest to them, so that they may see the punishment and torment in it before entering it, and that this may be more effective in hastening distress and grief for them.

In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hell will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, pulled by seventy thousand bridles, with each bridle held by seventy thousand angels [dragging it]." [[Addition from MS F, MS A, and Muslim.]] [[Sahih Muslim, no. (2842).]]

Then He said, informing about them: "Those whose eyes were under a covering from My remembrance" (18:101). That is, they feigned blindness, paid no heed, and made themselves deaf to accepting guidance and following the truth, as He said: "And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful, We appoint for him a devil, and he is his companion" (43:36). And He said here: "And they were unable to hear" (18:101), meaning they did not comprehend from Allah His command and His prohibition.

Then He said: "Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as protectors besides Me?" (18:102). That is, do they believe that this will be valid for them and that they will benefit from it? "No! They will reject their worship and will become opponents to them" (19:82). Therefore, He informed that He has prepared for them Hell as their abode on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 18, verses 103–106:

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Mus'ab, who said: I asked my father, meaning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, about: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in their deeds?﴾ Are they the Harouriyya (Kharijites)? He said: No. They are the Jews and the Christians. As for the Jews, they denied Muhammad (ﷺ). As for the Christians, they disbelieved in Paradise and said: There is no food in it and no drink. The Harouriyya are those who break the covenant of Allah after its affirmation. Sa'd (may Allah be pleased with him) used to call them "the wicked" (al-fasiqin). [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4728.]

'Ali ibn Abi Talib [in one manuscript: "Talhah"] and al-Dahhak, and others besides them, said: They are the Harouriyya.

The meaning of this from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) is that this noble verse includes the Harouriyya just as it includes the Jews, the Christians and others. It was not revealed specifically about these groups alone, nor about this one group alone. Rather, it is more general than this, for this verse is Meccan, revealed before the address to the Jews and Christians and before the Kharijites existed at all. It is general to everyone who worships Allah in a manner other than the accepted way, thinking that he is correct in it and that his deed is accepted, while he is mistaken and his deed is rejected. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Faces that Day will be humbled, labouring and weary, roasting in a scorching Fire﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 88:2–4]. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan 25:23]. And the Exalted said: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾ [al-Nur 24:39].

He said regarding this noble verse: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you﴾, i.e., tell you, ﴿of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ Then He explained who they are, saying: ﴿Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world﴾, i.e., they did deeds that were void, not according to a lawful, prescribed, accepted, and approved way, ﴿while they think they are doing good work﴾, i.e., they believe that they are upon something, and that they are accepted and beloved.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him﴾, i.e., they denied the signs of Allah in this world and His proofs which He established for His oneness and the truthfulness of His messengers, and they denied the Last Abode. ﴿So We will not establish for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾, i.e., We will not make their scales heavy, because they are empty of good.

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, al-Mughirah informed us, Abu al-Zinad narrated to me, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed, a man, great and fat, will come on the Day of Resurrection, but he will not weigh the wing of a mosquito with Allah." And he said: "Recite if you wish: ﴿So We will not establish for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾."

And from Yahya ibn Bukayr, from Mughirah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Zinad, the like of it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4729.]

Thus he (al-Bukhari) mentioned it from Yahya ibn Bukayr as a mu'allaq (suspended narration). Muslim narrated it from Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yahya ibn Bukayr, with the same wording. [Sahih Muslim, no. 2785.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Walid narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to us, from Salih, the freedman of al-Tawamah, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man who eats much, drinks much, and is great will be brought, and he will be weighed against a single grain, and it will not weigh it." He said: And he recited: ﴿So We will not establish for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾.

Similarly, Ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Abu al-Salt, from Abu al-Zinad, from Salih, the freedman of al-Tawamah, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) report, and he mentioned it with the wording of al-Bukhari, the same. [Tafsir al-Tabari, 16/29.]

Al-Bazzar, Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq, said: 'Abbas ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Awn ibn 'Imarah narrated to us, Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us, from Wasil, from 'Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when a man from Quraysh came, strutting in a garment of his. When he stood before the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "O Buraydah, this is one of those for whom Allah will not establish any weight on the Day of Resurrection." [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2956, Kashf al-Astar.]

Then he (al-Bazzar) said: Wasil, the freedman of Abu 'Anbasah [in one manuscript: "the freedman of 'Ubayd"; in another: "the freedman of Abu 'Uyaynah"], was alone in narrating it, and 'Awn ibn 'Imarah [in one manuscript: "'Amir"] is not a reliable memorizer (hafiz), and it was not corroborated by others in this.

Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shimr [in one manuscript: "Samurah"], from Abu Yahya, from Ka'b, who said: A great, tall man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, but he will not weigh the wing of a mosquito with Allah. Recite: ﴿So We will not establish for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari, 16/29.]

* *

His saying: ﴿That is their recompense: Hell, because they disbelieved﴾, i.e., We only requited them with this recompense, Hell, because of their disbelief and their taking the signs of Allah and His messengers in mockery. They ridiculed them and denied them with the most severe denial.
