Al-Bazzar, Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq, said: 'Abbas ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Awn ibn 'Imarah narrated to us, Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us, from Wasil, from 'Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when a man from Quraysh came, strutting in a garment of his. When he stood before the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "O Buraydah, this is one of those for whom Allah will not establish any weight on the Day of Resurrection." [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2956, Kashf al-Astar.]

Then he (al-Bazzar) said: Wasil, the freedman of Abu 'Anbasah [in one manuscript: "the freedman of 'Ubayd"; in another: "the freedman of Abu 'Uyaynah"], was alone in narrating it, and 'Awn ibn 'Imarah [in one manuscript: "'Amir"] is not a reliable memorizer (hafiz), and it was not corroborated by others in this.

Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shimr [in one manuscript: "Samurah"], from Abu Yahya, from Ka'b, who said: A great, tall man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, but he will not weigh the wing of a mosquito with Allah. Recite: ﴿So We will not establish for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari, 16/29.]

* *

His saying: ﴿That is their recompense: Hell, because they disbelieved﴾, i.e., We only requited them with this recompense, Hell, because of their disbelief and their taking the signs of Allah and His messengers in mockery. They ridiculed them and denied them with the most severe denial.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 18, verses 103–106:

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Mus'ab, who said: I asked my father, meaning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, about: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in their deeds?﴾ Are they the Harouriyya (Kharijites)? He said: No. They are the Jews and the Christians. As for the Jews, they denied Muhammad (ﷺ). As for the Christians, they disbelieved in Paradise and said: There is no food in it and no drink. The Harouriyya are those who break the covenant of Allah after its affirmation. Sa'd (may Allah be pleased with him) used to call them "the wicked" (al-fasiqin). [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4728.]

'Ali ibn Abi Talib [in one manuscript: "Talhah"] and al-Dahhak, and others besides them, said: They are the Harouriyya.

The meaning of this from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) is that this noble verse includes the Harouriyya just as it includes the Jews, the Christians and others. It was not revealed specifically about these groups alone, nor about this one group alone. Rather, it is more general than this, for this verse is Meccan, revealed before the address to the Jews and Christians and before the Kharijites existed at all. It is general to everyone who worships Allah in a manner other than the accepted way, thinking that he is correct in it and that his deed is accepted, while he is mistaken and his deed is rejected. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Faces that Day will be humbled, labouring and weary, roasting in a scorching Fire﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 88:2–4]. And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan 25:23]. And the Exalted said: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing﴾ [al-Nur 24:39].

He said regarding this noble verse: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you﴾, i.e., tell you, ﴿of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾ Then He explained who they are, saying: ﴿Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world﴾, i.e., they did deeds that were void, not according to a lawful, prescribed, accepted, and approved way, ﴿while they think they are doing good work﴾, i.e., they believe that they are upon something, and that they are accepted and beloved.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him﴾, i.e., they denied the signs of Allah in this world and His proofs which He established for His oneness and the truthfulness of His messengers, and they denied the Last Abode. ﴿So We will not establish for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾, i.e., We will not make their scales heavy, because they are empty of good.

Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, al-Mughirah informed us, Abu al-Zinad narrated to me, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed, a man, great and fat, will come on the Day of Resurrection, but he will not weigh the wing of a mosquito with Allah." And he said: "Recite if you wish: ﴿So We will not establish for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾."

And from Yahya ibn Bukayr, from Mughirah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from Abu al-Zinad, the like of it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4729.]

Thus he (al-Bukhari) mentioned it from Yahya ibn Bukayr as a mu'allaq (suspended narration). Muslim narrated it from Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yahya ibn Bukayr, with the same wording. [Sahih Muslim, no. 2785.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Walid narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to us, from Salih, the freedman of al-Tawamah, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man who eats much, drinks much, and is great will be brought, and he will be weighed against a single grain, and it will not weigh it." He said: And he recited: ﴿So We will not establish for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾.

Similarly, Ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Abu al-Salt, from Abu al-Zinad, from Salih, the freedman of al-Tawamah, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) report, and he mentioned it with the wording of al-Bukhari, the same. [Tafsir al-Tabari, 16/29.]

Al-Bazzar, Ahmad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Khaliq, said: 'Abbas ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Awn ibn 'Imarah narrated to us, Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us, from Wasil, from 'Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when a man from Quraysh came, strutting in a garment of his. When he stood before the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "O Buraydah, this is one of those for whom Allah will not establish any weight on the Day of Resurrection." [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 2956, Kashf al-Astar.]

Then he (al-Bazzar) said: Wasil, the freedman of Abu 'Anbasah [in one manuscript: "the freedman of 'Ubayd"; in another: "the freedman of Abu 'Uyaynah"], was alone in narrating it, and 'Awn ibn 'Imarah [in one manuscript: "'Amir"] is not a reliable memorizer (hafiz), and it was not corroborated by others in this.

Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shimr [in one manuscript: "Samurah"], from Abu Yahya, from Ka'b, who said: A great, tall man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, but he will not weigh the wing of a mosquito with Allah. Recite: ﴿So We will not establish for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari, 16/29.]

* *

His saying: ﴿That is their recompense: Hell, because they disbelieved﴾, i.e., We only requited them with this recompense, Hell, because of their disbelief and their taking the signs of Allah and His messengers in mockery. They ridiculed them and denied them with the most severe denial.

Ibn Kathir said:

Allah, exalted is He, informs about His happy servants, those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and affirmed what he brought, that for them are the Gardens of Firdaws (the highest paradise).

Mujahid said: "al-Firdaws is al-bustan (the garden) in Roman (Greek) language."

Ka'b, al-Suddi and al-Dahhak said: "It is the garden in which there are grapevines."

Abu Umamah said: "al-Firdaws is the navel (center) of Paradise."

Qatadah said: "al-Firdaws is the elevated part (rabwah) of Paradise, its middle and its best part."

This has been related in a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ) report from the route of Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Samurah, from the Prophet ﷺ: "al-Firdaws is the elevated part of Paradise, its middle and its best." [Related by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7/213) through Abu al-Jamahir, from Sa'id ibn Bashir.] Similarly, Isma'il ibn Muslim related it from al-Hasan, from Samurah, as marfu'. It has also been related from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, as marfu', with similar wording. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, transmitted all of this. [Tafsir al-Tabari (16/30). Related by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. 3174, through Rawh ibn 'Ubadah, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."]

In the Two Sahihs: "When you ask Allah for Paradise, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the highest of Paradise and its middle, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 7423.]

As for His saying ﴿nuzulan﴾ (as hospitality), meaning a welcoming provision, since an-nuzul is hospitality.

As for His saying ﴿khalidina fiha﴾, meaning: remaining and dwelling therein, never departing from it forever. ﴿La yabghuna 'anha hiwalan﴾ means: they do not choose anything other than it, and do not love anything besides it, as the poet said:

"I have taken the heart's core as my abode; I seek no other, nor do I turn from my love for it..."

In His saying ﴿la yabghuna 'anha hiwalan﴾ there is an indication of their desire for it and their love of it. Though one might suppose that whoever dwells permanently in a place would tire of it or become bored, He informs that despite this constant, everlasting abiding, they do not choose any change, transfer, departure, journey, or substitute from that dwelling.

Ibn Kathir said:

Allah, exalted is He, informs about His happy servants, those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and affirmed what he brought, that for them are the Gardens of Firdaws (the highest paradise).

Mujahid said: "al-Firdaws is al-bustan (the garden) in Roman (Greek) language."

Ka'b, al-Suddi and al-Dahhak said: "It is the garden in which there are grapevines."

Abu Umamah said: "al-Firdaws is the navel (center) of Paradise."

Qatadah said: "al-Firdaws is the elevated part (rabwah) of Paradise, its middle and its best part."

This has been related in a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet ﷺ) report from the route of Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Samurah, from the Prophet ﷺ: "al-Firdaws is the elevated part of Paradise, its middle and its best." [Related by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7/213) through Abu al-Jamahir, from Sa'id ibn Bashir.] Similarly, Isma'il ibn Muslim related it from al-Hasan, from Samurah, as marfu'. It has also been related from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, as marfu', with similar wording. Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, transmitted all of this. [Tafsir al-Tabari (16/30). Related by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. 3174, through Rawh ibn 'Ubadah, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."]

In the Two Sahihs: "When you ask Allah for Paradise, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the highest of Paradise and its middle, and from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 7423.]

As for His saying ﴿nuzulan﴾ (as hospitality), meaning a welcoming provision, since an-nuzul is hospitality.

As for His saying ﴿khalidina fiha﴾, meaning: remaining and dwelling therein, never departing from it forever. ﴿La yabghuna 'anha hiwalan﴾ means: they do not choose anything other than it, and do not love anything besides it, as the poet said:

"I have taken the heart's core as my abode; I seek no other, nor do I turn from my love for it..."

In His saying ﴿la yabghuna 'anha hiwalan﴾ there is an indication of their desire for it and their love of it. Though one might suppose that whoever dwells permanently in a place would tire of it or become bored, He informs that despite this constant, everlasting abiding, they do not choose any change, transfer, departure, journey, or substitute from that dwelling.

Allah the Exalted says: Say, O Muhammad: "If the sea were ink for the pen with which the words of my Lord are written, and His wisdoms and His signs which point to Him, ﴿the sea would be exhausted﴾, that is, the sea would run dry ﴿before the writing of that was finished. And even if We brought the like of it﴾, that is, another sea like it, and then another, and so on, seas to replenish it, with which to write, ﴿the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if whatever trees upon the earth were pens and the sea, replenished thereafter by seven seas, [were ink], the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise﴾ [Luqman: 27].

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: The likeness of the knowledge of all the servants in comparison to the knowledge of Allah is like a drop of water from all the seas. And Allah revealed this: ﴿Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as replenishment﴾.

He means: even if the sea were ink for the words of Allah, and all the trees were pens, the pens would break and the water of the sea would run out, while the words of Allah would remain established, not perished by anything; because no one can truly measure His measure or praise Him as He deserves, until He Himself praises Himself. Our Lord is as He says, and above what we say. Indeed, the likeness of the pleasures of this world, from its beginning to its end, compared to the pleasures of the Hereafter, is like a grain of mustard in the midst of the entire earth.

Al-Tabarani narrated through Hisham ibn 'Ammar, from Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, from 'Amr ibn Qays al-Kufi, that he heard Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan say: "This is the last verse that was revealed" [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (19/392). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/14): "Its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)."]].

Allah says to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) [[In T, F, A: "may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him."]]: ﴿Say﴾ to these polytheists who deny your message: ﴿I am only a human being like you﴾. Whoever claims that I am a liar, let him bring something like what I have brought. I do not know the unseen regarding what I have told you of the past, such as what you asked about: the story of the People of the Cave and the account of Dhu al-Qarnayn, which corresponds to reality, except what Allah has informed me of. ﴿And I tell you that your God﴾, whom I call you to worship, ﴿is one God﴾ with no partner, ﴿so whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾, that is, hopes for His reward and good recompense, ﴿let him do righteous deeds﴾, meaning what conforms to the law of Allah, ﴿and let him not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾. This is what is intended to be for the sake of Allah alone, with no partner. These two are the two pillars of accepted deeds: they must be sincerely for Allah and correct according to the Shari'ah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [[Addition from F, A.]].

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Ma'mar, from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Tawus, who said: A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I stand in positions seeking the face of Allah, and I love that my station be seen." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not answer him at all, until this verse was revealed: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾.

Similarly, Mujahid and others narrated it in mursal form.

Al-A'mash said: Hamzah Abu 'Umarah, client of the Banu Hashim, narrated to us, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: A man came to 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit and said: "Inform me about what I ask you: Do you see a man who prays seeking the face of Allah while loving to be praised, and fasts seeking the face of Allah while loving to be praised, and gives charity seeking the face of Allah while loving to be praised, and performs Hajj seeking the face of Allah while loving to be praised?" 'Ubadah said: "He has nothing." Allah the Exalted says: "I am the best partner. Whoever has a partner with Me in an act, it belongs entirely to that partner; I have no need of it." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (16/32).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, Kathir ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Rubayh ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa'id al-Khudri, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "We used to take turns with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), spending the night with him when he had a need, or when something happened at night, and he would send us. The volunteers and the watchmen increased, and we would converse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us and said: 'What is this secret talk? [Did I not forbid you from secret talk?]' [[Addition from F, A, and the Musnad.]]" He said: We said: "We repent to Allah, O Prophet of Allah; we were only discussing the Messiah and were afraid of him." He said: "Shall I inform you of what I fear for you more than the Messiah?" We said: "Yes." He said: "Hidden shirk: that a man stands to pray so that another man may see him." [[al-Musnad (3/30). Its chain includes Rubayh ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, of whom Ahmad said: "He is not well known," and al-Bukhari said: "Munkar al-hadith (weak in narrations)."]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us, 'Abd al-Hamid (i.e., Ibn Bahram) narrated to us, who said: Shahr ibn Hawshab said: Ibn Ghanm said: When Abu al-Darda' and I entered the Mosque of al-Jabiyah, we met 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit. He took my right hand with his left, and Abu al-Darda's left hand with his right, and went out walking between us while we were conversing privately, and Allah knows what we were conversing about. 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit said: "If the lifespan of one of you two, or both of you, is prolonged, you will soon see a man from the midst of the Muslims, meaning from the middle, who recites the Qur'an in the manner of Muhammad (ﷺ), repeats it and begins it again, makes lawful what is lawful and forbids what is forbidden, and stands at its stations. He will not be effective among you except as the head of a dead donkey is ineffective." He said: "While we were like that, Shaddad ibn Aws, may Allah be pleased with him, and 'Awf ibn Malik came by and sat with us. Shaddad said: 'The thing I fear most for you, O people, is what I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The hidden desire and shirk."' 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit and Abu al-Darda' said: 'O Allah, forgive us. Had not the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told us that Satan has despaired of being worshipped in the Arabian Peninsula? As for the hidden desire, we know it: it is the desires of this world, of women and their pleasures. So what is this shirk you warn us about, O Shaddad?' Shaddad said: 'Tell me, if you saw a man praying for another man, or fasting for another man, [or giving charity for him, do you think he has committed shirk?] They said: "Yes, by Allah, whoever prays or fasts for a man, or gives charity for him, has committed shirk."' [[Addition from F, A, and the Musnad.]] Shaddad said: 'I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [say] [[Addition from F, A, and the Musnad.]]: Whoever prays showing off has committed shirk, whoever fasts showing off has committed shirk, and whoever gives charity showing off has committed shirk.'" Then 'Awf ibn Malik said: "Will Allah not single out the deed, of all that deed, which was sought for His face, and accept what was purely for Him and leave what was associated with Him?" Shaddad then said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Allah says: I am the best partner for whoever associates someone with Me. Whoever associates anything with Me, his deed, small and great, belongs to his partner whom he associated with Me, and I am free of it.'" [[al-Musnad (4/125).]]

Another route for part of it: Imam Ahmad said: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad told me, 'Ubadah ibn Nusayy informed us, from Shaddad ibn Aws, may Allah be pleased with him, that he wept. He was asked: "What makes you weep?" He said: "Something I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying [and I recalled it], and it made me weep. I heard the Messenger of Allah say: 'I fear for my ummah shirk and hidden desire.'" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, will your ummah commit shirk [after you?]" He said: "Yes. Indeed they will not worship the sun, the moon, a stone, or an idol, but they will show off with their deeds. Hidden desire is when one of them fasts in the morning, then a desire of his desires presents itself to him, and he abandons his fast."

It was narrated by Ibn Majah from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Dhakwan, from 'Ubadah ibn Nusayy, with it [[al-Musnad (4/123) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4305).]]. In 'Ubadah there is weakness, and his hearing from Shaddad is questionable.

Another hadith: al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Ja'far al-Ahmar narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Thabit narrated to us, Qays ibn Abi Husayn narrated to us, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah says on the Day of Resurrection: I am the best partner. Whoever associates anyone with Me, it belongs entirely to that one."

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, I heard al-'Ala' narrate from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who related it from his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, that He said: "I am the best of partners. Whoever performs a deed in which he associates another with Me, I am free of him, and it belongs to the one he associated." This is a narration that is unique in this route [[al-Musnad (2/301). Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it in his Sahih no. (938) through Muhammad ibn Ja'far.]].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yunus narrated to us, Layth narrated to us, from Yazid, i.e., Ibn al-Had, from 'Amr, from Mahmud ibn Labid, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The thing I fear most for you is the minor shirk." They said: "What is the minor shirk, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Showing off. Allah will say on the Day of Resurrection when people are recompensed for their deeds: Go to those you used to show off to in the world, and see whether you find any reward with them." [[al-Musnad (5/428). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/102): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]]

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, 'Abd al-Hamid (i.e., Ibn Ja'far) informed us, my father informed me, from Ziyad ibn Mina', from Abu Sa'id ibn Abi Fadalah al-Ansari, who was one of the Companions, that he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Allah gathers the first and the last for the Day of Resurrection, a day about which there is no doubt, a caller will call out: Whoever associated anyone with Allah in a deed he did for Allah, let him seek his reward from other than Allah, for Allah is the most free of partners from association."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, [from the hadith of Muhammad ibn] Bakr, who is al-Burtusani, with it [[al-Musnad (4/215); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3154); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4203).]].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, Bakkar narrated to us, my father, meaning 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Bakrah, narrated to me, from Abu Bakrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever makes his deed heard, Allah will make him heard by it, and whoever shows off, Allah will show him off by it" [[al-Musnad (5/45).]].

Imam Ahmad also said: Mu'awiyah narrated to us, Shaybin narrated to us, from Firas, from 'Atiyyah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever shows off, Allah will show him off by it, and whoever makes his deed heard, Allah will make him heard by it" [[al-Musnad (3/40).]].

Another hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Shu'bah, Amr ibn Murrah told me, who said: I heard a man in the house of Abu 'Ubaydah, that he heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr narrating to Ibn 'Umar that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever makes people hear of his deed, Allah will make him heard by it; He will make him known to His creation and belittle and humiliate him." [He said] [[Addition from F, A.]]: And the eyes of 'Abd Allah overflowed [with tears] [[al-Musnad (2/162).]].

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: 'Amr ibn Yahya al-Aylī narrated to us, al-Harith ibn Ghassan narrated to us, Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The deeds of the children of Adam will be presented before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection in sealed scrolls. Allah will say: Cast this away and accept this. The angels will say: O Lord, by Allah, we have seen nothing from him but good. He will say: Indeed his deed was not for My sake, and today I accept from deeds only that which is done seeking My face."

Then al-Harith ibn Ghassan said: A group narrated from him, and he is Basri, and there is nothing wrong with him [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (3435), Kashf al-Astar.]].

Ibn Wahb said: Yazid ibn 'Iyad narrated to me, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from 'Abd Allah ibn Qays al-Khuza'i, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever stands to pray for show and reputation, will remain under Allah's aversion until he sits down." [[Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/223): "al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is Yazid ibn 'Iyad, who is matrūk (abandoned)." It has a witness from the hadith of Abu Hind al-Dari narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/270).]]

Abu Ya'la said: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Ibrahim al-Hajari, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Awf [in some manuscripts: "Urwa"] ibn Malik, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs the prayer well where people can see him, and performs it poorly where he is alone, that is an act of contempt (istihanah) with which he has treated his Lord, Mighty and Majestic." [Musnad Abi Ya'la (9/54). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar graded it hasan in al-Matalib al-'Aliyah (3/183), while al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/221): "In its chain is Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hajari, who is weak."]

Ibn Jarir said: Abu 'Amir Isma'il ibn 'Amr al-Sakuni narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Ibn 'Ayyash [in some manuscripts: "Ibn 'Abbas"] narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Qays al-Kindi narrated to us, that he heard Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan recite this verse: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾, and he said: "It is the last verse to have been revealed of the Qur'an." [Tafsir al-Tabari (16/32).]

This is a problematic report, for this verse is the last verse of Surah al-Kahf, and al-Kahf is entirely Meccan. Perhaps Mu'awiya meant that no verse came after it that abrogates it (naskh) or changes its ruling; rather it is affirmed and muhkam. The report became confused for some narrators, so they narrated it by meaning according to their own understanding. And Allah knows best.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us, Abu Qurra narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites in a night: ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾, there will be for him a light from 'Adan Ayyan to Mecca, its filling being angels." [Musnad al-Bazzar no. 3108 (Kashf al-Astar). Abu Qurra al-Asadi was regarded as unknown by al-Dhahabi and Ibn Hajar; al-Dhahabi said: "Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl alone narrated from him." Ibn Hajar said: "Ibn Khuzayma included his hadith in his Sahih and said: I do not know him to have either adjustment (adalah) or criticism (jarh)."] It is extremely strange (gharib jiddan).

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Kahf, and all praise is due to Allah.
